title: Registration complete
content:
[TRADER] Registration complete

## General TPN Search/ Track Application The user who wishes to register into eCMS for trade related activity, should first update there TPN details in RAMIS system from DRC office. Once the Trader/individual has updated their details, they can check in there TPN under the TPN Search/Track Application to check if the TPN is available in eCMS. Go to your browser: type in www.ecms.gov.bt . In the home page under the heading eCMS e-Services. Click on the TPN Search/ Track Application: ## The below screen gets populated, here in you need to key in the primary TPN: Type in the primary TPN: ## The list of TPN associated to the trader will get populated, as the TPN has been updated in RAMIS: Select the TPN which you wish to do trade and authorize the CFA with. For example: Here the user wishes to do trade with TPN DAC00061_01 for trade, so we take that TPN to do the registration or do CFA authorization. ## CFA Authorization Type in url: www.ecms.gov.bt Under the eCMS e-Services, Click on CFA Authorization/De-authorization. ## OTP Authentication Here in we add the we want to use for trade and authorize the CFA for trade related activity: ## Details: TPN: The TPN of the Registered Trader ## Mobile: mobile number to get the OTP Email id: email id to get the OTP Note: The user has to key in either mobile no or the email id for the OTP authentication. Key in the OTP received, and the validation happens, and the Registration tab appears. ## Click on the Registration Tab Select the option Apply CFA Authorization ## Fill in the details in the field: Details: CFA TPN: add in the CFA TPN to authorize the CFA for trade related activity. CFA name and CFA License Number gets auto- populated. Start Date and End Date: the date for the authorization period needs to be mentioned. ## Click on Submit button to Submit the application The Application number gets generated for tracking. Once the application has been approved by the customs, the trader and CFA will be notified through the registered mail: ## CFA De-authorization Type in url: www.ecms.gov.bt ## Under the eCMS e-Services, Click on CFA Authorization/De-authorization: OTP Authentication ## Details: TPN: The TPN of the Registered Trader ## Mobile: mobile number to get the OTP Email id: email id to get the OTP Note: The user has to key in either mobile no or the email id for the OTP authentication. Key in the OTP received, the validation happens, and the Registration tab appears. ## Click on the Registration Tab Select the option Cancel CFA Authorization \ ## Select the dropdown My Authorized CFA TPN It will list the CFA TPN authorized. Select the one you want the deauthorize. Click Submit. ## The deauthorization remark for cancellation The deauthorization or cancellation mail notification will be sent to the concern trader and CFA registered mail: ## Registration OTP based Authentication for Registration The OTP based verification will ensure that the user who is applying for registration of a TPN in eCMS is a valid and authorized user. eCMS will send an OTP to the registered mobile or email of the TPN as available in eCMS TPN Master through RAMIS/BITS integration. Once the OTP is validated in eCMS, system will consider the user as valid and allow the user to register in eCMS (Please refer to Registration SRS for the various types of Registration). For registration purpose, we will need to first go into the OTP based authentication where in you will be allowed to key in your TPN, registered email address and phone number to receive the OTP for authentication as in the process below: To get into the authentication the users are to key in the url: www.ecms.gov.bt and then Click on Registration as highlighted below: ## Figure 1.home screen Step 1: User clicks on the Registration link in the eCMS Portal. System will navigate to OTP Authentication page. ## Figure 2.OTP Authentication Screen 1 Step 2: User provides necessary details and clicks on Generate OTP. System validates and sends OTP to the user. After successful sending of OTP, system enables the OTP entry for the user. User will need to key in the OTP received from eCMS to the registered email or the phone number and click on Validate OTP. ## Figure 3.OPT Authentication Screen 2 Step 3: System will validate the OTP and, if it is found to be correct, it will allow the user to proceed with Registration. ## Figure 4.Registration List Registration for FE Users: ## To register into e-CMS: After the OTP authentication is completed, the user can then select the user they want to register into as shown in the Figure 4. The individual user can register themselves as the following: ## You can choose the option from the list for registration: Trader Registration: ## Click >>Trader Registration: The subsequent screen will be displayed: ## Party Details: Input TPN Number: The system will validate if the TPN Number is PIT – The filed to add in the CID number will be appeared and if you select BIT & CIT – the filed to add in the Trade License number will be appeared. ## TPN number if for PIT, the below screen shall be shown: Figure 6.Trader Party details Application Details: general information of an individual. ## Document Details Summary Details and Submit Summary details provides the view of certain details filled in by the user and the user need to tick the acknowledge and submit the same. Once submitted Registration number will be genetrated which shall be used to get the status: ## Click Submit >> The application is submitted, and Reg No is provided to you for tracking CFA Registration: ## Click >>CFA Registration The subsequent screen will be displayed: ## Party Details: Application Details: ## Document Details Summary Details and Submit ## This will give the preview of the details one filled for registration, as shown below: Click Submit >> The application is submitted, and Reg No is provided to you for tracking ## Bonded Warehouse Operator (BWH) Registration Click >> BWH Registration ## The subsequent screen will be displayed: Party Details: ## Application Details: Document Details ## Summary Details and Submit This will give the preview of the details one filled for registration, as shown below: ## Click Submit >> The application is submitted, and Reg No is provided to you for tracking Temporary Storage Operator (TSO) ## Click >> TSO Registration The subsequent screen will be displayed: ## Party Details: Application Details: ## Document Details Summary Details and Submit ## This will give the preview of the details one filled for registration, as shown below: Click Submit >> The application is submitted, and Reg No is provided to you for tracking Note: Approval process is done by Custom Officer, once approval is done the user will receive the mail with username and default password ## Password send to the provided registered mail id as shown below: Logging in to eCMS After the registration is completed, the individual will be provided with the login credentials username and default password, which will be asked to set while login for the first. Once completed the user can login to the portal and perform the task associated. ## To login to the e-CMS FE: Type in URL: www.ecms.gov.bt in your Internet browser to access the e-CMS. ## Click on the Login you will be taken to the page to key in your username and password: Input the username and password that was created for the individual. (Trader, CFA, BWH, TSO), upon login with default the user will be asked to provide their own password for further use. After the process is done the user will be allowed to login with the password set by them self. For that click on Click Here to login After login in the user will be seeing their individual dashboard with various menu to perform different task. ## Logout of the FE Users: This function allows the user to log out from the application any time. User can sign out from the eCMS any time by simply clicking the button available at the upper right corner of the user logged-in window. ## Log Out Page Password Reset The function allows to reset the password if the user forgets the password. Click on the Forget Password under the login tab as shown under: The next page to key in the username and registered main along with the captcha to authenticate will be provided. Once the user provided the credentials, the default password will be sent to the registered mail provide. title: Road manifest
content:
[TRADER] Road manifest

## General Introduction Road manifests are submitted by Declarants and CFAs. In road manifest amendment and cancellation can be done unless it has been used in the declaration and pass release. ## Front End User The user needs to log into eCMS using the URL: www.ecms.gov.bt ## Click on login menu and provide the required credentials to log in to the system: Create Road Manifest ## Select Road Manifest for the list of menus provided in the dashboard as highlighted below: Under the Road Manifest menu, Select Create Road Manifest: ## Key in the following details: Road Manifest Header Select the Regime as import, export, transit, temporary import, temporary export, re-import and re-export, warehousing and fill in the details >> Save the details: ## Invoice Details Add New invoice and either save or save and go to the next page: ## Supporting Documents Details The declarant shall attach any supporting documents (invoice, packing list etc) for approval: ## Summary The declarant can review his/her road manifest declaration and submit the same for approval: ## Track Application An application Number will be Generated: ## The users will be able to track their application from Search Road Manifest: Update Road Manifest and Update Road Manifest Vehicle: User can apply for update of Road manifest in general or can apply update for just vehicle mentioned in the RM due to certain reasons. ## The road manifest is not used in a declaration or The consignment against the road manifest has not exited the country. ## Cancel Road Manifest User can cancel the Road Manifest that has already submitted and approved due to certain user error: The below screen will be provided for the user to do the cancel of a particular RM by providing the reason and remarks: ## My Party Road Manifest This tab gives the user the list of RM till date submitted by the user profile:

content:
[TRADER] Passenger manifest

## General Logging In Airlines: ## The user needs to log into eCMS using the url: www.ecms.gov.bt Click on login menu and provide the required credentials to log in to the system: ## Create Passenger Manifest Select passenger manifest from the list of menus provided in the dashboard: ## Under the Passenger Manifest menu, Select Create Passenger manifest: Key in the details under each menu provided: Manifest header: here need to provide the details of the flight and no of passenger details, filling in all the required ## Passengers: add in the details of the crew/ passenger for the manifest Summary: provide the summarized details of the detailed filed in for passenger manifest ## Track Application An application Number will be Generated: ## The users will be able to track their application from search passenger manifest: Update and Cancel Passenger Manifest The created and submitted passenger manifest can be updated or cancelled by providing the valid reasons. ## Click onto Update Passenger Manifest for update of the manifest Click onto Cancel Passenger Manifest for cancellation of the manifest

title: Air Cargo manifest
content:
[TRADER] Air Cargo manifest

## General Introduction Air manifest is submitted by Declarants and CFAs. Users manually create the manifest. Users can also mark air waybills as consolidated and assign the corresponding consolidating party. ## FE user The user needs to log into eCMS using the url: www.ecms.gov.bt ## Click on login menu and provide the required credentials to log in to the system: Create Air Cargo Manifest ## Select Air Cargo Manifest for the list of menus provided in the dashboard: Under the Air Cargo Manifest menu, Select Create Air Cargo Manifest: ## Key in the following details: Manifest Header: here the applicant needs to provide the details of the flight and no of passenger details, filling in all the required: ## Air waybills: to add in the airway bills details: Supporting Documents: The declarant shall attach any supporting documents (invoice, packing list etc) for approval: Summary: The declarant can review his/her air cargo manifest declaration and submit the same for approval: ## Track Application An application Number will be Generated: ## The users will be able to track their application from Search Air Cargo Manifest: Additional Air Cargo Manifest This will allow the user to create additional air cargo manifest, if they have missed additional detailed missed in the previous manifest: ## Amend Air Cargo Manifest The manifest that has been applied for can be amended that can be done by applying the amend request for the submitted manifest. ## Click on the Amend Air Cargo Manifest Click on the button to add in the request Fill in the details in the field providing but first need to select the Manifest number that needs to be amended, select the AWB Number then add in the reason for amendment >> Save ## Cancel Air Cargo Manifest The manifest that has been applied for can be cancelled. Cancellation happens to the manifest which has been submitted. ## Click on the Cancel Air Cargo Manifest Click on button to select the manifest which 1 needs to be cancelled. Select the manifest number under the tab Manifest Number, then the Manifest Cancellation Type. Here we have two and base on the selected the AWB Number mandatory filed gets highlighted. Fill in the required details and Submit. Air Manifest Cancellation number gets generated. Double click on the number and then press Submit button. Dialogue box with the application number gets generated. Once the cancellation is being approved by the concern officer, the status of the application can be viewed from the Search Air Cargo Manifest. ## Air Cargo House Manifest eCMS will enable the user to select a consolidated air waybill that assigned to the user’s party and use it to create a house manifest. House manifests can be created through manual input/upload. eCMS will also enable a customs officer to approve the submission. ## Create Air Cargo House Manifest While creating the Air Cargo Manifest, under the Bill of Lading Tab, if the user has selected the BL Type as Consolidated, then once the Air Cargo Manifest has been approved the declaration will then be available in the Create Air Cargo House Manifest, after that the user can create the Air cargo house manifest and submit the same by providing the details under each header. ## Amend and Cancel Air Cargo House Manifest The Air Cargo House Manifest once submitted can also be amended and cancelled. ## View Air Cargo Manifest Audit Details Gives the details of the actions considered into the Air Cargo Manifest.

title: TARIFF
content:
[GENERAL] TARIFF

## General Release No 1.0 – May 2021 ## Endorsement by System Owner (internal) release history ## Table of Contents Table of Contents 3 ## Introduction 4 A. Definitions and Abbreviations 4 ## B. References 6 1. Functional Requirements 7 1.1 Tariff System Overview 7 1.1.1 Entity Hierarchy in Tariff system 7 1.2 HS Code Maintenance 9 1.2.1 Description 9 1.2.2 Design Considerations 9 1.3 Tax Types 11 1.3.1 Description 11 1.3.2 Ad Valorem 11 1.3.3 Specific Rate 12 1.3.4 Derive Cost 12 1.3.5 Additional Tax (Derive Tax) 12 1.4 HS Code Configurations 13 1.4.1 Description 13 1.4.2 Commercial Name 13 1.4.3 Unit of Measurement (UOM) 14 1.4.4 HS Code Tariff configuration 14 1.4.5 Prohibited 14 1.4.6 Restricted Goods 14 1.5 Customs Procedure Code (CPC) Maintenance 14 1.5.1 Description 14 ## Use case diagram for CPC 15 1.6 Agreements/Preferential Tariffs 15 1.6.1 Description 15 ## Use case diagram for Preferential Tariff 16 1.7 Duties and Taxes Computation Process 16 1.7.1 Description 16 1.7.2 Computation Process 17 1.8 Advance Rulings 21 1.8.1 Description 21 1.8.2 Process flow for application of Advance Rulings 21 1.8.3 Process flow for Revoking Advance Rulings 22 1.8.4 Use Cases of Advance Rulings 24 ## Appendix A 25 1. Configuration blueprint (CBP) 25 ## Introduction This document defines & illustrates the business requirements, process flows as well as the detailed functional requirements of eCMS Tariff module to be implemented for Department of Revenue and Customs, Bhutan. With Tariff Management, harmonized codes for almost every type of goods are identified, defined, and classified. Tariff rates that are to be imposed for the calculation of duties and tax fees are configured. Preferential tariff based on regional trade blocs or FTA can also be configured and used in the computation. This module also maintains which governmental authority is responsible for the classification and monitoring of every type of goods. ## Definitions and Abbreviations The table below lists the different acronyms and abbreviations as well as the definitions used throughout this SRS. ## References The creation of the BECMS SRS was referenced using the following documents: ## FUNCATIONAL REQUIREMENT SPECIFICATION.docx TECHNICAL REQUIREMENT SPECIFICATION.docx ## Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-3.pdf Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-4.pdf ## Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-5A.pdf Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-5B.pdf ## Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-6A.pdf Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-6B.pdf ## Functional Requirements Tariff System Overview With Tariff Management, harmonized codes for every type of goods are identified, defined and classified. Tariff rates that are to be imposed for the calculation of duties and tax fees are also determined. This module also maintains the preferential tariff for regional trade blocs and FTAs. The Customs Procedure Code (CPC) is also maintained and configured here. Certain CPC’s has duties and taxes suspended; this is configured in this module. Tariff module is involved in all Regime flows. Refer to the regimes flows in the declaration processing SRS. Tariff module codes like Chapter/Heading/Subheading/HS codes are used in Declaration, OGA, Valuation and System Admin modules. ## Entity Hierarchy in Tariff system CPC Group/Regime level will have the highest level which controls the sub processes like custom procedure codes (CPC). One CPC group can have many CPC and CPC can have its own tax configurations. Tax types are configured at HS code level where system provides the option to configure new rate at HS code level or derive the rate from tax type directly. ## Process Flow for Tariff Code Maintenance (Generic) HS Code Maintenance ## Description The HS Code format followed in eCMS is as per recommended by WCO. It comprises of 8-10 digits. The 8-chars are for chapter, heading, sub-heading & HS Code. The last 2-digits are for country specific classification. The Chapter Code is the initial part of the HS Code to classify goods. This is a 2-numbered code that specifies a broader classification. For example, the Chapter Code ‘10’ is used to represent all metallic objects. Heading Code is a 4-numbered code where the first two digits refer to the Chapter, and the last two digits as the Heading position in a HS code. These represent additional classification. For example: ## Chapter 10 – All Metals Heading 1001 – Gold Metal Sub heading code is the 6 digits comprising of the chapter, heading and a further sub-division of the heading by 2 digits. HS Code is an 8-digit international nomenclature system. ## Example: To represent a 24-carat gold, the HS code can be 10010001, where: 10 is the Chapter Code to represent all metals. 1001 is the Heading Code to represent a specific metal (here Gold) 10010001 is the HS Code to represent a 24-carat gold to be measured in KGM (Kilogram) Section will be created and linked to the chapters. There are around 18 sections defined in the system. Every chapter will be linked to section available in the system for the view purpose. However, this will not be used as part of HS Code. HS code will be considered from chapter onwards in declaration and tax configuration. ## Design Considerations Use Case Diagram for HS Code maintenance ## Tax Types Description Tax Types define a complete list of all tax types applicable in the country, such as Customs Duties, Consumption Tax, Luxury Tax, Goods and Services Tax (GST), Green Tax (GRT), Surcharges & any other charges. It forms the line item in the duties and taxes computation. The following are the configurable fields defined at the tax type level: ## Ad Valorem The ad valorem tariff type has the below configurations: ## Specific Rate The specific rate tariff type has the below configurations. If the HS Code has UOM for e.g., milk can have UOM as Liter then the specific rate can be defined as UOM. ## Derive Cost The customs value (defined as cost here) is based on CIF or FOB etc. as described above in ad valorem section. In addition to this, eCMS provides for flexibility where the user can define different tariff rates at each of the component of the INCOTERM. For e.g., instead of a flat rate of 5% on CIF (as customs value), the user may choose to define 5% on Cost, 4% on Insurance and 2% on Freight. This will give customs the flexibility to rationalize & accurately apply duty for products whose value is less, but freight may be higher. ## Additional Tax (Derive Tax) In addition to the 3 methods illustrated above (i.e., ad valorem and specific), eCMS provides a flexibility where the user can combine different tax types to derive a tax. For e.g., if GST has additional tax on the Customs Duty Rate (CDR) and Green Tax Rate (GTR), system will take the computed value of CRD and GTR and apply configured 10% of GST tax on the computed Customs Duty Rate (CDR) and computed Green Tax Rate (GTR). ## Use Case Diagram for Tax Type maintenance HS Code Configurations ## Description Each HS Code has tariff & tariff related configurations in order to calculate the duty of that particular item declared in declarations. The computation done at the HS Code level will be part of the item level taxes. ## The tariff configuration for the HS Code comprises of the following types of tariff: Ad-valorem Rate - Rate is defined in percentage of the items value (e.g., 5% of the item value) Specific rate - Rate is defined in the specific quantity of the items (e.g., 5 Dollars per 10 KGM). The UOM used for the specific rate should be same as the default UOM configured for the HS code. System does not handle the conversion between different UOMs. ## Commercial Name Each HS code should be configured with commercial names. This will help in understanding of the description of the HS code and commercial usage. One HS code can have multiple commercial names. ## Unit of Measurement (UOM) Each HS Code can have 1 Unit of Measurement (UOM) assigned to it. During declaration submission only this configured UOM can be used. This UOM can be used in the specific rate configuration for the HS code. ## HS Code Tariff configuration Each HS code can have more than 1 tax types assigned to it. These configured taxes will be read by system and duty computation will be performed during declaration submission. ## Prohibited Each HS code can be updated as prohibited in HS code maintenance. Once the HS code is prohibited, system will alert the user if the declaration the selected HS code is prohibited and cannot be used in Declaration module during submission of declaration. ## Restricted Goods Each HS code can be updated as restricted in HS code maintenance. During declaration submission, system will show the validation message to the user to upload the permit copy of the agency as attachment in supporting document section. We will configure a separate document type to be uploaded when the restricted goods are included as part of declared item i.e. HS Code ## Customs Procedure Code (CPC) Maintenance Description A Customs Procedure Code (CPC) is used to identify the nature of the transaction being affected and indicates the details of the movement of the goods. CPC is composed of five digits where the first digit identifies the regime; the second digit identifies the previous regime (if applicable); and the rest are given by the officer. ## Example Import for home use - 40001 ## Import from warehouse for home use – 40701 40 is import regime 70 is warehouse regime In addition to defining the nature of processing CPC, eCMS defines validation rules at CPC level which has impact on computation of duties and taxes. Below are the tariff related configurations: ## Use case diagram for CPC Agreements/Preferential Tariffs ## Description This is applicable when there are preferential agreements on the tariff that are based on common agreements or on any national preferential agreements or Trade blocs (e.g. SARC etc. The preferential tariff is defined using the country groups or country list. The preferential tariff may be configured and associated with CPC. The configurations related to preferential tariff are as below: Note: Bhutan is having bi-lateral agreement with Bangladesh. In this case, system will show only the preferential CPC in declaration if the added HS code is in preferential tariff list and country of origin is Bangladesh. We should be able to configure preferential tariff once the agreement is finalized, like Thailand and Nepal. ## Use case diagram for Preferential Tariff Duties and Taxes Computation Process ## Description Duty computation in eCMS takes in account 4 major inputs i.e., HS Code, Tax Types, CPC & Preferential Tariff configurations. Based on these 4 key inputs the duties and taxes are derived at item level and declaration header level. ## Computation Process The process for Duties and Tax computation is shown below. The amount is computed for all items in the declaration in the same manner, and all tax line items are aggregated for final computation. ## Rebate & Exemption There will be an option to create CPC with Rebate and Exemption where we can configure the tax which is rebated or exempted. System will pick up this configuration during declaration submission and applies the rebate or exemption taxes accordingly. User should be selecting the appropriate rebate or exemption CPC while submitting either rebate or exemption declarations. ## Example Exemption CPC has to be selected to apply on right tax rate ## GST alone EET alone ## GST & EET Preferential CPC There will be an option to create CPC for preferential tariff. System will fetch these preferential CPC in declaration submission based on provided HS code and country of origin. ## Use Case Diagram for Duties and Taxes Calculation Advance Rulings ## Description Any registered user must be able to apply for advanced rulings, which will incur an application fee. Customs must be able to issue notifications of advanced rulings, which must be sent to the applicant and then published on the Customs website. Customs must also be able to issue Demand Notices for application fees, which must be automatically sent to the revenue system for processing. ## Process flow for application of Advance Rulings Note: System will insert the commercial names for HS code once the advance ruling is approved. P02: System Validation System will validate for any data issue, duplication etc. P03: Create or Update in eCMS The codes will be created or updated in eCMS system. [TABLE] S/N | Validation Rules 2 | Each HS Code can have 1 Unit of Measurement (UOM) assigned to it. During declaration submission only these configured UOM can be used. 3 | The system should have the capability to extend the HS code to 10 digits. 10 digits of HS Code consists of Chapter Code (2 digits), Heading Code (2 digits), Sub Heading Code (2 digits) and HS Code 4 Code (4 digits). [TABLE] Field | Description Tax Type Code/Name | Unique identified for the tax type Validity Period | Defines the period when the tax type is valid Item/Header Level Indicator | To indicate if the Tax Type is at the Item level or Header level Fixed Tax Indicator | This is to indicate if this is a fixed tax (or fees) for a particular CPC/CPC Group. For example, if there is a fixed Transit processing fee, then it will be indicated as “Fixed”. If it is not fixed, then it will be based on the tariff HS Code selected Tax Rate | Ad valorem – a percentage of the value Specific – based on a specific unit of measurement for e.g., $5 per box of an item. Derived – Based on the customized rate for specific INCOTERMS for e.g., 2% of Cost. Or 2% of cost and 1% of insurance. Tax Rate Validity Period | Defines the period when the tax rate is valid CPC Group | To specify if the tax type is applicable only to certain CPC groups / regime. [TABLE] Rate Types | Description | Additional Configurations Cost Base | The cost base used to compute the base value for which the Ad valorem is applied | FOB or CIF or FOB + Any combination of Freight, Insurance and Other Costs Derive Cost Base From | The cost base is derived from any of the following. | Derive rate from Tax Type – The ad valorem rate is taken from the tax type and not HS Code level Derive cost from Tax Type – The cost base is taken from the tax type and not HS code level. Has Additional Taxes – This indicates if there are additional taxes i.e. GST. Derive cost from HS Code – The cost base is taken from the HS Code. The one in Tax Type will be ignored. [TABLE] Rate Types | Description | Remarks Rate Amount | The amount per UOM | For e.g., $10 per -litre Rate Currency | The currency for the rate amount Rate Unit | The unit’s name | In above case unit name is “-litre” UOM ID | The Unit of Measure | In above case it is the litre [TABLE] S/N | Configurations 1 | Through the CPC, the system should be able to suppress any tax types, while it maintains the others, so the suppression is at Tax Type level. For e.g., for Transit, the duties should be suppressed (Not Applicable) and only a Transit Fee should be charged. 2 | Tax Types applicable to certain CPC only, for e.g., Declaration Processing Fee is applicable to all Import related to CPC Groups. This may be configured at the tax type level. 4 | Precedent entry CPC (Previous CPC) [TABLE] S/N | Fields | Preferential Configurations 1 | HS Code/ Subheading/ Heading/ Chapter | Preferential tariff rate may be applied to specific HS Code or at the sub-heading, chapter or heading level. 2 | Rate Type | Can be ad valorem or specific. 3 | CPC | Preferential tariff may be applied to specific CPC only. For e.g. all imports by diplomats for a certain county are entitled for preferential tariff on certain goods. 4 | Tax Type | The tax type on which the preferential rate is to be applied. [TABLE] Process Steps P01: Tariff Table Retrieve the HS Codes for each item and the applicable tax types and tariff rates. The duty is computed based on the defined tariff rate. P02: Tax Types The order of computation is retrieved from Tax types of table. Note: GST has to apply on top of the CDR, hence it has to be configured after the CDR tax order. P03: Compute Taxes If any of the amounts (FOB, freight, insurance, etc.) are in foreign currency, it is converted to the local currency first before the duty computation starts. The duties and taxes are always expressed in local currency. Store the computed amount in the DB for reporting purposes. P04: CPC Codes Retrieve the CPC Codes at the declaration item level and all the CPC attributes. Apply CPC level tax not applicable indicators, if any. P05: Agreements Declarant chooses the preferential tariff CPC for the item in the declaration. Retrieve the tax rates from the preferential tariff table, and then compute the preferential tariff from the taxes computed above. P06: Compute Duties and Taxes Compute the duty and tax with exemption for all the items in the declaration and aggregate. [TABLE] Process Steps P01: Submit application User must be able to apply for an advance ruling by completing an online application form. User can attach the supporting documents such as brochures, photographs of samples etc. P02: Verify Documents The verifier at customs head officer can verify the documents and recommend for approval or reject the application. P03: Notify applicant on rejection If the application is rejected, then system will notify the applicant by email notification with reason for rejection. P04: Verify & Approve The Assessor at customs head office will verify the application where he/she can either approve or reject the application. Mail notification with reason of rejection will be triggered in case of rejection by Assessor. Once approved, advance ruling has a validity period of 2 years. A notification will be issued to applicant. Customs Officer has to publish the new advance ruling on customs website (i.e. Notice and update). BTC code in tariff module must be updated with advance ruling details i.e. commercial name. P05: Calculate the application Fees If the application is approved, system will calculate the application fees based on below factor. A base fee of Ngultrum 500 to a maximum of 10 commodities. Additional fee of Ngultrum 100 per commodity that exceeds the maximum limit of 10 commodities. P06: Send confirmation A confirmation mail notification will be shared to applicant upon approval of the advance ruling. P07: Send to Revenue system The payment information shared to revenue system. The revenue system will return the details of receipt to the eCMS once payment has been made. [TABLE] Process Steps P01: Revoke by Customs Customs officer should have an option to search and revoke the approved advance ruling. Officer opens the advance ruling and update the status to be revoked. P02: Update status to Revoked The eCMS system status will get be updated the advance ruling as revoked. Customs Officer has to publish the revocation in customs website (i.e. Notice and update).

## General Introduction The Custom Official has the right to approve the application that has been submitted by the Front-end user. Click on the Road Manifest in dashboard. ## Search Road Manifest Provides the list of Road Manifest that has been applied till date. ## Approve Submitted Request Click on “Approve Submission Request”. List of application pending shall be shown, then the focal person will be able to act by double clicking on the application or by right-clicking on the on the right and Select Edit ## Status of the application submitted is taken place by selecting the status as: Approve: the application is approved for further process Reject: the application is rejected, and remark is provided for the rejection. Reject for amendment: the application gets rejected for amendment and the applicant can amend the application and resubmit the same application. ## Approve Cancel Request Click on “Approve Cancel Request”. List of application pending shall be shown, then the focal person will be able to act by double clicking on the application or by right-clicking on the on the right and Select Edit ## Status of the application submitted is taken place by selecting the status as: Road Manifest Cancel Approved: the application is approved for further process. title: Valuation
content:
[CUSTOMS] Valuation

## General Introduction Customs Valuation is one of the sub-systems in the CMS component of the eCMS system. In this sub-system, Customs valuation unit creates and uses the historical transaction data as reference for valuation of all commodities in the declaration. Specific profile-based valuation range may also be defined when valuation officers are sure on the valuation of certain commodities meeting certain criteria. Profile based valuations are used to target specific cases of valuation frauds and “as such” will be used less frequently than transaction based. This valuation sub-system also captures the value based on last transactions made during the period for all the HS Codes. For transaction method, the system builds the valuation database. Profile based or transaction-based valuation can be selected based on the HS Code. Once eCMS receives the declaration, the declaration value is verified with the valuation database or the profile if configured. The valuation assessment will indicate if the goods are “under value” or “overvalued” or cleared. The valuation assessing officer may update his inputs on the valuation. Valuation process is involved in Import, Transit, Warehouse, Temporary Import, Re-Import Regime flows. ## Logging in as Valuation Officer The user needs to log into eCMS using the url: www.ecms.gov.bt ## Click on login menu and provide the required credentials to log in to the system: Valuation Click on the menu Valuation. ## Create Global Criteria The Global Valuation criteria refers to the default criteria for all the Items and is considered when there are no available Specific Valuation criteria for the H.S Code of that corresponding item. This functionality allows Customs control to establish the verification criteria based on the historical valuation records available in eCMS system and the past transaction details captured in the eCMS system. The configuration set for the criteria is used to check the value declared by the Declarant for an Item in the declaration that falls in the Customs criteria value or not. ## Click on Create Global Criteria Click on to add the Global Criteria Details Select the valuation Type from drop down list >> Number of days/transactions>>provide the Percentile Lower >> percentile Upper>> Select Status (Active/Non Active)>> Save The Global Criteria gets create and can be viewed in the list. ## HS Code Criteria Click on HS Code Criteria ## Click on to add the HS Code Criteria Select the BTC Code from drop down list >> Select the Valuation Type>>Provide the number of Days/Transactions >> Provide Percentile Lower>> Provide Percentile Upper Select Status (Active/Non Active)>> Save The HS Code Criteria gets create and can be viewed in the list. ## Valuation Profile The profile-based configuration for valuation criteria is a process of setting the specific profile with valuation boundaries i.e. upper and lower limits with variance at HS Code level. \ ## Click on Valuation Profile Click on to add the Valuation Profile Provide the Profile details and Associated Criteria >> Save the same. The list gets create and can be viewed in the list. ## Minimum Price List Click on Minimum Price List ## Click on to add the Minimum Price List Select the BTC Code from drop down list >> Select the UOM>>Provide Declaration>> Provide Minimum Value Price>> Select Status (Active/Non-Active)>> Save The list gets create and can be viewed in the list. ## Search Valuation List Go to Valuation menu and click on “Search Valuation List”. List of declaration that has gone through valuation or pending for valuation gets populated. ## Pending Valuation List Go to Valuation menu and click on “Pending Valuation List”. List of declaration that pending Valuation will be populated. Select the declaration for valuation >> provide the results for valuation then update the status >> Submit the declaration.

title: Offence
content:
[CUSTOMS] Offence

## General Introduction Offence module in Electronic Customs Management System (eCMS) allows Policy Sections to manage the complete lifecycle of an offence under Customs Rules and Regulations of Bhutan Revised Edition 2023. This module also enables Intelligence Agencies to report the offences. This module includes management of Offence Reports, processing of offence reports, Offence Case Files, managing inquiries, orders, notices etc. This user manual provides a detailed guide for Officers to work with this module. ## Create Offence: - eCMS enables an offence officer to complete offence reports that have been created by a declaration goods inspection failure reported by a customs officer. eCMS also allows an offence officer to create ad-hoc offence reports due to risk/intelligence failure. An offence can involve personnel or declaration goods. The offence report will also contain the demand note to pay and the action applied on the goods involved. ## Offence routed through Inspection Logging in as Custom Officer ## The user needs to log into eCMS using the url: www.ecms.gov.bt Click on login menu and provide the required credentials to log in to the system: ## Do the approval process of declaration Approves / Rejects for Amendment/ Reject the declaration. ## In case of the different status: Rejects for amendment the declaration is send back to the concern declarant with the remarks for rejection: Reject: the declaration submitted is being rejected with remarks for rejection. ## Approved: the declaration submitted has been approved and then moves for payment Once approved payment needs to be proceeded with the generation of the receipt and share the same to the respective declarant via SMS and mail for payment. ## Payment To do the same following are the steps: ## Click >> Payment CMS Select -> Pending Voucher -> Select the declaration for payment -> provide the details under each tab -> Payment number gets generated. Select -> Pending Payment -> provide the required details and submit. ## Valuation of the declaration The declaration moves to valuation tab, where in the concern officer will provide the details as per his/her finding from the valuation. ## Under valuation the list of items can be valuated, and the following are the finding: All the items are evaluated individually, and data is also updated individually, for that: Click >> Valuation Tab >> Select Pending Valuation List (list of declaration that needs to be valuated will be populated for the valuation) ## Once selected the valuation details has the tab: Declaration Details: provided the details for declaration and declaration date: Valuation Result: Here in the list of items from the declaration that needs to be evaluated. Select -> Item from the list of items from the declaration. ## The details pop up that needs to be filled in with the valuation data: Here in Custom Value needs to be added in as per the valuation. Once the value is added the Result Tab, selected the details and update the same. ## After the valuation is done and any of the item is found to be as follows: Inside Define Range – The item gets cleared. Under Value - then it will go further for Risk assessment. ## Centralized Risk Click >> Centralized Risk ## Select -> Pending Risk Assessment Under Pending Risk Assessment ## Fill in the details for the Risk Assessment as per the details required and update the declaration Inspection Click >> Inspection. Select >> Create Physical Examination. ## Fill in all the details: Header: ## Containerized Cargo Non-Containerized Cargo ## Valuation Details Support Documents: attach the document required. Examination: here under the Physical Examination Status = Physical Examination failed (Amendment/Offence) ## Print out of the Physical Examination Report Offence Management Module ## Create Offence Select -> Create Offence ## Select the declaration which has been routed through inspection for offence and click on Create Offence is being created: ## Search Offence Report Gives the list of declaration under offence. Shows the list of offence that has been committed. Select the Offence that has been committed. Add in details on the offence as per the finding and Click on Update button. ## Assuming Offence here in each item level: Item 1 (Origin) – here the item has issue with origin so that has been recorded and provided with outcome as Detention and now will be shared to the Custom Warehouse. Item 2 (Valuation) – if the item has valuation offence, the item will be detained and send to Custom Warehouse Item 3 (Cleared) : if the item has no issue , it clear and the outcome of the item is updated as Released Under Summary tab – provides the summary of the offence that has been created. To check for the status offence, get the details from the list by providing the offence number as below: The Item that has been detained will now be added to the Custom Warehouse via concern authority. ## Custom Warehouse procedure for detained goods Click >> Customs Warehouse Select -> Admit Goods List of declaration with item gets populated and the item under each is being admitted to the warehouse. ## Seize process for detained goods The Offence gets reopened to check for the outcome by the concern officer, the status now will be changed from Detention to Seize. ## Click >> Offence Management System Select -> Search Offence Report ## Select the Offence that need to be worked onto Under the item change the Offence Outcome Requested as: Seize. The concern officer will now take the declaration and check for the status, here the status that will be shown is Declaration Amendment as shown below: ## Got to Declaration CMS >> Select Amendment by Customs Do the changes into the item where in the office was committed, in our case we have item1 having origin and item2 having under value. Here under the declaration the amendment is made by the concern official. ## General information no change Bill of landing Invoice and Consignor – as there was offence under item, update needs to be made on the item level. Amendment completed. The Status of the declaration will now be pending payment there was valuation mismatch. Next Go to Payment CMS, make the additional payment and submit. ## Release The concern official will now check the offence and status now will be Released. Status changed to Release the Official in charge of the Custom Warehouse, will release the goods accordingly. Once all release the offence status will be Closed.

## General Release No 0.4 – June 2021 ## Endorsement by System Owner (internal) release history ## Table of Contents Table of Contents 3 ## Introduction 4 A. Definitions and Abbreviations 4 ## B. References 6 1. Functional Requirements 7 1.1 Air Manifests 7 1.2 Road Manifests 40 1.2.1 Overview 40 1.2.2 Manifest Structure 40 1.2.3 Road Manifest Submission 40 1.2.4 Road Manifest Update 45 1.2.5 Road Manifest Cancellation 49 1.2.6 Gate-In Vehicle 52 1.2.7 Cancel Gate-In 54 1.3 Passenger Manifests 57 1.3.1 Overview 57 1.3.2 Manifest Structure 57 1.3.3 Passenger Manifest Submission 57 1.3.4 Update Passenger Manifest 61 1.3.5 Passenger Manifest Cancellation 65 1.4 Dispatch Challan 69 1.4.1 Overview 69 1.4.2 Assumptions and Restrictions 69 1.4.3 Dispatch Challan Notification 69 1.4.4 Dispatch Challan Process 70 1.4.5 Dispatch Challan Amendment 73 1.4.6 Gate-In Challan 77 1.5 Temporary Storage 80 1.5.1 Overview 80 1.5.2 Admit Goods into Temporary Storage 80 1.5.3 Release Goods from Temporary Storage 82 ## Appendix A 85 1. Configuration blueprint (CBP) 85 2. Air Manifest Upload files 85 3. Passenger manifest Integration file template 85 4. Manifest Printouts 85 5. Temporary Storage Tracking Details 86 6. Dispatch Challan Printout 86 7. Scheduler Jobs 86 8. User Interface 86 ## Introduction This document defines & illustrates the business requirements, process flows as well as the detailed functional requirements of eCMS Manifest module to be implemented for Department of Revenue and Customs Bhutan. ## Definitions and Abbreviations The table below lists the different acronyms and abbreviations as well as the definitions used throughout this SRS. ## References The creation of the eCMS SRS was referenced using the following documents: ## FUNCATIONAL REQUIREMENT SPECIFICATION.docx TECHNICAL REQUIREMENT SPECIFICATION.docx ## Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-3.pdf Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-4.pdf ## Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-5A.pdf Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-5B.pdf ## Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-6A.pdf Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-6B.pdf ## 1. Functional Requirements Air Manifests ## Overview Process ID: 03.01– Air manifest Air manifest is submitted by Declarants and CFAs. Users manually create the manifest. Users can also mark air waybills as consolidated and assign the corresponding consolidating party. ## Manifest Structure The air manifest document is logically structured as shown in the below diagram: ## AIR MANIFEST STRUCTURE The master manifest follows the IATA format. The master manifest comprises the CIMP FFM, the relationship to AWB (waybill) is 1-to-Many. The FFM indicates if the waybill is a master waybill or is consolidated (AHL). The containers in the AWB/AHL are not captured in the manifest. ## Business Rules & User Group Access For the business rules & user group access refer CBP document for Air manifests. ## Shipment Type in Air Waybill Following are the shipment types supported in the AWB processing. Samples are given below: ## Shipment ype ## Air Manifest Submission eCMS will enable the user to submit air master manifests through manual input/upload. eCMS will also enable a customs officer to approve the submission. ## Pre-Requisites Users for submitting an Air Manifest should be a registered Declarant (or CFA) in eCMS. Customs officers for approving an Air Manifest should be a registered Customs officer in eCMS. Both Declarants and Custom officers are authorized to access eCMS and have access to the required application. Declarants who will be submitting consolidated AWBs already know which consolidator party assigned to the same AWB. User groups allowed to become consolidators of a master AWB have been configured. ## Process Flow Process ID: 03.01.01– Air manifest submission ## Use Case Diagram Note/s: A manifest in Draft status can be updated/deleted/submitted by any user of the same party that created the manifest or by a CFA. The list of consolidators can be configured as part of the registration process. ## Business Validation Additional Air Manifest eCMS will enable the user to add air waybills to an approved air master manifest through manual input/upload. eCMS will also enable a customs officer to approve the request. ## Pre-Requisites Users for submitting an Additional Air Manifest should be a registered Declarant (or CFA) in eCMS. Customs officers for approving an Additional Air Manifest should be a registered Customs officer in eCMS. Both Declarants and Custom officers are authorized to access eCMS and have access to the required application. Declarants who will be submitting consolidated AWBs already know which consolidator party assigned to the same AWB. User groups allowed to become consolidators of a master AWB have been configured. ## Process Flow Process ID: 03.01.02 – Additional Air manifest ## Use Case Diagram Note/s: A draft request can be updated/deleted/submitted by any user of the same party or by a CFA. The list of consolidators can be configured as part of the registration process. ## Business Validation Air Manifest Amendment eCMS will enable the user to amend an air waybill in an approved air master manifest through manual input. eCMS will also enable a customs officer to approve the request. ## Pre-Requisites Users for submitting an Air Manifest Amendment should be a registered Declarant (or CFA) in eCMS. Customs officers for approving an Air Manifest Amendment should be a registered Customs officer in eCMS. Both Declarants and Custom officers are authorized to access eCMS and have access to the required application. Declarants who will be submitting consolidated AWBs already know which consolidator party assigned to the same AWB. User groups allowed to become consolidators of a master AWB have been configured. ## The air manifest should have already been approved by customs Process Flow ## Process ID: 03.01.03 – Air Manifest Amendment Use Case Diagram ## Note/s: A request in Draft status can be updated/deleted/submitted by any user of the same party that created the manifest or by a CFA. ## Business Validation Air Manifest Cancellation eCMS will enable the user to cancel a manifest or one of its air waybills through manual input. eCMS will also enable a customs officer to approve the cancellation. ## Pre-Requisites Users for submitting an Air Manifest cancellation should be a registered Declarant (or CFA) in eCMS. Customs officers for approving an Air Manifest cancellation should be a registered Customs officer in eCMS. Both Declarants and Custom officers are authorized to access eCMS and have access to the required application. ## The Air manifest submitted for cancellation has to be approved Air Manifest by customs Declarants who will be submitting consolidated AWBs already know which consolidator party assigned to the same AWB. ## User groups allowed to become consolidators of a master AWB have been configured Process Flow ## Process ID: 03.01.04 – Air Manifest Cancellation Use Case Diagram ## Note/s: A request in Draft status can be updated/deleted/submitted by any user of the same party that created the manifest or by a CFA. ## Business Validation Note/s: Please refer to Auto-Cancel AWB in Scheduler Jobs Section under Appendix for details regarding the batch job that auto-cancels AWB. ## Air House Manifest Submission eCMS will enable the user to select a consolidated air waybill that assigned to the user’s party and use it to create a house manifest. House manifests can be created through manual input/upload. eCMS will also enable a customs officer to approve the submission. ## Pre-Requisites Users for submitting an Air House Manifest should be a registered Declarant (or CFA) in eCMS. Customs officers for approving an Air House Manifest should be a registered Customs officer in eCMS. Both Declarants and Custom officers are authorized to access eCMS and have access to the required application. ## The House manifest submitted for cancellation has to be approved Air Manifest by customs Process Flow ## Process ID: 03.01.05 – Air House Manifest Submission Use Case Diagram ## Notes: A house manifest in Draft status can be updated/deleted/submitted by any user of the same consolidator party. ## Business Validation Air House Manifest Amendment eCMS will enable the user to amend an air waybill in an approved air house master manifest through manual input. eCMS will also enable a customs officer to approve the request. ## Pre-Requisites Users for submitting an Air House Manifest Amendment should be a registered Declarant (or CFA) in eCMS and is the consolidator of the air house manifest. Customs officers for approving an Air House Manifest Amendment should be a registered Customs officer in eCMS. Both consolidator and Custom officers are authorized to access eCMS and have access to the required application. ## The house manifest submitted for amendment should be an approved house manifest by customs Process Flow ## Process ID: 03.01.06 – Air House Manifest Amendment Use Case Diagram ## Note/s: A request in Draft status can be updated/deleted/submitted by any user of the same party that created the manifest or by a CFA. ## Business Validation Air House Manifest Cancellation eCMS will enable the user to cancel a house manifest or one of its air waybills through manual input. eCMS will also enable a customs officer to approve the cancellation. ## Pre-Requisites Users for submitting an Air House Manifest cancellation should be a registered Declarant (or CFA) in eCMS. Customs officers for approving an Air House Manifest cancellation should be a registered Customs officer in eCMS. Both Declarants and Custom officers are authorized to access eCMS and have access to the required application. ## Process Flow Process ID: 03.01.07 – Air House Manifest Cancellation ## Use Case Diagram Business Validation ## Road Manifests Overview ## Process ID: 03.02 – Road Manifest Road manifest is submitted by Declarants and CFAs. In road cargo, amendment can be done as well as cancellation. ## Manifest Structure The road manifest document is logically structured as shown in the below diagram: ## ROAD MANIFEST STRUCTURE The road manifest comprises a header and 1 or more invoices. The invoice is equivalent to the air waybill in the air manifest. The road manifest supports four types of cargo including 1) Containers 2) Bulk 3) Vehicles 4) and General Cargo Only one type of cargo can be selected for an invoice. Separate invoices need to be created for manifests containing different types of cargo. ## Road Manifest Submission eCMS will enable the user to submit road manifests through manual input. eCMS will also enable a customs officer to approve the submission. ## Pre-Requisites Users for submitting a Road Manifest should be a registered Declarant (or CFA) in eCMS. Customs officers for approving a Road Manifest should be a registered Customs officer in eCMS. Both Declarants and Custom officers are authorized to access eCMS and have access to the required application. ## Process Flow Process ID: 03.02.01– Road Manifest Submission ## Use Case Diagram Note/s: A draft road manifest can be updated/deleted/submitted by any user of the same party or by a CFA. An invoice can be distributed into multiple manifests in case the invoice needs more than one vehicle for transport. One Road manifest can be linked to one declaration as a default. Multiple Road manifests can be linked to one declaration if they have the same importers. ## Business Validation Update Road Manifest eCMS will enable the user to update an approved road manifest through manual input. eCMS will enable the user to amend the following the road manifest ## Add invoices Delete Invoices ## Amend vehicle details Amend driver’s details Accordingly, eCMS will also enable a customs officer to approve the request. ## Pre-Requisites Users for submitting a Road Manifest Amendment should be a registered Declarant (or CFA) in eCMS. Customs officers for approving a Road Manifest Amendment should be a registered Customs officer in eCMS. Both Declarants and Custom officers are authorized to access eCMS and have access to the required application. ## The request for amendment, the road manifest should have been approved by customs Process Flow ## Process ID: 03.02.02 – Update Road Manifest Use Case Diagram ## Note/s: A request in Draft status can be updated/deleted/submitted by any user of the same party that created the manifest or by a CFA. ## Business Validation Road Manifest Cancellation eCMS will enable the user to cancel an approved road manifest. eCMS will also enable a customs officer to approve the cancellation. ## Pre-Requisites Users for submitting a Road Manifest cancellation should be a registered Declarant (or CFA) in eCMS. Customs officers for approving a Rpad Manifest cancellation should be a registered Customs officer in eCMS. Both Declarants and Custom officers are authorized to access eCMS and have access to the required application. the road manifest submitted for cancellation has to be an approved road manifest. ## Process Flow Process ID: 03.02.03 – Road Manifest Cancellation ## Use Case Diagram Note/s: Please refer to Auto-Cancel Invoice in Scheduler Jobs Section under Appendix for details regarding the batch job that auto-cancels invoices. ## Business Validation Gate-In Vehicle eCMS will enable the customs officer to gate-in a vehicle along with selected vehicle registration number and manifest/s. This is to allow the customs officer to indicate which vehicle and the manifests that are included in the vehicle that is about to cross the border. ## Pre-Requisites Customs officers for updating a vehicle for gate-in should be a registered Customs officer in eCMS. Custom officers are authorized to access eCMS and have access to the required application. ## Process Flow Process ID: 03.02.04 – Gate-in Vehicle ## Use Case Diagram Business Validation ## Cancel Gate-In eCMS will enable the customs officer to remove manifests that had been incorrectly included in a vehicle gate-in. This is since vehicles can have multiple manifests and some of them will be arriving at the border at different schedules. As an example, customs officer may have included a manifest in a vehicle that has crossed the border in the morning, only to find out that the manifest associated with the same vehicle will arrive at the border in the evening instead. ## Pre-Requisites Customs officers for cancelling a vehicle gate-in should be a registered Customs officer in eCMS. Custom officers are authorized to access eCMS and have access to the required application. ## Process Flow Process ID: 03.02.05 – Cancel Gate-in ## Use Case Diagram Business Validation ## Passenger Manifests Overview ## Process ID: 03.03 – Passenger Manifest Passenger manifest is submitted by airline operators. For passenger lists, amendment is done by replacement of the original manifest after cancellation. Likewise, supplementary is also done as replacement after cancellation of the original manifest. ## Manifest Structure PASSENGER MANIFEST STRUCTURE The passenger manifest comprises of a header and a list of passengers. ## Passenger Manifest Submission eCMS will enable the user to submit passenger manifests through manual input or upload. eCMS will also enable a customs officer to approve the submission. ## Pre-Requisites Users for submitting a Passenger Manifest should be a registered Declarant (or CFA) in eCMS. Customs officers for approving a Passenger Manifest should be a registered Customs officer in eCMS. Both Declarants and Custom officers are authorized to access eCMS and have access to the required application. ## Process Flow Process ID: 03.03.01 – Passenger Manifest Submission ## Use Case Diagram Notes: A draft passenger manifest can be updated/deleted/submitted by any operator of the same airline company. ## Business Validation Update Passenger Manifest eCMS will enable the user to update an approved passenger manifest through manual input. eCMS will also enable a customs officer to approve the submission. At the time of submission of an update request, the applicant can update the following but not limited to; ## Add/delete passenger from the manifest Edit passenger details in the manifest ## Pre-Requisites Users for updating a Passenger Manifest should be a registered Declarant (or CFA) in eCMS. Customs officers for approving a Passenger Manifest update should be a registered Customs officer in eCMS. Both Declarants and Custom officers are authorized to access eCMS and have access to the required application. ## Process Flow Process ID: 03.03.02 – Update Passenger Manifest ## Use Case Diagram Notes: A draft request can be updated/deleted/submitted by any operator of the same airline company. ## Business Validation Passenger Manifest Cancellation eCMS will enable the user to cancel an approved passenger manifest. eCMS will also enable a customs officer to approve the cancellation. ## Pre-Requisites Users for cancelling a Passenger Manifest should be a registered Declarant (or CFA) in eCMS. Customs officers for approving a Passenger Manifest cancellation should be a registered Customs officer in eCMS. Both Declarants and Custom officers are authorized to access eCMS and have access to the required application. ## Process Flow Process ID: 03.03.03 – Passenger Manifest Cancellation ## Use Case Diagram Business Validation ## Dispatch Challan Overview ## Process ID: 03.04 – Dispatch Challan Dispatch Challan are required by Traders for Transportation of International Transit Declaration across the International boundary for entry into Bhutan. It serves twin purpose of authorization of transportation through the international boundary as well as for Gate in of the goods in Bhutan. Post approval of the International Transit declaration and associated LOG (Letter of Guarantee), the declarant shall liaison with local Customs of the transiting country and procure the Bill of entry details. Subsequently, the declarant will submit a Dispatch challan for each International Transit declaration including amongst others, ## The Vehicle registration number of the transporting vehicle The approved International Transit declaration. ## The details of the driver of the vehicle Upon submission of the dispatch Challan, the LTO office will review and approve the Challan. System will consolidate the approved dispatch Challan based on matching Vehicle number and date of departure and assign a unique Consolidated challan number. Once the LTO determines that all dispatch challans are consolidated, the LTO can take a print of the consolidated Challan and handover to the Transporter for transiting to Bhutan. ## Assumptions and Restrictions Since multiple CFA’s can apply for dispatch challan for the same vehicle, therefore, after consolidation, the LTO shall generate the print of the Consolidated challan. This will control inadvertent printing of the consolidated Challan by the CFA before the consolidation could be completed. A dispatch challan can be linked to only one International Transit Declaration. The system will consolidate individual dispatch challan automatically at the vehicle level during customs approval. Consolidation will be done even if there is only one dispatch challan against the vehicle. It is assumed that a given vehicle engaged in transportation of international transit declaration cannot do multiple trips on the same day. Gate In at the Bhutan border shall be done at the Consolidated challan level. However, at the time of declaration the individual dispatch challan will be used Prints shall be generated only for the Consolidated dispatch challan. Prints are not required for individual dispatch challan. The international transit declaration instead of the dispatch challan will be used for temporary storage in LTO. ## Dispatch Challan Notification The system sends a notification through email at various stages of the dispatch challan processing. The events at which notification is sent is listed below. ## Dispatch Challan Process eCMS will enable the user to submit dispatch challans through manual input. eCMS will also enable a LTO officer to approve the submission. ## Pre-Requisites 1. Associated International Transit declaration has been submitted and approved. 2. LOG associated with the international transit declaration has been submitted. 3. Declarant has coordinated with local Customs body of the transiting country and procured the Bill of entry details required as an input for the dispatch Challan. 4. Declarant has the correct and accurate vehicle details which will be engaged for transporting the consignments. 5. Declarant should be registered in the System and can access eCMS. 6. LTO Officers are registered and can access eCMS. ## Process Flow Process ID: 03.04.01 – Dispatch Challan Process ## Use Case Diagram Note/s: A draft dispatch can be updated/deleted/submitted by any user of the same party or by a CFA. ## Business Validation Dispatch Challan Amendment eCMS will enable the user to amend an approved dispatch challan through manual input. eCMS will also enable a LTO officer to approve the request. ## Pre-Requisites Users for submitting a Dispatch Challan Amendment should be a registered Declarant (or CFA) in eCMS. LTO officers for approving a Dispatch Challan Amendment should be a registered Customs officer in eCMS. Both Declarants and LTO officers are authorized to access eCMS and have access to the required application. ## Process Flow Process ID: 03.04.02 – Dispatch Challan Amendment ## Use Case Diagram Note/s: A request in Draft status can be updated/deleted/submitted by any user of the same party that created the amendment request or by a CFA. ## Business Validation Gate-In Challan eCMS will enable the customs officer to gate-in a consolidated challan along with the declarations (international transits declaration) linked to it. This is to allow the customs officer to indicate which dispatch challan/s registered under a particular vehicle that is about to cross the border. ## Pre-Requisites Customs officers for updating a consolidated challan for gate-in should be a registered Customs officer in eCMS. Custom officers are authorized to access eCMS and have access to the required application. ## Process Flow Process ID: 03.04.03 – Gate-in Challan ## Use Case Diagram Business Validation ## Temporary Storage Overview ## Process ID: 03.05 – Temporary Storage Goods that arrive by Air transport (AWB), Road (Manifest Invoice) the declarant/CFA must submit separate request to admit into temporary storage after the Air/Road manifest or Dispatch Challan has been approved. ## Admit Goods into Temporary Storage The process of admitting the goods into the Temporary Storage starts once the manifest/dispatch challan is submitted and approved and moved the consignment into temporary storage by submitting a Temporary Storage Request. The system will save the request with a Pending Admittance status and the request will be routed to the temporary storage operator assigned to the storage. ## Pre-Requisites Declarant/CFA must be submitting an entry request to temporary storage before admitting into Temporary Storage. ## Process Flow Process ID: 03.05.01 – Goods Admittance to Temporary Storage ## Use Case Diagram Business Validation ## Release Goods from Temporary Storage The process of releasing the goods from the Temporary Storage starts after the Clearance process (i.e., Release Cargo) of the declarations ## Pre-Requisites Declaration must be submitted, duties are paid and completed the customs clearance process. ## Process Flow Process ID: 03.05.02 – Goods Release from Temporary Storage ## Process Steps Use Case Diagram ## Business Validation Note/s: Declarations are created using the relevant manifest in case the specific manifest is admitted into temporary storage that declaration will be released from temporary storage after the “Release Cargo” process. If submitted master AWB (10 Qty) must split into 2 House AWB (7 Qty and 3 Qty). Then we recommend splitting the master AWL into 2 as house manifest and then request to submit House AWB to admit into temporary storage as two separate requests i.e. 7 Qty and 3 Qty. This will allow declarant to submit declaration to the corresponding House AWB and release accordingly. Entry manifest quantity and import declaration quantity must be equal and 1 manifest must have 1 declaration only. Additionally, consolidated AWB cannot be submitted for Temporary Storage admission. ## Appendix A Configuration blueprint (CBP) ## Configuration Blueprint (CBP) for Manifest: Configuration Blueprint (CBP) for Temporary Storage: ## Air Manifest Upload files IATA Specification for Air Manifest: ## Sample FFM (Master Manifest) File: Sample FWB (Additional Manifest) File: ## Sample FHL (House Manifest) File: Passenger manifest Integration file template ## Passenger manifest integration File: Manifest Printouts ## Air Manifest Printout: Road Manifest Printout: ## Passenger Manifest Printout: Temporary Storage Tracking Details ## Inventory Report: Dispatch Challan Printout ## Dispatch Challan: Scheduler Jobs ## User Interface Please refer to the prototype. Note: Though we released the prototype, actual UI implementation look-and-feel may vary based on SmartGWT framework. [TABLE] Process Steps P01.1: Create Manifest Header The user creates an air manifest starting with the header data. After entering all the mandatory inputs, the user can save the header data. But before allowing the header to be saved, the system will validate the inputs and will display messages if there are errors encountered. If there are no validation issues, the system will generate a unique Provisional Manifest Number and save the air manifest header with a Draft status. The Provisional Manifest Number will have the following format: PAM<DDMMYYYY######> where: DD – date MM – month YYYY – year ##### - running sequence number P01.2: Create Air Waybill/s The user can create air waybill/s only after the header data has been saved. The user can create as many AWBs in the system. After entering all the mandatory inputs, the user can save the AWB data. But before allowing the AWB to be saved, the system will validate the inputs and will display messages if there are errors encountered. If there are no validation issues, the system will save the AWB. Note/s: The AWB number should be assigned a reference value that is unique within the manifest. If the AWB type is Consolidated, then user must select a Consolidator Account Code from the list of Freight Forwarder/Clearing Agent parties and assign it to the AWB. The assigned Freight Forwarder can submit House Manifest and subsequent declaration. P01.3: Upload Manifest File The user can also create an air manifest by uploading a file in eCMS. The file format will be the one approved by DRC. The user uploads the file with minimal mandatory inputs. Only one manifest can be created per file upload. After entering all the mandatory inputs, the user can save the air manifest file. But before allowing the file to be saved, the system will validate the inputs and file contents and will display messages if there are errors encountered. If there are no validation issues, the system will save the air manifest file and start processing its data. P01.4: Create Air Manifest After the system uploads the manifest file, the system will create and save the corresponding manifest header & AWBs with a Draft status.
