Afterwards, the user must enter the number of containers to add and create the corresponding number of container records. After entering all the mandatory inputs, the user can save the invoice/container data. But before allowing the invoice/container to be saved, the system will validate the inputs and will display messages if there are errors encountered. If there are no validation issues, the system will save the invoice/container record. Note/s: The Invoice number should be assigned a reference value that is unique within the manifest. The container should be unique within the manifest. P03: Submit Road Manifest The user submits the road manifest after creating the necessary invoice/s and truck detail/s . But before allowing the manifest to be submitted, the system will validate the manifest as a whole and will display messages if there are errors encountered. If there are no validation issues, the system will submit the manifest with a Pending Approval status and will route the manifest it to a customs officer for approval. The customs officer who will receive the manifest will depend on the Customs Office that the user selected for the manifest. Note/s: The number of invoices created should be equal to the number of invoices indicated in the manifest header. P04: Reject or Approve The manifest is routed to a customs officer for approval. The customs officer selects the manifest and determines which of the following statuses will be applied: Approve Reject for Amendments Reject If the customs officer rejected the manifest/rejected the manifest for amendments, the user will be notified via email. If the customs officer rejected the manifest, the user can submit a new Road Manifest afterwards to replace the rejected one. If the customs officer rejected the manifest for amendments, the manifest will be routed back to the user for update and re-submission. If the customs officer approved the manifest, the manifest and its invoices will have an Approved status. Note/s: During approval, the customs officer will see all the vehicles with manifests that have not yet been approved/rejected. The customs officer will choose a vehicle and another screen will be displayed that will contain all the manifests associated with the vehicle. The customs officer can finally choose the manifest that has a pending approval status and do the approval. A manifest will be auto-approved by the system if its customs office has been configured to auto-approve a manifest. P05.1: Update Road Manifest After the request was rejected for amendments, the user updates the road manifest to correct the issues that caused its rejection. If the user updates the manifest header and then tries to save it, it will be subjected to the same validation process mentioned in P01. If the user updates an invoice and then tries to save it, it will be subjected to the same validation processes mentioned in P02. P05.2: Approve Road Manifest After the customs officer approves the manifest, the invoices can then be used to submit declarations. P06: Submit Temporary Storage Request The user can choose to move the consignment to temporary storage by submitting a Temporary Storage Request. The system will save the request with a Pending Admittance status and the request will be routed to the temporary storage officer assigned to the storage the user selected. P07: Admit to Temporary Storage The temporary storage officer who receives the request will facilitate the actual movement of the consignment to the temporary storage. Once this has been completed, the request will be updated with an Admitted status. If the temporary storage request is rejected, then the Declarant/CFA should submit the declaration with the AWB. [TABLE] S/N | Validation Rules 1 | The Invoice number should be assigned a reference value that is unique within the manifest. 2 | The chassis number of the vehicle should be unique within the manifest. 3 | The container should be unique within the manifest. 4 | The number of invoices created should be equal to the number of invoices indicated in the manifest header. [TABLE] Process Steps P01: Create Request Header The user creates a road manifest amendment starting with the request header. The user selects a manifest created by the user’s party and with an Approved status. Only one manifest can be selected for a road manifest amendment request. After selecting the manifest, the user can start updating Road Manifest header details except for the Rotation Number. An invoice will be available for update/deletion if: it is not used/linked in an active declaration it is not used in another cancellation request that is pending approval it is not cancelled it is not used in another amendment request that is pending approval Multiple invoices can be selected in a road manifest amendment request. The system will allow amendment of the vehicle details as well as driver details. After entering all the mandatory inputs, the user can save the header data. But before allowing the header to be saved, the system will validate the inputs and will display messages if there are errors encountered. If there are no validation issues, the system will generate a Provisional Amendment Manifest Number and save the request header with a Draft status. The Provisional Amendment Manifest Number will have the following format: PAMR<DDMMYYYY######> where: DD – date MM – month YYYY – year ##### - running sequence number Note/s: Once the request header has been saved, the selected manifest number for update can no longer be changed. P02: Update Road Manifest Header The system will load the road manifest the user selected, and the user can update it. After updating all the editable inputs, the user can save them. But before allowing the details to be saved, the system will validate the inputs and will display messages if there are errors encountered. If there are no validation issues, the updates will be saved. Note: Manifest Number cannot be updated. P03: Update Invoice List The system will load the invoice list of the manifest that the user selected. The user can then add/delete invoices from the invoice list or update invoice data in the list. After updating all the editable inputs, the user can save them. But before allowing the details to be saved, the system will validate the inputs and will display messages if there are errors encountered. If there are no validation issues, the updates will be saved. P04: Submit Road Manifest Update The user submits the road manifest amendment after saving the invoice updates. But before allowing the request to be submitted, the system will validate the request as a whole and will display messages if there are errors encountered. If there are no validation issues, the system will submit the manifest with a Pending Approval status and will route the manifest to a customs officer for approval. The customs officer who will receive the manifest will depend on the Customs Office that the user selected for the manifest. P05: Reject or Approve The request is routed to a customs officer for approval. The customs officer selects the request and determines which of the following statuses will be applied: Approve Reject for Amendments Reject If the customs officer rejected the request for amendments, the user will be notified via email. If the customs officer rejected the request, the user can submit a new Road Manifest Amendment afterwards to replace the rejected one. If the customs officer rejected the request, the request will be routed back to the user for update and re-submission. If the customs officer approves the request, the request will have an Approved status. P06.1: Update Rejected Manifest After the request was rejected for amendments, the user updates the road manifest update to correct the issues that caused its rejection. If the user updates the request header and then tries to save, it will be subjected to the same validation process mentioned in P02. If the user updates an invoice and then tries to save, it will be subjected to the same validation process mentioned in P03. P06.2: Update Manifest After the customs officer approves the request, the updates will take effect and will be in the current version of the manifest. A copy of the previous original values of the updated manifest will also be saved with a version number for audit purposes. A unique Amendment Manifest Number will also be assigned to the request. The Amendment Manifest Number will have the following format: AMR<DDMMYYYY######> where: DD – date MM – month YYYY – year ###### - running sequence number [TABLE] S/N | Validation Rules 1 | An invoice will be available for an update request if: it is not used in an active declaration it is not used in another cancellation request that is pending approval it is not cancelled it is not used in another amendment request that is pending approval 2 | The manifest number cannot be updated. [TABLE] Process Steps P01: Create Request Header The user creates a road manifest cancellation starting with the request header. The user selects a manifest created by the user’s party and with an Approved status. Only one manifest can be selected for a road manifest cancellation request. A manifest can be selected for cancellation if: it is not used in an active declaration It is not yet included another cancellation request pending approval it is not cancelled it is not in temporary storage vehicle has not yet entered the country (no gate-in reference number) After entering all the mandatory inputs, the user can save the header data. But before allowing the header to be saved, the system will validate the inputs and will display messages if there are errors encountered. If there are no validation issues, the system will generate a Cancellation Manifest Number and save the request header with a Draft status. The Cancellation Manifest Number will have the following format: CNCL<DDMMYYYY######> where: DD – date MM – month YYYY – year ##### - running sequence number P02: Submit Road Manifest Cancellation The user submits the road manifest cancellation. If there are no validation issues, the system will save the request with a Pending Approval status and will route the request to a customs officer for approval. The customs officer who will receive the request will depend on the Customs Office that the user selected for the original road manifest. P03: Reject or Approve The request is routed to a customs officer for approval. The customs officer selects the request and determines which of the following statuses will be applied: Approve Reject If the customs officer rejected the request the user will be notified via email. The user can submit a new Road Manifest Cancellation afterwards to replace the rejected one. If the customs officer approved the request, the request will have an Approved status. P04: Cancel Manifest After the request has been approved, the manifest in the request will have a Cancelled status The system will maintain the history of the record. [TABLE] S/N | Validation Rules 1 | A manifest can be selected for cancellation if: it is not used in an active declaration It is not yet included another cancellation request pending approval it is not cancelled it is not in temporary storage vehicle has not yet entered the country (no gate-in reference number) [TABLE] Process Steps P01: Select Vehicle for Gate-In The customs officer will be presented with a list of vehicles whose manifest are not included in a vehicle that has crossed the border (or gate-in). Only one vehicle can be selected at a time for gate-in update. P02: Select Manifest/s to be Included with Vehicle After selecting a vehicle, the customs officer will be presented with a list of manifest/s that include the vehicle but have not yet been included in a gate-in. The list will be filtered to show the manifests whose ETA is today’s date. The customs officer must determine which manifest/s are included in the vehicle that is about to cross the border and select them. At least one manifest should be selected for gate-in. Note: The system will automatically cancel those approved manifest that do not enter the country after 30 days from the date of approval. P03: Gate-In Vehicle with Manifest/s After selecting the manifest/s, the customs officer can update the vehicle status to Gate-In. A Gate-in timestamp and Gate-in Reference Number will be assigned to the vehicle and selected manifests. Manifest/s that were included in the gate-in will no longer shown for gate-in purposes unless their gate-in status has been cancelled. [TABLE] S/N | Validation Rules 1 | Manifest/s that were included in the gate-in will no longer shown for gate-in purposes unless their gate-in status has been cancelled. [TABLE] Process Steps P01: Select Vehicle for Gate-in Cancellation The customs officer will be presented with a list of vehicles whose manifest are included in a gate-in process. Only one vehicle can be selected at a time for gate-in update. P02: Select Manifest/s to Cancel Gate-In After selecting a vehicle, the customs officer will be presented with a list of manifest/s had been included in the vehicle’s gate-in. The customs officer must determine which manifest/s are not included in the vehicle that had crossed the border and select them. At least one manifest should be selected for gate-in cancellation. P03: Cancel Manifest/s that had Gate-In After selecting the manifest/s, the customs officer can clear the manifest’s Gate-In date and Gate-In reference number. Manifest/s that were included in the gate-in cancellation will again show-up for gate-in purposes. [TABLE] S/N | Validation Rules 1 | Manifest/s that were included in the gate-in cancellation will again show-up for gate-in purposes. [TABLE] Process Steps P01.1: Create Manifest Header The user creates a passenger manifest starting with the header data. After entering all the mandatory inputs, the user can save the header data. But before allowing the header to be saved, the system will validate the inputs and will display messages if there are errors encountered. If there are no validation issues, the system will generate a unique Manifest Number and save the passenger manifest header with a Draft status. The Manifest Number will have the following format: XXX<DDMMYYYY######> where: XXX – Customs Site Code DD – date MM – month YYYY – year ###### - running sequence number P01.2: Create Passenger List The user can create the passenger record only after the header data has been saved. The user can create as many passengers as possible in the system. After entering all the mandatory inputs, the user can save the passenger data. But before allowing the passenger to be saved, the system will validate the inputs and will display messages if there are errors encountered. If there are no validation issues, the system will save the passenger record. Note/s: The passport number should be unique within the manifest. P01.3: Upload Passenger Manifest File The user can also create a passenger manifest by uploading it as a file in eCMS. The file format will be the one approved by DRC. After receiving the manifest, the system will validate the inputs and will respond with messages if there are errors encountered. If there are no validation issues, the system will respond with a success message and save the passenger manifest file and start processing its data. P01.4: Create Passenger Manifest After the system uploads the manifest file via system integration, the system will create and save the corresponding manifest header & passenger list with a Draft status. A unique Manifest Number will also be generated and will be displayed so that the user can use it to access the record later and manually submit. The Manifest Number will have the following format: XXX<DDMMYYYY######> where: XXX – Customs Site Code DD – date MM – month YYYY – year ###### - running sequence number P02: Submit Passenger Manifest The user submits the passenger manifest after creating the necessary passenger records. But before allowing the manifest to be submitted, the system will validate the manifest as a whole and will display messages if there are errors encountered. If there are no validation issues, the system will submit the manifest with a Pending Approval status and will route the manifest to a customs officer for approval. The customs officer who will receive the manifest will depend on the Customs Office that the user selected for the manifest. Note/s: The number of passengers created should be equal to the number of passengers indicated in the manifest header. P03: Reject or Approve The manifest is routed to a customs officer for approval. The customs officer selects the manifest and determines which of the following statuses will be applied: Approve Reject for Amendments Reject If the customs officer rejected the manifest/rejected the manifest for amendments, the user will be notified via email. If the customs officer rejected the manifest, the user can submit a new Passenger Manifest afterwards to replace the rejected one. If the customs officer rejected the manifest for amendments, the manifest will be routed back to the user for update and re-submission. If the customs officer approved the manifest, the manifest and passenger list will have an Approved status. P04.1: Update Passenger Manifest After the request was rejected for amendments, the user updates the passenger manifest to correct the issues that caused its rejection. If the user updates the manifest header and then tries to save, it will be subjected to the same validation process mentioned in P01.1. If the user updates a passenger and then tries to save, it will be subjected to the same validation process mentioned in P01.2. P04.2: Approve Passenger Manifest After the customs officer approved the manifest, the passenger manifest is no longer editable. [TABLE] S/N | Validation Rules 1 | The number of passengers created should be equal to the number of passengers indicated in the manifest header. [TABLE] Process Steps P01: Create Request Header The user creates an update passenger manifest starting with the request header. The user selects a manifest created by the user’s party and with an Approved status. Only one manifest can be selected for an update passenger manifest request. A passenger manifest can be selected for update if: it is not used in another update request that is pending approval it is not used in another cancellation request that is pending approval it is not cancelled After entering all the mandatory inputs, the user can save the request. But before allowing the request to be saved, the system will validate the inputs and will display messages if there are errors encountered. If there are no validation issues, the system will generate an Update Manifest Number and save the request header with a Draft status. The Update Manifest Number will have the following format: UPD<DDMMYYYY######> where: DD – date MM – month YYYY – year ##### - running sequence number P02: Update Passenger Manifest Header The system will load the passenger manifest the user selected and the user can update it. After updating all the editable inputs, the user can save them. But before allowing the details to be saved, the system will validate the inputs and will display messages if there are errors encountered. If there are no validation issues, the updates will be saved. Note: Manifest Number cannot be updated. P03: Update Passenger List The system will load the passenger list of the manifest that the user selected. The user can then add/delete passengers from the passenger list or update passenger data in the list. After updating all the editable inputs, the user can save them. But before allowing the details to be saved, the system will validate the inputs and will display messages if there are errors encountered. If there are no validation issues, the updates will be saved. P04: Submit Passenger Manifest Update The user submits the passenger manifest update. If there are no validation issues, the system will submit the request with a Pending Approval status and will route the request to a customs officer for approval. The customs officer who will receive the request will depend on the Customs Office that the user selected for the original passenger manifest. P05: Reject or Approve The request is routed to a customs officer for approval. The customs officer selects the request and determines which of the following statuses will be applied: Approve Reject for Amendments Reject If the customs officer rejected the request/rejected the request for amendments, the user will be notified via email. If the customs officer rejected the manifest, the user can submit a new Update Passenger Manifest afterwards to replace the rejected one. If the customs officer rejected the request for amendments, the request will be routed back to the user for update and re-submission. If the customs officer approved the request, the request will have an Approved status. P06.1: Update Rejected Request After the request was rejected for amendments, the user updates the passenger manifest update request to correct the issues that caused its rejection. If the user updates the request header and then tries to save it, it will be subjected to the same validation process mentioned in P02 and P03. P06.2: Update Manifest After the request has been approved, then only the updates will take effect in the passenger manifest. [TABLE] S/N | Validation Rules 1 | A passenger manifest can be selected for update if: • it is not used in another update request that is pending approval • it is not used in another cancellation request that is pending approval • it is not cancelled 2 | The manifest number cannot be updated. [TABLE] Process Steps P01: Create Request Header The user creates a passenger manifest cancellation starting with the request header. The user selects a manifest created by the user’s party and with an Approved status. Only one manifest can be selected for a passenger manifest cancellation request. A manifest can be selected for cancellation if: current date is not past the Estimated Arrival Time After entering all the mandatory inputs, the user can save the header data. But before allowing the header to be saved, the system will validate the inputs and will display messages if there are errors encountered. If there are no validation issues, the system will generate a Cancellation Manifest Number and save the request header with a Draft status. The Cancellation Manifest Number will have the following format: CNCL<DDMMYYYY######> where: DD – date MM – month YYYY – year ##### - running sequence number P02: Submit Passenger Manifest Cancellation The user submits the passenger manifest cancellation. If there are no validation issues, the system will save the request with a Pending Approval status and will route the request to a customs officer for approval. The customs officer who will receive the request will depend on the Customs Office that the user selected for the original passenger manifest. P03: Reject or Approve The request is routed to a customs officer for approval. The customs officer selects the request and determines which of the following statuses will be applied: Approve Reject If the customs officer rejected the request the user will be notified via email. The user can submit a new Passenger Manifest Cancellation afterwards to replace the rejected one. If the customs officer approved the request, the request will have an Approved status. P04: Cancel Manifest After the request has been approved, the manifest in the request will have a Cancelled status. The system will maintain the history of the record. [TABLE] S/N | Validation Rules 1 | A manifest can be selected for cancellation if: It is not yet included another cancellation request pending approval it is not cancelled [TABLE] Function | Notification Rejection after submission | Declarant/Trader Rejection for amendment | Declarant/Trader Individual approval of manifest | Declarant/Trader Approval along with Consolidation number | Declarant [TABLE] PROCESS STEPS P01: Create Dispatch Challan The declarant creates a dispatch challan and provides the following key inputs amongst others Approved International Transit Declaration. Vehicle number for transportation of goods. Drivers Details Additionally, declarant will provide all required mandatory field and submit the dispatch challan. P02: Submit Dispatch Challan After submission of the dispatch challan, the challan shall be routed to the work queue of the next available Verifier at the LTO, on a rotational basis. If the Verifier is not available for any reason, Senior Verifiers must also be able to re-assign work assigned to Verifiers within their team. P03: Verify Dispatch Challan Verifier will verify the dispatch challan and ascertain that all details are provided correctly. The verifier will have the following options. Approve: In this case, the challan will be approved and routed for consolidation. Reject: In this case, the challan shall be rejected. Recommend for Amendment: In this case, the challan shall be routed back to declarant for amendment and re-submission. In all cases, declarant shall be notified of the decision of LTO through email. In case of Rejection, reasons for rejection shall be communicated. P04: Reject for amendment If the Verifier determines that the challan needs to be amended, then the verifier can reject the challan for amendment. The challan shall be routed for Amendment. Declarant shall receive an email notification and can amend the challan and re-submit. P05: Rejected If the verifier determines that the challan needs to be rejected, then the verifier shall select reason for rejection and provide remarks. The challan shall be rejected, and no further actions are possible on the rejected challan. Declarant will be sent a notification on the rejection. P06: Approval and Consolidation of Challans If the verifier concludes that provided dispatch challan are correct, then the verifier can approve the dispatch challan. Upon approval of the dispatch challan, system will consolidate the approved dispatch challan with previously approved dispatch challan sharing the same vehicle registration number. A unique consolidation number shall be generated which will link all related dispatch challan which share the same vehicle number. After completion of consolidation, the CFA shall be informed on the approval and consolidation number through email. System shall also offer the following Consolidation number will be shown to the CFA alongside the dispatch challan in the CFA view of dispatch challan. LTO can search and view Consolidation details of all dispatch challans through a consolidated challan search and view interface. P07: Generate consolidated dispatch challan number During consolidation of dispatch challan, system will generate a unique consolidation number for the consolidation at the vehicle registration number level. Future approved dispatch challan for the same vehicle number shall be consolidated under the consolidation number already generated for the vehicle. Once a consolidation number for a vehicle has been generated, it shall be used for all consolidation against the vehicle until the vehicle completes gate-out from LTO. Once the vehicle gates out from LTO the consolidation number shall be deemed as closed and the system will not allow any further consolidation of dispatch challan. Future dispatch challans against the same vehicle will have a new consolidation number. P08: Print dispatch challan number After consolidation, LTO can generate a print of the consolidated dispatch challan. P09: Gate in in Bhutan using consolidated dispatch challan number A Gate officer at Bhutan port can Gate in using the consolidated dispatch challan. Upon completion of Gate in, the consolidation shall be considered as closed. Additional process for Gate in is covered separately under Gate In process for Dispatch challan. [TABLE] S/N | Validation Rules 1 | The CFA can only view dispatch challan created by them. 2 | CFA will need to link an approved international transit declaration which was submitted by the same CFA. 3 | An international transit declaration can be linked to only one dispatch challan. 4 | A dispatch challan can have only one international transit declaration. 5 | The consolidated dispatch challan will have multiple international transit declaration 6 | After gate-out from the LTO, future dispatch challan will not be consolidated under the same and any dispatch challan submitted for the same vehicle will have a new consolidation. 7 | Before Gate out from LTO, all dispatch challan approved for a vehicle will share the same consolidation number. The dispatch challan should have at least one declaration linked to it. The consolidated challan can have at least one dispatch challan linked to it. [TABLE] Process Steps P01.1: Create Request Header The user creates a dispatch challan amendment request starting with the request header. The user selects a dispatch challan created by the user’s party and with an Approved status. A dispatch challan will be available for an amendment request if: the international transit declaration in the dispatch challan has not gated it is not used in another amendment request that is pending approval After entering all the mandatory inputs, the user can save the header data. But before allowing the header to be saved, the system will validate the inputs and will display messages if there are errors encountered. If there are no validation issues, the system will generate a Provisional Amendment Dispatch Challan Number and save the request header with a Draft status. The Provisional Amendment Dispatch Challan Number will have the following format: PCHR<DDMMYYYY######> where: DD – date MM – month YYYY – year ##### - running sequence number Note/s: Once the request header has been saved, the selected dispatch challan can no longer be changed. P01.2: Update Dispatch Challan The user can update the dispatch challan only after the header data has been saved. After updating the inputs, the user can save the challan data. But before allowing the challan to be saved, the system will validate the inputs and will display messages if there are errors encountered. If there are no validation issues, the system will save the updates. Note/s: The dispatch challan number cannot be updated. P02: Submit Dispatch Challan Amendment The user submits the dispatch challan amendment after saving the updates. But before allowing the request to be submitted, the system will validate the request as a whole and will display messages if there are errors encountered. If there are no validation issues, the system will submit the manifest with a Pending Approval status and will route the manifest to a customs officer for approval. The customs officer who will receive the manifest will depend on the Customs Office that the user selected for the manifest. P03: Reject or Approve The request is routed to a customs officer for approval. The customs officer selects the request and determines which of the following statuses will be applied: Approve Reject for Amendments Reject If the customs officer rejected the request for amendments, the user will be notified via email. If the customs officer rejected the request, the user can submit a new Road Manifest Amendment afterwards to replace the rejected one. If the customs officer rejected the request, the request will be routed back to the user for update and re-submission. If the customs officer approves the request, the request will have an Approved status. P04.1: Update Dispatch Challan Amendment After the request was rejected for amendments, the user updates the road manifest amendment to correct the issues that caused its rejection. If the user updates the request header and then tries to save, it will be subjected to the same validation process mentioned in P01.1. If the user updates an invoice and then tries to save, it will be subjected to the same validation process mentioned in P01.2. P04.2: Amend Dispatch Challan After the customs officer approves the request, the dispatch challan updates will take effect and will be in the current version of the dispatch challan. A copy of the previous original values of the updated dispatch challan will also be saved with a version number for audit purposes. A unique Amendment Dispatch Challan Number will also be assigned to the request. The Amendment Dispatch Challan Number will have the following format: ACHR<DDMMYYYY######> where: DD – date MM – month YYYY – year ###### - running sequence number [TABLE] S/N | Validation Rules 1 | An approved individual dispatch challan will be available for an amendment request if: the international transit declaration in the dispatch challan has not yet cleared the first port it is not used in another amendment request that is pending approval However, the system will not allow consolidation of individual manifest after the same has been released from the port of exit (LTO) [TABLE] Process Steps P01: Select Consolidated Challan for Gate-In The customs officer will be presented with a list of consolidated challan whose vehicle have not yet crossed the border (or gated-in). Only one consolidated challan can be selected at a time for gate-in update. P02: Gate-In Consolidated Challan After selecting a vehicle, the customs officer will be presented with a list of declarations linked to the consolidated challan. The customs officer can then update the consolidated challan’s status to Gate-In. A Gate-in timestamp and Gate-in Reference Number will be assigned to the consolidated challan. Once a consolidated challan has gated-in, the vehicle will be available for new dispatch challan. [TABLE] S/N | Validation Rules 1 | The vehicle will be available again for dispatch challan once it has gate-in in Bhutan. [TABLE] Process Steps P01: Submit Temporary Storage Request Once the CFA submitted the request to admit manifest into temporary storage which they were importing for home use, the manifest can be seen by the concerned temporary Storage Operator for admission of the goods into the temporary storage. Note/s: An air waybill/invoice will be available for a temporary storage request if: it is not used in an active declaration (for invoice/air waybill) it is not a consolidated BL type (for air waybills) it is not used in another cancellation request that is pending approval (for invoice/air waybill) it is not used in another amendment request that is pending approval it is not cancelled (for invoice/air waybill) it is not in temporary storage P02: Admit to Temporary Storage The temporary storage operator will process the request and facilitate the actual movement of the consignment to the temporary storage. Once this has been completed, the request will be updated with an Admitted status. [TABLE] S/N | Validation Rules 1 | An air waybill/invoice details will be available for a temporary storage request if: it is not used in an active declaration (for invoice/air waybill) it is not a consolidated BL type (for air waybills) it is not used in another cancellation request that is pending approval (for invoice/air waybill) it is not used in another amendment request that is pending approval it is not cancelled (for invoice/air waybill) it is not in temporary storage 2 | The temporary storage officer can only admit goods that have been requested for the temporary storage assigned to the officer. [TABLE] P01: Calculate Storage Fees Declarants need to create and submit import declaration and calculate the charges based on goods can only remain in temporary storage for up to seven (7) working days. After seven (7) working days, the goods have not removed from temporary storage, then storage charges will be applied for each day up to a maximum of fifteen (15) working days. P02: Release from Temporary Storage Once the release officer released the goods in the import declaration/temporary admission/warehouse, national transit, the approved declaration can be seen by the concerned Temporary Storage Operator for release of the goods from the Temporary Storage. The goods/items of the Import declaration are released from the Temporary Storage by the Temporary Storage Operator. [TABLE] S/N | Validation Rules 1 | The temporary storage officer can only release goods that have been admitted in the temporary storage assigned to the officer. [TABLE] Job Name | Running Interval | Remarks Auto-Cancel AWB | Everyday | Cancel AWB if 30 days (configurable) after Estimated Time of Arrival: it is not in Temporary Storage it is not in a declaration Auto-Cancel Road Manifest | Everyday | Cancel Road manifest if 30 days (configurable) after Estimated Time of Arrival, if it has no Gate-In Reference Number and is not linked to a Declaration

title: PCA user manual
content:
[TRADER] PCA user manual

## General Release No 1.0 – March 2021 ## Endorsement by System Owner (internal) release history ## Table of Contents Table of Contents 3 ## Introduction 4 A. Definitions and Abbreviations 4 ## B. References 6 Audit Trail Functional Requirements 7 1. Audit Trail Overview 7 1.1 Audit Trail Data Collector 7 1.2 Audit Type 7 1.3 Viewing Audit Trail 8 1.4 Audit Requirement 9 1.5 Use Case Diagram for Audit Data Collector and Audit Viewing 13 ## Code Maintenance Functional Requirements 14 2. Code Maintenance Overview 14 2.1 Code Maintenance to create, update, view. 14 2.2 Process Flow for Code Maintenance (Generic) 15 2.3 Use Case Diagram for Code maintenance to create/update and view. 18 ## Reset Password Functional Requirements 19 3. Reset Password Overview 19 3.1 Process Flow for Reset Password (Generic) 19 3.2 Use case for Reset Password. 20 ## Notice and Update Functional Requirements 21 4. Notice and Update Overview 21 4.1 Process Flow for Notice and Update (Generic) 22 4.2 Use case for Notice and Update. 23 ## Resource Management FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS 24 5. RESOURCE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM OVERVIEW 24 5.1 Resource Management 24 5.2 Resource Assignment 26 5.3 Use Cases for Resource Management 30 ## Appendix A 32 1. Configuration blueprint (CBP) 32 ## Introduction This document defines & illustrates the business requirements, process flows as well as the detailed functional requirements of CMS System Administration module to be implemented for Department of Revenue and Customs Bhutan. ## Definitions and Abbreviations The table below lists the different acronyms and abbreviations as well as the definitions used throughout this SRS. ## References The creation of the CMS SRS was referenced using the following documents: ## FUNCATIONAL REQUIREMENT SPECIFICATION.docx TECHNICAL REQUIREMENT SPECIFICATION.docx ## Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-3.pdf Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-4.pdf ## Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-5A.pdf Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-5B.pdf ## Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-6A.pdf Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-6B.pdf ## Audit Trail Functional Requirements Audit Trail Overview The Audit Trail module is used to audit various functionalities in CMS modules by storing the details in audit tables. The Audit Trail module contains mainly two functions. The first one is called Data Collector and the other one is called Data Viewer. All modules in CMS will have audit logging. The Audit Trail module is used by the system administrator (Customs) for system auditing and transaction auditing. Detailed audit tracking of each transaction can be done using the Audit Trail module. The Audit Trail module is a centralized module, and it tracks CMS audit. It is comprised of a front end for administrators to query and view a transaction audit log. At the backend all submitted transactions are audit trailed. System events like login/log out etc. will also be audited. The IP of the logged in user will also be tracked in the audit logs. ## Audit Trail Data Collector The Audit Trail Data Collector collects audit data from individual modules. Its function is to receive audit trail data from applications and then store the data in the database. ## Audit Type Audit type defined for the data collector determines if the audit is a transaction audit or a system error or system event. The following audit types are defined: Error – Errors & exceptions generated in the system. Log – This is general audit information. System – System events like system/instance restarts, instance shut down etc. ## Viewing Audit Trail A UI shall be provided for the system admin to view the audit logs. The UI will include filter options & search options to look for audit trail based on: ## Time period of audit Module ## User Id Audit type The search page will have a view option to view the audit record. The user will be able to see the data as a name value pair. For e.g. Declaration data will be shown as below: ## Declaration Number: DECL1000101 Declaration Type: Import ## CPC Group: Import from Home Destination Country: SG ## Audit Requirement Below is the table showing the information captured for each transaction. The business transaction reference number is the key for all transaction. ## Use Case Diagram for Audit Data Collector and Audit Viewing Code Maintenance Functional Requirements ## Code Maintenance Overview Code Maintenance is used to maintain the codes used in eCMS for a set of predefined code type. Code Maintenance allows for customs officer to create/update, view the code. The code type will be preloaded from the code master. After which, the customs officers can make the necessary updates. The code entered must be unique for that code type. ## Code Maintenance to create, update, view. Code Maintenance allow for the users to view, add, update. To add a new code, select the green, ‘+’ from the top right and user will be presented with a page (below). All the user requires to enter the code and description. The code entered must be unique for that code type. Example, Incoterm code type cannot have duplicate ‘EXW’ code. Validation is done during save process. ## Process Flow for Code Maintenance (Generic) Below is the table showing the description of each code type. ## Use Case Diagram for Code maintenance to create/update and view. Reset Password Functional Requirements ## Reset Password Overview User can reset password in Registration module. Password automatically generated by system and notification will send to registered user email. ## Process Flow for Reset Password (Generic) Use case for Reset Password. ## Notice and Update Functional Requirements Notice and Update Overview Admin will create or Update Notice/News under System Admin Module, Once Created/Updated Notice/News will publish on eCMS portal, Users can view the published notice details. ## Process Flow for Notice and Update (Generic) Use case for Notice and Update. ## Resource Management FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS RESOURCE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM OVERVIEW CMS use the resource management to assign officers to perform certain business functions like document verification, inspection on a specific declaration etc. The assignment is linked to a specific business transaction. The manager/supervisor of the customs office will configure resource management and can manually assign officers to task. ## Resource Management The setup for customs Admin and supervisor includes the following: ## Calendar year configuration Work shift assignment ## Setup vacation period of custom officers Task Configuration ## Pending tasks Calendar Year Configuration ## In the calendar year configuration, there are 4 tabs which requires setup: Calendar Setup for calendar year. ## Work week Setup of office hours for each day of the week. ## Work Shifts Working shifts Each custom officer is assigned a work shift when on duty. ## Holidays Setup for eCMS to recognize public holidays ## Work Shift Assignment This setup the custom officer’s “work shift” and the start and end date of the work shift assignment. ## Here are the fields needs to be setup: User ID – custom office user id. This is the ID which has been setup in the Registration-CMS User. From Date and To Date – the start and end of the configured work shift. Shift Name – This is the shift defined during the setup of the calendar. Active – it is valid. ## Setup of vacation period of custom officers All custom office needs to setup the vacation period so eCMS assignment engine will know whether an officer is present and can be assignment with new tasks. ## Here are the fields needs to be setup: User ID – custom office user id. From Date and to date - Start and end date of vacation. Remark - description. Active – value for eCMS assignment engine to know whether custom office is on vacation. ## Task Configuration This is the setup of the task and the roles of the assigned modules. ## Here are the fields needs to be setup: Task code – task code, unique. ## Task Name – Description of the task Module – Module for this task. Role – eCMS will only display the roles which is tied to the module. The role of the custom officers assigned to this task. This is tied to the CMS user’s role. Party – once set, it is only for the defined organization i.e. Customs. Customs office – once set, it is valid for the defined custom office. ## Algorithm Round Robin – each office is assigned a task assigned fairly. ## Due dates (from creation date) Days – number of days for the task to be completed once assigned. Type of Days – Working days/Calendar days. Calendar days mean weekend included while working days is tied to the work week as setup. ## Pending Tasks. This is used for reassignment of task to another officer. Supervising officer will use the function to assign task to another officer. ## Resource Assignment There are 2 ways for resources to be assigned to a task manual and automatically. ## Assignment Engine The automatic task assignment engine will be running on a periodic time to assign newly arrived task to the available officers. The engine will follow routing as per flow diagram below. ## Process Steps Design Considerations ## Manual Assignment Manual assignment will be available for the supervising custom officer to assign task which is not completed within the schedule or when a task is not assigned to any officer. Supervising officer uses the pending task menu found in Resource Management to assign task to specific custom officer. ## Overdue task engine There will be an engine which runs daily searching for open task that has past due dates. When a past due task is found, an email notification is sent to the supervisor informing about the pending task. The supervisor can take action by either reassigning to another custom officer or let is remain as it. ## Process Steps Business Rules Refer the “System Admin CBP” excel template for business rules title: SRS_eCMS_Application_ACT_Exemption_V_1.0_Finalized
content:
[TRADER] SRS_eCMS_Application_ACT_Exemption_V_1.0_Finalized

## General Release No 1.0 – Sep 2021 ## Endorsement by System Owner (internal) release history ## Table of Contents Table of Contents 3 ## Introduction 4 A. Definitions and Abbreviations 4 ## B. References 6 1. Functional Requirements 7 1.1 Authorized Complaint Trader (ACT) 7 1.1.1 Pre-Requisites 7 1.1.2 Process Flow for Authorized Compliant Trader 7 1.1.3 Use Case Diagram for Authorized Compliant Trader 8 1.1.4 Business Validation 10 1.2 Import Duty Exemption 11 1.2.1 Pre-Requisites 12 1.2.2 Process Flow for Import Duty Exemption 12 1.2.3 Use Case Diagram for Import Duty Exemption 13 1.2.4 Business Validation 15 1.3 Duty Free Quota 16 1.3.1 Pre-Requisites 16 1.3.2 Process flow for Duty Free Quota 16 1.3.3 Use Case Diagram for Duty Free Quota 17 1.3.4 Business Validation 19 ## Appendix A 23 1. Configuration blueprint (CBP) 23 2. Types of Exemption 23 3. Annual duty free quota limits 24 4. Exemption Print 25 5. Backend Jobs 25 6. Exemption Approval Matrix 26 ## Introduction This document defines & illustrates the business requirements, process flows as well as the detailed functional requirements of eCMS Application module (Authorized Compliant Trader and Exemption) to be implemented for Department of Revenue and Customs, Bhutan. ## Definitions and Abbreviations The table below lists the different acronyms and abbreviations as well as the definitions used throughout this SRS. ## References The creation of the BECMS SRS was referenced using the following documents: ## FUNCATIONAL REQUIREMENT SPECIFICATION.docx TECHNICAL REQUIREMENT SPECIFICATION.docx ## Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-3.pdf Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-4.pdf ## Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-5A.pdf Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-5B.pdf ## Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-6A.pdf Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-6B.pdf ## Functional Requirements Authorized Complaint Trader (ACT) An external user can apply for Authorized Compliant Trader (ACT) in eCMS. ACT are accorded certain procedural advantages in eCMS which result in a quicker and smoother clearance. The below section details out the process of applying for an ACT in eCMS. ## Pre-Requisites Trader should have a valid TPN which is available in eCMS PIN Master through BITS integration. Trader has a history of compliance which can be validated against BITS provided information in PIN master. Company admin has access to eCMS ACT application functionality. ## Process Flow for Authorized Compliant Trader Process ID: 01.01 – Authorized Compliant Trader ## Use Case Diagram for Authorized Compliant Trader Additional Functionality ## Business Validation Import Duty Exemption An external registered user can apply for import duty exemption in eCMS after logging into eCMS. Exemptions can be applied for specific items and for a specific reason (for example, for setting up a Manufacturing unit etc). Approved exemptions can be referred while declaring consignments and system will accordingly exmpt applicable Customs duties and charges. The below section details out the process of applying for an Exemption for import duty in eCMS. Overall, Exemption will be structured as follows. Each exemption will be uniquely identified by the TPN of the Importer. Each exemption will be structured as below, and applicant will need to select at the point of submission of the application: Exemption Type (Ex: Vehicle) – Applicant will need to select an Exemption type from a configured list of Exemption types. Only one Exemption type can be specified for an application. Exemption Issued for (For ex: Armed Forces) – Applicant will need to select an “Exemption Issued for” from the configured list of “Exemption Issued for” under each “Exemption Type.” Only one Exemption issued for can be specified for an application. Exemption Category (Ex: Vehicle Quota) - Applicant will need to select an “Exemption Category” from the configured list of “Exemption Category” under each “Exemption Issued for.”. Only one Exemption Category can be specified for an application. In addition, an additional Exemption type named “Refund Exemption” shall be provided. This will be applied by the Applicant for Exemption after the Declaration has been cleared from Customs. In this case, the Applicant for Refund Exemption will be required to key in the Declaration number along with the TPN of the Importer. After verification of provided Declaration and Importer TPN, the applicant shall provide the Invoice and item details like any other Exemption. Post approval from Customs, the importer can apply for refund using the approved Refund exemption. Based on the specified Exemption type, issued for and Category, system will fetch the configured exempted tax type which may be any combination of existing tax types of namely CDR, GT, EET and GST. The ceiling on the value for the combination of Exemption type, issued for and category will be configured in Rules files. In case if the Ceiling on the value is not specified in Rules, then the verifier will need to manually provide the exempted Value or Quantity during review. If the ceiling is specified in the rules, then system will default the exempted value to the ceiling. Each exemption type will have an approval matrix (Configurable in the System) which will determine the required approvals for the exemption type and will be configured in the Rules file. For instance, certain Exemption type may require approval from RRCO followed by approval from Head office. If no rules are configured, then it will be routed by default to Head office (Verifier followed by Assesor). The SRS currently covers the default flow, but it is understood that the implementation will handle the configured routing. An approved exemption which has not been consumed in a declaration and nearing expiry can be extended. Applicant will need to apply for renewal. Exemption certificate can be printed by the Importer and Customs after final approval. (Details of current Exemption types and Exemption certificate print is provided in the appendix section) ## Pre-Requisites TPN of the Trader should be active and available in eCMS PIN Master through BITS integration. In case Trader does not have a TPN, they will either need to apply in BITS or use Fast TPN Link in eCMS. incase of CFA applying for an importer without a TPN, the TPN for the importer can be registered by the CFA by using the fast-track interface. Exemption will be based on TPN, and this will used to link and validate an exemption when it is applied in a declaration. Trader has required supporting document like item list, invoice information etc. Company admin has access to eCMS Import duty exemption application functionality. ## Process Flow for Import Duty Exemption Process ID: 01.02 – Import Duty Exemption It is either the Head office or the RRCO verifying as well approving the exemption. However, some of the exemption processes are decentralised. Eg. Exemption for raw materials is verified, approved, and issued by the RRCO and exemption for plant and machinery are verified, approved, and issued by the head office. ## Use Case Diagram for Import Duty Exemption Additional Functionalities ## Business Validation Duty Free Quota An external user can apply for Duty-Free Quota in eCMS. The application will be made available in the public portal and will not require the user to login to eCMS. The below section details out the process of applying for a Duty-Free Quota in eCMS. ## Overall, Duty Free Quota will be structured as follows: Applicant will provide ID number and TPN Number. ID Number will be CID in case of Bhutanese national and Passport number/ work permit no in case of non-Bhutanese. TPN number should be available in eCMS PIN Master through BITS integration and will be validated. System will maintain a list of available Privileged members along with quota value in USD. During verification, Customs verifier will indicate the privileged member (only one per application). During verification, Customs will be able to verify all the details including configured quota value but cannot change the value. (Details of privileged members and quota values in USD are provided in the appendix ) ## Pre-Requisites Applicant should be eligible for duty free quota. Bhutanese applicant should have a valid TPN. ## Foreigners applying for quota should have a valid stay and TPN Foreign applicant should have a valid work permit number. ## Process flow for Duty Free Quota Process ID: 01.03 – Duty Free Quota ## Use Case Diagram for Duty Free Quota Additional Functionalities ## Business Validation CFA Authorization A Trader will need to authorize a CFA to act on its behalf and transact in eCMS as its representative. For this, the Trader will need to apply from the Portal (outside Login) and indicate the CFA to be authorized. Upon submission, the application shall be reviewed and approved by a Verifier at the Customs Head office. Post approval from Customs, the CFA can act on behalf of the Trader and submit declarations and other trade related documents in the System. The below section details out the process of CFA Authorization. ## Pre-Requisites Trader should have a valid TPN which is available in eCMS PIN Master through BITS integration. CFA should be registered in eCMS as a CFA Operator (Please refer to Registration SRS for detailed steps) Customs Verifier at Head office has access to eCMS. ## Process Flow for CFA Authorization Process ID: 01.04 – CFA Authorization ## Use Case Diagram for CFA Authorization Additional Functionality ## Business Validation Appendix A ## Configuration blueprint (CBP) Configuration Blueprint (CBP) for ACT and Exemption ## Types of Exemption Additionally, Exemption Type “Refund Exemption” shall also be included ## Annual duty free quota limits Exemption Print ## Backend Jobs System will check through a batch job for any updates done to PIN Master by BITS and update the ACT Status if needed for effected TPN’s. ## Exemption Approval Matrix Below is the Exemption approval matrix for different types of Import Exemption. Approval matrix for Goods and commodities need to be finalized. Approval matrix can be configured in the System using Rule File. Customs Office RTO | Regional Trade Office RAMIS | Revenue Administration Management Information System SAARC | South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation SITA | International Aeronautical Telecommunications Society SCTS | Single Customs Trade System SAD | Single Administration Document TPN | Taxpayer Number UPU | Universal Postal Union [TABLE] Process Steps P01: Submit Application A user will prepare an application for ACT after logging into eCMS. Before submission of the Application, eCMS will validate the provided TPN in PIN Master. Following are the steps for validation of TPN. System will retrieve the details from eCMS PIN Master. If the TPN keyed in is valid then System will fetch the related TPN details and display in the application. In case of importer most of the data will be prepopulated based on login TPN. If the TPN is found and valid, then the application will be accepted for submission and the application shall be taken up for review by DRC and for certification as an ACT (Authorized Compliant Trader). A unique reference no will be generated once the application is submitted and the same can be used by the applicant to track the status of the application. Application status can be checked through the Portal as well (Outside the login). P02: Verify Application System will assign the application to the work queue of a Verifer at the Customs head office on a round-roobin basis using Resource allocation module. The verifier will verify the applicant details and determine the validity of the application. The verifier based on the review will either recommend, reject, or revert for amendment. In case of an incomplete application, the applicant must be notified that they must furnish the correct documents within thirty (30) days. The number of days should be configurable. P03: Notify Applicant of Rejection During verification, if the verifier concludes that the application is invalid for any reason, then the Verifier will provide reasons for rejection and reject the application. The applicant shall be notified of the rejection including the reason for rejection by email. The status of the application should be rejected. If the application is reverted back for amendment, then the status of the application should be re-submit. P04: Check ACT Criteria (Assessor) If the application has been recommended for ACT by the verifier, System will assign the application to the work queue of an Assessor at the Customs head office on a round-roobin basis using Resouce allocation module. Assessor will check recommended application detail and determine if it qualifies for ACT. If the assessor determines that the application needs to be rejected for any reason, then the assessor will reject the application and provide reasons for rejection. eCMS will notify the applicant of the rejection (please refer P03). the status of the same will be rejected. P05: Certify Trader During assessment, if the Assesor concludes that the provided documents and related details are in order, then the Assessor can approve the application for ACT certification. In this case, System will certify the applicant as an ACT in eCMS. Applicable fees are configured in the System, and, if any fees are configured, System will apply fees and route for payment. Note: Fees will be defined in the Rules files, however we have catered payment process flow, if fees are applied. P06: Send Confirmation Post registration, System will notify the applicant on the successful certification as an Authorized Compliant Trader (ACT). P07: Generate Payment advice Post approval and registration, system will determine if fees are applicable based on configuration. If no fees are applicable, system will allow printing of certificate of registration. If fees are applicable, a payment advice shall be generated and sent to Revenue. Registration certificate printing and ACT certification shall be withheld till all payments are completed. P08: Send to Revenue System eCMS will integrate with Revenue system and send the payment advice generated in previous step. P09: Receive payment confirmation from Revenue System Revenue system will send a payment confirmation to eCMS after collecting payment in Revenue system. After receipt of collection message, eCMS will enable printing of “Authorized Compliant Registration certificate” and ACT certification will be restored. [TABLE] S/N | Additional Functionality 1. | Customs can suspend an ACT at any time if any serious irregularalities are detected. In this case, a notification shall be sent to the ACT after suspension. 2. | Customs can withdraw the suspension, and, in this case, ACT shall be activated. 3. | Customs could revoke an authorization in case if the trader did some very serious offence. In this case, the holder cannot re-apply for ACT for a period of three (3) years (configurable). A notification shall be sent to the ACT after revocation. [TABLE] S/N | Validation Rules 1. | Trader applying for ACT should be complying as per BITS. 2. | At given time, only one ACT application can be submitted per Trader (No duplicate submission) 3. | In case applicant is required to submit additional documents during ACT Review, the applicant will need to submit requested additional documents by Customs verifying officer within thirty (30) days. 4. | Rejected Application cannot be amended and re-submitted. [TABLE] Process Steps P01: Submit Application An external user will login to eCMS and prepare an application for Import Exemption. In case of a CFA applying exemption on behalf of the importer, User shall provide the TPN number of the Importer. System will retrieve the details from eCMS PIN Master and load the data for CFA based on entered TPN. In case of importer most the data will be prepopulated based on login TPN. However, If the TPN cannot be validated and is not registered with eCMS PIN Master, the system should provide a link for fast-track TPN registration in BITS. User will provide required mandatory information for getting an exemption and submit. The following information but not limited to shall be captured in the item tab: The HS Code of the item along with details like invoice Value, Quantity, Country of Origin (COO) etc. In case of Refund Exemption, the applicant will additionally need to provide the Customs cleared Declaration and Importer TPN. Upon submission, System will generate an application number. Application can be to. Renewed (If the exemption has not been used in a declaration) Expiry date only. Cancel (If the exemption has not been used in a declaration) New (In case of a Refund Exemption, renew is not applicable) A unique reference no will be generated once the application is submitted and the same can be used by the applicant to track the status of the application. P02: Verify Application When the exemption application has been submitted, System will route the application for review to the work queue of the Verifier in a round-robin basis using the Resource allocation module and based on the configured approval matrix. The Verifier will verify the applicant details and determine the validity of the application. The verifier based on the review will either recommend, reject, or revert for amendment. The status of the application shall reflect the action taken by the verifier. For each item, the verifier will mark the field on which exemption will be provided as provided below. Value, Quantity The system should be able to generate and issue exemption base on either value or quanity. (Note: In case if ceiling value is configured for the provided Exemption type, system will default the value to the configured ceiling.) Based on this field, the exemption will be tracked in the declaration when items are declared. P03: Notify Applicant of Rejection During verification, if the verifier concludes that the application is invalid for any reason, then the Verifier will provide reasons for rejection and reject the application. The applicant shall be notified of the rejection including the reason for rejection by email. Amendment: if the documents submitted are incomplete or the application needs further amendment, the same will be revereted back to the applicant for amendment The status of the application will be as per the action taken by the verifier. P04: Approve Application If the exemption has been verified and recommended by the verifier, System will route the application for review to the work queue of an Assessor at the Customs Head Office on a round-robin basis using the Resouce allocation module and based on configured approval matrix. Assessor will check recommended application detail and determine if it can be approved. If the assessor determines that the application needs to be rejected for any reason, then the assessor will reject the application and provide reasons for rejection. eCMS will notify the applicant of the rejection (please refer P03). The application can be reverted to the verifier for further review too by the assessor. If the application is approved, the applicant must be issued an Import Duty Exemption Certificate (IDEC), which must be allocated a unique system generated reference number and will be valid for one (1) year. In case where an exemption has been granted to a business, which is upgraded to a company and assigned a new TPN, the IDEC will no longer be valid. Essentially, system must ensure that the TPN for which the IDEC was approved is also the TPN which is using the IDEC to import goods. Note: To claim Customs duty exemption, the importer must include the IDEC No. at Header level of the import declaration (Exemptions of the type “Refund Exemptions” cannot be linked during Declaration submission). There should be no need to attach the certificate itself, as it must be linked within the eCMS. P05: Send Confirmation System will notify the applicant on the approval of the Exemption request. System to allow applicant to print the exemption from the system. [TABLE] S/N | Additional Functionality 1. | System will provide an option for Customs to search exemption details by clicking search menu and entering following details: Application Number, TPN to view individual exemption. 2 | System will alert the importer as well as customs if before the validity of the exemption expires [TABLE] S/N | Validation Rules 1. | Total invoice value and total value of items under that invoice should match. 2. | Rejected Application cannot be amended and re-submitted. 3. | Expired exemption cannot be used during declaration 4 | Refund Exemptions cannot be used in a Declaration directly unlike other Exemptions. 5 | Only Customs cleared Declaration can be used for Refund Exemption 6 | For Refund Exemption, only one Declaration can be linked to an application, 7 | Refund Exemption can be applied multiple time for a Declaration and System will validate that exempted Item quantity is not beyond the Declared quantity. Example, Declaration has 1000 quantity submitted by Importer for 2 parties. Exempted parties can split the quantities say 500 and 500. 8 | The Importer of the Declaration and the Applicant applying Refund Exemption cannot be the same. 9 | Refund Exemptions cannot be renewed. [TABLE] Process Steps P01: Submit Application An external user will prepare an application for Duty free quota outside the eCMS login. For Bhutanese nationals: The system shall allow the applicant to key in CID. If the applicant keys in the CID, the same should hit the eCMS PIN Master, and list all the TPN registered against the CID. For the selected TPN, System will fetch the related TPN details and display in the application. For duty free quota, only individual shall be allowed (No Business or Company TPN) However, If the TPN cannot be validated and is not registered with eCMS, system will provide a link to the SSP (Self Service Portal) registration in BITS to apply for TPN registration in eCMS. For Other nationals: Non-Bhutanese must provide a valid work permit and TPN, TPN verification shall be applicable and eCMS will validate the TPN with eCMS PIN Master. In case TPN cannot be validated and is not registered with eCMS, system will provide a link for the SSP in BITS to apply for TPN registration in eCMS. Applicant shall provide mandatory information for getting a duty-free quota and submit. Duty free quota is provided on value which shall be specified by the approving officers and not by the applicant. For foreign nationals, start date and end date of tenure should be provided. eCMS will generate an application number when the application is submitted by the applicant. Application can be to. Renew New cancellation P02: Verify Application When the duty-free quota application has been submitted, System will route the application for review to the work queue of a Verifier at the Head Office on a round-robin basis using the Resouce allocation module. The verifier based on the review outcomes will either recommend, reject, or revert for amendment. P03: Notify Applicant of Rejection During verification, if the verifier concludes that the application is invalid for any reason, then the Verifier will provide reasons for rejection and reject the application. The applicant shall be notified of the rejection including the reason for rejection by email. Amendment: if the documents submitted are incomplete or the applicant need further amendment, the same will be revereted back to the applicant for amendment by email P04: Approve Application If the Duty-Free Quota has been verified and recommended by the verifier, System will route the application to the work queue of an Assessor at the Customs Head Office on a round-robin basis using the Resouce allocation module. Assessor will check recommended application detail and determine if it can be approved. If the assessor determines that the application needs to be rejected for any reason, then the assessor will reject the application and provide reasons for rejection. eCMS will notify the applicant of the rejection (please refer P03) If the application is approved, System must genetrate an approval letter with a unique system generated Quota number which shall be valid till 31st Dec of the approval year based on date of approval. Note: Quota will not be carry forwarded to next year, unused quota will be forfeited by 31st Dec. Once the quota validity is over, it cannot be used further, and balance quota shall be forfeited and cannot be carried forward. Duty free stores will submit the declaration in eCMS for claiming the duty exemption. P05: Send Confirmation System will notify the applicant on the approval of the Duty-Free Quota request and include the Quota details as well. The quota details shall be communicating with the applicant via email and the duty-free store who is issuancingof duty-free card. No prints are required for quota from eCMS as this will be provided by the Duty-free stores. [TABLE] S/N | Additional Functionality System will allow renewal of duty-free quota. Applicant will need to visit the Application portal and key in the Quota number along with the TPN provided at the time of submitting the application. System will allow the user to update the existing application and submit for renewal. Application renewal will follow similar process as new application. Post renewal, a new Quota number will be generated. Customs can cancel the Duty-Free quota any time [TABLE] S/N | Validation Rules 1. | Only one application per applicant can be submitted (No duplicate) 2. | Rejected Application cannot be amended and re-submitted. [TABLE] Process Steps P01: Submit Application Trader will provide CID/TPN, and System will check for a valid CID and TPN through the following steps. The system will allow the applicant to key in CID as well as TPN. . The system will validate the kyed in CID and the TPN and accordingly allow the applicant to process further. In case of a business, the system will allow to key in the business licnese no and the TPN. If the TPN belongs to a Company, then the Applicant will be required to provide the Company registration number for authentication, the system will validate the keyed in TPN and the company registration number and accordingly allow the applcinat to proceed to fetch the TPN details and display in the Application. If the keyed in details is validated then System will fetch the related TPN details and display in the application (in case the TPN belongs to a Company, then system will follow authentication using Company registration number as mentioned in Step 2 before displaying TPN details). After providing a valid TPN, Trader shall indicate the CFA which needs to be authorized from a list of registered and active CFA’s in eCMS and proceed to submit the application for authorizing the selected CFA. Only one CFA per application can be indicated. The system will also allow the applicant to select the start date and end date. ( validity of the authorization) Application can be for: Create new Authorization Cancel existing Authorization A unique reference no will be generated once the application is submitted and the same can be used by the applicant to track the status of the application. P02: Review Application System will assign the application to the work queue of a Verifer at the Customs head office on a round-roobin basis using Resource allocation module. The verifier will verify the applicant details and determine the validity of the application. The verifier based on the review will either approve or reject the application. P03: Notify Applicant of Rejection During verification, if the verifier concludes that the application is invalid for any reason, then the Verifier will provide reasons for rejection and reject the application. The applicant shall be notified of the rejection including the reason for rejection by email. The status of the application should be rejected. P04: Approve Authorization During verification, if the Verifier concludes that the provided details are in order, then the Verifier can approve the Authorization. In this case, System will authorize the CFA to act on behalf of the Trader. After approval, System will send a notification to the Trader and the CFA. P05: Submit Documents on behalf of Trader After approval and receipt of notification, the following actions are possible In case of new Authorization, CFA can submit Declaration and other Trade related Documents in eCMS. System will present a list of authorized TPN’s for the CFA to choose from while creating a transaction in the System on behalf of the Trader. In case of Cancellation of existing Authorization, the CFA cannot select the TPN and cannot submit for the Trader. [TABLE] S/N | Additional Functionality N/A [TABLE] S/N | Validation Rules 1. | Trader can apply only one authorization for one CFA at one time. However, trader can submit multiple authorization but for different CFA at the same time. 2. | Rejected Application cannot be amended and re-submitted. 3. | If a CFA is already authorized for a Trader, the trader cannot submit another authorization for the same CFA. 4. | If during Customs review and, in the meantime, if the CFA is not active in the System for any reason, then System will not allow the approval to go through and Customs Verifier will need to reject the application. 5 | Cancellation can be applied only if the CFA is previously authorized by the Trader.
