Interface Requirements 30 2.1 Inspection Management 30 2.2 Release 31 2.3 Inter gateway Movement 32 3. Appendix 33 3.1 Scheduler Jobs 33 3.2 Configuration Parameter 33 3.3 Configuration blueprint (CBP) 33 ## Introduction This document defines & illustrates the business requirements, process flows as well as the detailed functional requirements of eCMS Clearance modules to be implemented for Department of Revenue and Customs, Bhutan. Clearance modules includes below processes. ## Inspection Documentary check ## Physical examination Release ## Inter gateway movement (transit) Definitions and Abbreviations The table below lists the different acronyms and abbreviations as well as the definitions used throughout this SRS. ## References The creation of the BECMS SRS was referenced using the following documents: ## FUNCATIONAL REQUIREMENT SPECIFICATION.docx TECHNICAL REQUIREMENT SPECIFICATION.docx ## Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-3.pdf Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-4.pdf ## Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-5A.pdf Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-5B.pdf ## Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-6A.pdf Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-6B.pdf ## Functional Requirements Inspection Management ## Overview Customs uses the Inspection Management module to update the Documentary check and physical examination details of a cargo in the system. Inspection process is involved in all the Regime flows. ## Documentary Check Description Document Check: Document check is required if the declaration assessed with yellow lane in the risk assessment module. The customs document verification officer verifies the document and update the status of verification in the system. ## Pre-Requisite Document Check: The Customs Officer has the right to access the eCMS application to the document verification module. The cargo must be routed for document verification. ## Process Flow Inbound – Document Check Process Flow Outbound – Document Check ## Process Step Business Rule ## Business Validation Physical Inspection ## Description Physical Examination: The Customs Officer examines the cargo and update the physical examination results and status in the eCMS System. ## Pre-Requisite Physical Examination: The Customs Officer has the right to access the eCMS application to the physical examination. The cargo must be routed for physical examination. ## Process flow Process Flow Inbound – Physical Examination ## Process Flow Outbound – Physical Examination Process Step ## Business Rule Business Validation ## Use Cases Release ## Description The Release Management module is one of the core clearance process and it is primarily used by Customs to release cargo during the clearance process. The Release Management module is accessed primarily by Customs to check and release the cargo and update the status. The system provides the facility to the customs officer/declarant to print the Release order after updating the status. Release process is involved in all Regime flows. ## Scope The scope of this System Requirements Specification (SRS) is: ## Release Order Release Cargo ## Process Flow Release Order and Release Cargo ## Description Release Order: Release order is a logical release of the cargo after the compliance process. The Cargo Transporter requires the release order from customs to physically transport the cargo. The cargo Gate officer can verify the Release order and update the cargo release status after physical release. Release Cargo: The gate officer verifies the Release order and physically releases the cargo by updating the status to confirm Cargo Release. The gate officer may release the cargo as and when the compliance process completes, provided there is a release order issued. After all the cargo has been released for the declaration the release officer needs to update the “Release Completed” status. Note: In case of the change in vehicle number, system will provide an option to update vehicle number in the declaration by declarant. ## Pre-Requisites Release Order: All necessary compliance process is completed. Release Cargo: The release order has been issued for the declaration. ## Process Steps Business Validations ## Use Cases Inter Gateway Movement (Transit) ## Description The Inter Gateway Movement module is one of the core clearance process and is primarily used by the Customs Gate Officer in entry and exit port for verifying the cargo release order and goods in transit by facilitating its movement from the entry port to the exit port. ## Inter Gateway Movement refers to the tracking and movement of transit cargo from the entry port to the exit port within the frontiers of the country en-route to the destination country/port.. The Customs Gate Officer at the exit port verifies the cargo release order, applies the seal and then, once confirmed, allows the cargo to leave the exit port in transit to the port of entry. At the entry port, the gate officer verifies the seal and the release order and releases the cargo. Optionally, the Customs Officer verify & does the physical examination of the cargo on a need basis at the port of entry and updates the system with the examination result and confirmation of the arrival of goods at the final destination. ## Scope The Inter Gateway Movement module in eCMS covers the following functions: ## Port of Exit Release Port of Entry Release ## Process Flow Port of Exit and Port of Entry ## Description Port of Exit: The Customs Gate Officer checks the cargo information and confirms the cargo release by updating the status as released in CMS. Port of Entry : The Customs Gate Officer checks the cargo information and confirms the cargo arrival by updating the status as “Arrived” in CMS. The Customs Gate Officer records the cargo details and then optionally sends it inspection, if required. The declaration status is updated subsequently. ## Pre-Requisites Port of Exit: A transit declaration should be submitted and has undergone compliance process. The cargo is released by the Customs Gate Officer from the Release Management module. Port of Entry: The declaration status should be “Transit in Progress”. ## Process Steps Business Validations ## Use Cases Interface Requirements ## Inspection Management Below diagram illustrates the interfaces integrated between Inspection module and other modules. ## Inspection functions as Service Consumer: Release ## Below diagram illustrates the interfaces integrated between release module and other modules. ## Release functions as Service Consumer: Inter gateway Movement ## Below diagram illustrates the interfaces integrated between Inter-gateway module and other modules. ## Inter-gateway functions as Service Consumer: Appendix ## Scheduler Jobs Note: This backend system job will check the declarations that have been released from the Port of Entry but have not been received in the Port of Exit within the specified configurable timeframe based on transit route. The timeframe is pre-defined in the transit route maintenance. Those declarations will be flagged out and notifications will be sent to the Customs Officer for intervention. ## Configuration Parameter Inspection Report We will implement this in XLS format and allow inspection officer to upload in the system as attachment document. ## Configuration blueprint (CBP) Configuration Blueprint (CBP) for Inspection, Release and Inter gateway. declaration to Document check if the lane is selected as “Yellow” P02: Cargo Gate-In (only for Outbound Declarations) The Gate in Officer creates the gate pass by inputting the vehicle information. P02: Document Verification Document Verifier verifies the cargo against declared details which are routed to document check process. The customs officer might ask for additional information via email to process the declaration. Note: Officer can upload the supporting document while completing the document check. P03: Update Document Check Status and Release The officer updates the overall document check status of the declaration. If the officer suspects the cargo to be physically verified, then mark the status of the document check completed with required physical examination. Else the cargo proceeds to the gate for final release. If the declaration needs to be amended by trader, then the officer should update the overall document status as “Document check failed” with further action as “Amendment”. If the declaration to be routed to offence, then the officer should update the overall document status as “Document check failed” with further action as “Offence”. The Officer can view all the comments made by all the officers in the upstream process by viewing the declaration “Other Details” tab. P04: Duty & Tax Re-assessment If the declaration is under-valued by the valuation process, after the examination is completed, then the system will re-assess the duties and taxes. P05: Additional Payment System creates the additional payment instruction for Declaration to do the payment and clear the consignment. Note: Payment details will be sent to BITS system for the collection. [TABLE] PROCESS | BUSINESS RULE Document inspection | Based on the risk assessment, a declaration might be directed to yellow lane, where documents will be verified The customs officer might ask for additional documents to review and verify the declaration via email After verification for additional documents the declaration might be directed to; 1. release 2. send back for amendment 3. re-assessment (If increase in valuation during valuation process) 4. red lane [TABLE] PROCESS | BUSINESS VALIDATION Document inspection | The Document verification Officer can only view and process the current declarations that are routed for documentary check and assigned to him/her. The system will provide an option for the customs to attach/upload additional documents received from the declarant. [TABLE] Process Steps P01: Initiate Inspection System will route the declaration to Document check if the lane is selected as “Yellow” or physical examination if the lane is selected as “red” in risk assessment P02: Cargo Gate-In (only for Outbound Declarations) The Gate in Officer creates the gate pass by inputting the vehicle information. P02: Document Verification Document Verifier verifies the cargo against declared details which are routed to document check process. Note: Officer can upload the supporting document while completing the document check. P03: Update Document Check Status and Release The officer updates the overall document check status of the declaration. If the officer suspects the cargo to be physically verified, then mark the status of the document check completed with required physical examination. Else the cargo proceeds to the gate for final release. If the declaration needs to be amended by trader, then the officer should update the overall document status as “Document check failed” with further action as “Amendment”. If the declaration to be routed to offence, then the officer should update the overall document status as “Document check failed” with further action as “Offence”. The Officer can view all the comments made by all the officers in the upstream process by viewing the declaration “Other Details” tab. P04: Physical Inspection The cargo enters examination area if the Lane is Red. For Yellow Lane, the Document verification Officer routes the declaration to examination by updating the document status to the “Physical examination required”. Officer can view the document verification status, details and the remarks from previous compliance processes. Note: Officer can upload the supporting document while completing the physical examination. P04.1 & P04.2: Update Examination Status and Release Cargo The Examination Officer updates the examination result and enters remarks. If there are discrepancies with the declaration, the Examination Officer routes the declaration based on the outcome. The following are the possible outcomes: If the declaration is non-suspect, it will be routed for release in case of “normal examination”. If the declaration is suspect and a change in HS-Code/Tariff/Quantity etc. is required, then the Examination Officer informs the declarant on the changes required. If the Declarant agrees to this, Examination Officer routes the declaration for Amendmentor route the declaration to offence management. (Case by case basis). If the Declarant does not agree to the changes, Officer updates the status and refers the case to “Offence Management”. Offence management team will follow-up on the declaration. Note: XLS Inspection report option will be provided officer to upload the inspection outcome and the report format was included in the Appendix. P05: Duty & Tax Re-assessment If the declaration is under-valued by the valuation process, after the examination is completed, then the system will re-assess the duties and taxes. P06: Additional Payment System creates the additional payment instruction for Declaration to do the payment and clear the consignment. Note : Payment details will be sent to BITS system for the collection. [TABLE] PROCESS | BUSINESS RULE Physical Inspection | Based on the risk assessment, a declaration might be directed to Red lane, where the consignment will be physically inspected Based on the inspection report, the declaration might be directed to; 1. release 2. send back for amendment 3. re-assessment [TABLE] PROCESS | BUSINESS VALIDATION Physical Inspection | The inspection Officer can only view and process the current declarations that are routed for Physical inspection and assigned to him/her. The system will provide an option for the customs to record the inspection report which will be standard and incorporated in the system [TABLE] S/N | Validation Rules Physical Examination | Physical Examination 1. | The Examination Officer can only view and process the current declarations that are routed for Examination and assigned to him/her. [TABLE] Process Steps P01: Release Order by System System will update the status of declaration as release order completed as soon as the declaration is available for release. The cargo release order number is generated by the system. Release order can be created by system when below scenarios encountered. After completion of risk for green lane declarations After completion of inspection for yellow/red lane declarations ACT TPN declarations will be considered as blue lane and directly routed to release. P02: Receive the Release Order Once the compliance process completed, release order will be available for the declarant. The printing of the release order is an optional process. The release officer prints the Release Order and passes it to the Cargo Transporter. P03: Verify the Release Order The gate officer verifies the release order upon arrival of the cargo at the gate. Gate Officers access the declaration to be released and cross verify the consignment details. Only the consignment that cleared the compliance process will be eligible for release. P04: Update Release details. The gate officer releases the cargo and updates cargo status as “Release Cargo Completed”. After “Confirm Release”, declaration status will get changed according to the regime. Warehouse: Pending warehouse admission Ex-warehouse (import): Pending warehouse release Import/Export: Cleared Transit: Gate Released [TABLE] S/N | Validation Rules Release Order | Release Order 1. | The “Release Order” is a logical release and the list of customs cleared declaration along with the transshipped vehicle no will be reflected in the gate out officer’s dashboard Release Cargo | Release Cargo 1. | The system will support the release cargo based on declaration number and transshipped vehicle no Note : System will allow to search and release using declaration number or vehicle number. [TABLE] Process Steps P01: Record Cargo Seal and Truck Numbers The Customs Gate Officer at the exit port cross-checks the cargo information with the release information from the system. Officer applies the seal on the container/cargo and records the cargo seal number in the system along with the truck numbers P02: Release Cargo Gate Officer releases the cargo and updates the transit status as Released. P03: Status Updated System updates the status as Cargo released from exit port. P04: Verify Cargo Information The Customs Gate Officer at the entry port cross-checks the information of the cargo that arrived with the Port of Exit information from the system. The Customs Gate Officer verifies the cargo seal and truck numbers etc. P05: Update the Cargo Release status Officer updates the status of cargo with below statuses. Received: Officer receives the cargo and updates the transit status as “Received”. Transit Port of Entry Inspection: If suspicious, Officer may send the cargo for inspection. The declaration is redirected to the Inspection department for physical examination of the cargo. Until the examination is successfully completed the declaration cannot be released in the Port of Exit. P06: Status Updated System updates the status as Cargo cleared from entry port. Gate officer should only be able to input seal number details/remarks. 2. | There should be configurable transit route pre-selected by the declarant in the declaration. Each transit route will have estimated travel time and based on this the system will notify customs if the means of transport has not arrived at the exit port. Port of Entry | Port of Entry 3. | The inspection routing should be ad-hoc and will be decided at the port of entry. Risk | Inspection | To get the Lane details of a declaration to be inspected. Code Maintenance | Inspection | Retrieve the Customs Office details by the Customs Office code. Inter Gateway | Inspection | Update the physical examination results of the declaration requested in the Port of Exit. Enforcement/ Offence | Inspection | To send declaration details to enforcement to create offence report Valuation | Inspection | Retrieve the valuation details for duty re-assessment [TABLE] Service Provider | Service Consumer | Service Description Code Maintenance | Release | Retrieve the Customs Office details by the Customs Office code. Declaration | Release | To retrieve the declaration details, Containerized and Non-Containerized cargos. Update the status of the declaration. Duties and Taxes | Release | Compute additional duties and taxes based on valuation outcome. Corresponding payment instruction will be created. Declaration | Inter-gateway | Retrieve the declaration details Inspection | Inter-gateway | To trigger the physical examination procedure at Port of Exit. Transit Route | The various possible predefined routes from a port of entry to a port of exit. Transit Route Period | The criteria parameter for the backend job is the “Transit Route Period”. This field can be configured in the Transit Route code table of Code Maintenance module.

The declaration submission is done by Declarants in ECMS and, post submission, the processing of the declaration will be done in eCMS. ## Scope The scope of the Declaration implemented in ECMS covers the following: ## Customs Declaration Preparation Customs Declaration Submission ## Declaration Validation Post Entries / Declaration Amendment Post Clearance Entry / Declaration amendment after release. ## Cancellation Request Bonded Warehouse admission and release ## Definitions and Abbreviations The table below lists the different acronyms and abbreviations as well as the definitions used throughout this SRS. ## References The creation of the Declaration submission SRS was referenced using the following documents: ## FUNCATIONAL REQUIREMENT SPECIFICATION.docx TECHNICAL REQUIREMENT SPECIFICATION.docx ## Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-3.pdf Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-4.pdf ## Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-5A.pdf Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-5B.pdf ## Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-6A.pdf Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-6B.pdf ## FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS Overview ## The Declaration submission module in eCMS covers the general process of the following regimes: Import ## Export Transit ## Warehouse Temporary Admission/Temporary Export The regime is used as a high level to define the procedure for customs declaration handling. The next level defined is the CPC Group and then the CPC code, the hierarchy is as shown below: Note: For details on CPC configuration, please refer to Tariff SRS. ## Assumptions and Restrictions 1. Declarant has all required supporting documents (like Invoice copies, COO certificate etc) which needs to be attached based on the CPC. 2. Declarant is fully aware of the Bhutan Customs Law and is well versed with various CPC procedures. ## Declaration Fields Declaration Fields The declaration fields in the ECMS are based on the WCO Data Model (v3.2) format. The declaration fields capture all the necessary data required for customs processing. Based on DRC request we have removed some of the WCO data fields to meet Bhutan customs requirement i.e. Item Weight. Based on the CPC Group selected during declaration creation, eCMS will request required fields (i.e. previous declaration number) along with mandatory checks. Additionally, for certain HS Codes, eCMS will request additional information in the item tab viz., strength of alcohol in case the BTC code selected is of the type “Alcohol” or Chassis number and related vehicle information in case the BTC code belongs to a Vehicle. ## Declaration Tariff Configurations VALUATION OF CUSTOMS VALUE Valuation of the goods will be on transaction value. The price inclusion shall be distributed among each cost of items on the invoice using weighted average method. ## For Example: For the above invoice the price inclusion shall be distributed as follows; The custom value should be calculated by distributing the adjusted cost on the FOB as per the weighted average method. ## Customs Duty should be calculated on the Customs Value Green Tax on the Customs Value ## GST on the Customs Value + CD + EET + GT Amount + Any other charges EET on the customs Value. It may arise after an audit, investigation from offense, appeal verdict etc. In this case the declarant will have to raise an amendment in a similar manner. The warehousing process applies to all declarations that are submitted with a warehouse regime and related CPC groups. The warehousing declaration is always followed by an ex-warehouse declaration for removal of the goods from the warehouse. ## WAREHOUSE & EX-WAREHOUSE DECLARATION The process for creation and submission of the Warehouse and Ex-warehouse declaration/s are done by the declarant or importer/exporter. However, admission and release of goods will be done by the bonded Warehouse Operator. ## Warehouse Warehouse declarations are the declarations, created as parent Warehouse declaration to store goods in a Warehouse. The Warehouse declarations are created to admit the goods into a Warehouse. ## Ex-warehouse Ex-warehouse declarations are the declarations, created from the parent warehouse declaration to consume in the country. The Ex-warehouse declaration allows the user to select any CPC group that has warehouse as the precedent CPC. The Ex-warehouse declarations are created for the release of the goods from a Warehouse. All the item quantities in the Ex-warehouse declaration should be less than or equal to items in the parent warehouse declaration. 1 parent warehouse declaration may have many Ex-warehouse declarations. Ex-warehouse can be created using 1 parent warehouse declaration only. Declarant can only reduce the quantity and/or remove the item (in case of part item/quantity removal). No new items can be added in the Ex-warehouse declaration. At least one Warehouse declaration has been released and admitted into a Warehouse to submit Ex-warehouse. The duties and taxes are applicable to Ex-warehouse declarations (same as import). ## WAREHOUSE DECLARATION ADMISSION Description The process of admitting the goods into the Warehouse starts after the Clearance process (i.e., Release Cargo) of the Warehouse declaration. The Warehouse in which the goods/items are stored is mentioned while creating the Warehouse declaration. All items in the declaration must be admitted into one Warehouse only. The admission of the goods will be done upon arrival of the goods into the Warehouse. ## Pre-Requisites The warehouse declaration must be gate released before admitting into warehouse. ## Process The warehouse goods admittance process is implemented as shown below in eCMS: ## Import Export Transit Warehouse Temporary Admission/Export The trader or a clearing agent on behalf of the trader can submit a declaration. In case of a clearing agent submitting a declaration, the clearing agent should be authorized by the Trader in the System. The declarant can add the rest of the information required that is not retrieved from the manifest. 1.3 Create Invoice and item details. The system will auto populate the invoices registered under the manifest submitted if manifest is lodged earlier than the declaration. The system will accordingly auto populate the relevant consignor details registered under the manifest against each invoice. In case where the declaration is lodged earlier than the manifest, the declarant will have to fill in the invoice details. The system will allow the declarant to add multiple invoices under one declaration. the system will calculate the invoice value in BTN if it is other currency by applying the current exchange rate. If applicable, the system will prompt the declarant if the goods are prohibited or restricted, which will be determined by the BTC code entered on each line item, and if there is a need for a license or permit. Duties and taxes will be calculated on the customs value as per section 2.4 of this document. 1.4 Supporting Documents. The system will allow the declarant to attach supporting documents. The declarant will be able to attach all the documents in the check list of documents in addition to other additional documents. The system will allow the system admin to configure additional documents if required. 1.5 Review Declaration The declarant will be able to review the declaration created in a summary before it is submitted for approval. Provisional Declaration number During creation and saving of the declaration, System will generate a provisional declaration number for drafts for future updates. The provisional declaration number will have the below format: The Provisional Declaration Number will have the following format: PROV<YYYY><##########> (Example: PROV20210000003254> where: PROV – Identifier for Provisional YYYY – Year of creation ########## - running sequence number P02: Submit Declaration The user submits the declaration after creating the declaration. But before allowing the declaration to be submitted, the system will validate the declaration as a whole and will display messages if there are errors encountered. If there are no validation issues, the system will submit the declaration with a Pending Approval status and will route the same to a customs officer for approval. The customs officer who will receive the declaration will depend on the Customs Office that the user selected for the declaration. Declaration number Once the declaration is submitted, the system will generate a unique reference no. The declarant will be able track the status of the declaration through the system by using the reference no. The Declaration cannot be amended or updated after the submission. The declarant must submit a post entry amendment or cancellation request to update or cancel the submitted declaration. The submitted declaration will have the following format and will be unique for each Declaration: <YYYY><DEC><##########> (Example: 2021DEC0000003254> where: YYYY – Year of submission DEC – Identifier for Declaration ########## - running sequence number P03: Verify Declaration When a declaration has been submitted by the declarant it must be automatically routed to the work queue of the next available Verifier at the RCCO, on a rotational basis. If the Verifier is not available for any reason, Senior Verifiers must also be able to re-assign work assigned to Verifiers within their team. Verifier will verify the declaration and ascertain that all details are provided correctly. The verifier will have the following options. Accept : In this case, the declaration will be accepted for processing. Reject : In this case, the Declaration shall be rejected. Reject for Amendment: In this case, the Declaration shall be routed back to declarant for amendment and submission. In all cases, declarant/traders shall be notified of the decision of Customs through email. In case of Rejection, reasons for rejection shall be communicated. P04: Reject for Amendment If the declaration submitted is incomplete or the applicant need further amendment, the same will be reverted to the applicant for amendment by email. P05: Reject Declaration During verification, if the verifier concludes that the declaration is invalid for any reason, then the Verifier will provide reasons for rejection and reject the declaration. The applicant shall be notified of the rejection including the reason for rejection by email. P06: Accept Declaration If the verifier approves the declaration, the declaration will be accepted, and the status of the declaration will be approved. The system will communicate the acceptance through mail to the declarant. The following are the actions post acceptance. An acceptance notice shall be generated, and an email notification shall be sent to the Declarant informing on the acceptance. After acceptance, the declaration shall be routed for further Customs processing example risk, valuation, and clearance. The system will calculate the invoice value in BTN if it is other currency by applying the current exchange rate. [TABLE] S.No | Business Validation [TABLE] 1 | Declaration should be submitted and pending payment. Amendment request by declarant is not allowed if the declaration is under Customs core clearance process and, in this case, only Customs can route for amendment. 2 | A single amendment request can be raised against a declaration at one time. 3 | A rejected amendment request cannot be amended any further. 4 | Once an amendment request has been approved another amendment request cannot be requested till the amended declaration has been submitted. The verifier will have the following options. Approve: In this case, the declaration will be opened for amendment. Reject: In this case, the amendment request shall be rejected. No further action is possible. In all cases, the Declarant shall be notified of the approval/rejection through email. P03: Approve for Post Clearance Amendment Upon approval of amendment request, the system shall re-open the cleared declaration for the amendment. This allows the declarant to go back and make the change. P04: Amend and Resubmit Declaration The Declarant makes the changes to the declaration and re-submits the declaration. The amended declaration will go through declaration acceptance. Clearance process will not be applicable and only additional payment (if any) shall be collected as per the existing payment process. The verifier will have the following options. Approve: In this case, the TIER application will be approved, and declarant can use the request to submit a Temporary Import / Export declaration. Reject: In this case, the TIER request shall be rejected. Reject for Amendment: TIER request shall be rejected for amendment and declarant can make required changes and re-submit for review. Appendix 53 4.1 Declaration Clearance Statuses 53 4.2 Payment Invoice Print 54 4.3 Release Order Print 56 ## INTRODUCTION This document defines & illustrates the business requirements, process flows as well as the detailed functional requirements of the declaration processing module in eCMS. The declaration submission is the first step in the eCMS System. After submission, the declaration goes through processing by various department of Customs. This document also illustrates the overall processing of the various regimes supported by eCMS. ## Business Architecture Of eCMS Declaration Processing The overall components of the eCMS Declaration Processing is listed below eCMS Declaration processing Business components ## All the functions in the CMS are categorized into the following: Declaration submission functions ## Core Clearance functions Clearance support functions ## Declaration submission Functions These are module which are involved with the declaration submission and approval process. The key factor in the declaration submission is the various CPC groups and details required for a successful declaration submission and ensuring that system level validations are carried out properly to ensure a valid and well-formed declaration to be submitted in eCMS. ## Core Clearance Process These are modules within the eCMS which are directly involved in the clearance processes. The declaration is the key input for these modules and the focus is on enhancing clearance. The key factor in the core clearance process is the processing & response time, and this is the key design consideration for these modules. The core clearance process relies heavily on system processing minimizing human interventions. ## Clearance Support Functions These are modules which are involved indirectly in the clearance processes. They support the clearance end to end process. They must be seamlessly integrated into the clearance process to ensure the clearance time and processing is not affected. Response time for automated and system tasks, flexibility & feature set for functions requiring customs officers’ input is the key. ## Scope of Declaration Processing The scope of the Declaration processing implemented in eCMS covers the following: ## Regime & CPC Group-wise Declaration process flows Definitions and Abbreviations The table below lists the different acronyms and abbreviations as well as the definitions used throughout this SRS. ## References The creation of the Declaration SRS was referenced using the following documents: ## FUNCATIONAL REQUIREMENT SPECIFICATION.docx TECHNICAL REQUIREMENT SPECIFICATION.docx ## Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-3.pdf Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-4.pdf ## Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-5A.pdf Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-5B.pdf ## Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-6A.pdf Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-6B.pdf ## FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS Overview The Declaration processing module in eCMS shows the overall declaration processing for different regimes and CPC. ## Assumptions and Restrictions The baseline declaration processing module will cover the processes illustrated in subsequent sections. ## Core Processing Steps Description After the Declaration is accepted by customs, the core processing steps is triggered by the system. Upon completion of payment process the system will automatically forward the declaration to the next process If the declaration is not subjected for payment, the system will automatically forward the declaration to the next process the system will also route the additional payment for a declaration to payment process. the additional payment will be linked to a particular declaration. Valuation The system will determine the customs value at item level and accordingly determine whether the declared value is under or over value. The system based on the order of execution (please refer the SRS Valuation) will reflect the system value for items that are either under or overvalued. Review by the Valuation Officer The system will allow the customs officer to decide on valuation based on the finding presented by the system and amend the declared value accordingly. The system will give an option to the valuation officer to direct the declaration to yellow or red channel. Risk Assessment The system will perform the risk assessment based on the risk profile in the system The lane will be decided based on profile criteria met. The possible outcomes are “Green”, “Blue”, “Yellow” or “Red” lanes. “Green” lane will go for release process. “Blue” lane will go for Post clearance audit after release. “Yellow” will go for document verification. “Red” will go for physical inspection. Examination Yellow Channel If the declaration is directed to yellow lane, the declaration will be reflected in the document verifier’s dashboard the system will also provide a platform to the document verifier officer to submit the examination report. The document verification officer may review the documents and decide to release or route for physical inspection or for re-assessment The system will then follow the additional payment process Red Lane If the declaration is directed to red lane, the declaration will be reflected in the inspection’s dashboard Upon physical inspection carried out by the inspection team, the system will also provide a platform to the inspection officer to submit the inspection report that is standard and incorporated in the system. Based on the inspection REPORT, the assessor will either. release the good send back to the declarant for amendment. Direct the declaration to the offences and penalties: Declaration intercepted with customs offence after examination can be routed to Offence and Penalties process by Inspection Officer Blue Lane The system will automatically direct the declaration submitted by ACT to blue lane The system will also provide a feature for the customs to direct a particular declaration to the blue lane. Green Lane The declaration directed to green lane will be released by the customs. Note: The system will provide an option for customs to upgrade the declaration as follows; Green Lane to either yellow or red channel Yellow lane to red channel Reassessment Once the declaration has been directed to offence and penalties, the system will provide an option for the customs to amend the declaration, reassess the additional payment along with the fines and penalties. However, the system will also maintain the original declaration submitted by the declarant Re-assessment by customs can either be Called after completion of Inspection. offence and penalties, wherein customs have intercepted customs offences and the same has been re-assessed as per the examination report. Additional Payment If the declaration has been reassessed, the system will raise a demand notice for the additional payment linking with the declaration. Release Upon completion of the customs procedures the system will generate a release order. The system will allow both the declarant and the customs office to print the release order if need be. During gate out the gate officer will be presented with the release order. Based on which the gate officer will release the cargo and the same will be recorded in the system. Appendix 27 3.1 LOG (Letter of Guarantee) Print 27 ## INTRODUCTION This document defines & illustrates the business requirements, process flows as well as the detailed functional requirements of the Transit declaration processing module in eCMS. The declaration submission is the first step in the eCMS System. After submission, the declaration goes through processing by various department of Customs. This document also illustrates the overall processing of the Transit regime supported by eCMS. ## Scope of Declaration Processing The scope of the Declaration processing implemented in eCMS covers the following: ## Declaration process flows for Transit Regime Definitions and Abbreviations The table below lists the different acronyms and abbreviations as well as the definitions used throughout this SRS. ## References The creation of the Declaration SRS was referenced using the following documents: ## FUNCATIONAL REQUIREMENT SPECIFICATION.docx TECHNICAL REQUIREMENT SPECIFICATION.docx ## Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-3.pdf Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-4.pdf ## Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-5A.pdf Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-5B.pdf ## Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-6A.pdf Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-6B.pdf ## FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS Overview The Declaration processing module in eCMS shows the overall declaration processing for Transit regimes. This SRS is a supplement to the Declaration Processing PART I for Non-Transit regimes and should be referred to for the common processing and core-clearance processes. ## Assumptions and Restrictions The baseline declaration processing module will cover the processes illustrated in the Declaration Processing SRS. ## Transit Overall Transit Hierarchy: Transit can be either international transit, Inland Transit, or regular National transit (not linked to any preceding procedure). For International transit, below is the hierarchy of the processes and shall be presented accordingly in this document. Note: Profile can be configured to route Transit declaration through red lane Alternatively, configuration can be skipped, and risk profiling will be applied, and system will decide the lane. ## International Transit Prerequisite ## The international declarant submitted should be accepted by customs The details required to generate LoG should be acquired ## Process Flow Process ID: 04.32 – Import Declaration ## Process Step Additional Functions ## Business Rule Business Validation ## Customs Expense (International Transit) Prerequisite For Containerized International Transit declaration, the declaration should have Gated in, and the LOG should have been released For Non-Containerized International Transit declaration, the declaration should have Gated out from LTO ## Process Flow Process ID: 04.33 – Customs Expense (International Transit) ## Process Step Business Rule ## Business Validation Import from International Transit ## Prerequisite The Declaration should have been accepted by customs. ## Process Flow Process ID: 04.34 – Import from International Transit ## Process Step Business Rule Please refer to Entry for home use after international transit in Import Section of Declaration Processing SRS for Non-Transit. ## Business Validation Please refer to Entry for home use after international transit in Import Section of Declaration Processing SRS for Non-Transit. ## Inland Transit from International Transit Prerequisite The Declaration should have been accepted by customs. ## Process Flow Process ID: 04.35 – Inland Transit from International Transit ## Process Step Business Rule ## Business Validation (Note: System will also allow Inland Transit from National Transit. The above process steps will apply for Inland Transit from National Transit with the following difference 1. Instead of an International Transit, an approved National Transit will need to be linked. 2. Services charges which are applicable for International Transit shall not apply if the Inland Transit is being done from National Transit) ## National Transit from International Transit Prerequisite The Declaration should have been accepted by customs. ## Process Flow Process ID: 04.36 – National Transit from International Transit ## Process Step Business Rule ## Business Validation Warehouse Declaration from International Transit ## Prerequisite The Declaration should have been accepted by customs ## Process Flow Process ID: 04.37 – Warehouse from International Transit ## Process Step Business Rule Please refer to Warehousing after international transit in Warehouse Declaration Section of Declaration Processing SRS for Non-Transit. ## Business Validation Please refer to Warehousing after international transit in Warehouse Declaration Section of Declaration Processing SRS for Non-Transit. ## National Transit (without Precedence) Prerequisite 1. Note: Though we released the prototype, actual UI implementation look, and feel may vary based on SmartGWT framework. ## Hardware Interfaces NA ## Software Interfaces Declaration module may use below component to achieve some functionalities. ## Drools Expert (rule engine) Appendix ## LOG (Letter of Guarantee) Print LOG can be printed for International Transit Declaration after the declaration is released from the source port by LTO. The system will allow printing of the LoG by both the declarant and the customs. The trader can then submit the LoG to the Indian Customs for release of goods from the customs house along with a Bill of Enter No. In LOG, CIF value will use Indian customs exchange rate while LOG creation and should convert to INR. [CUSTOMS] SRS_eCMS_Offence_Appeal.v1.0

## General Release No 1.0 – Jul 2021 ## Endorsement by System Owner (internal) release history ## Table of Contents Table of Contents 3 1 Introduction 4 1.1 Scope 4 1.2 Definitions and Abbreviations 4 1.3 References 6 2 Functional Requirement 7 2.1 Offence 7 2.2 Appeal 15 2.3 Customs Warehouse 21 3 System Integration 28 4 Appendix 29 4.1 Item Statuses 29 4.2 Offence Statuses 29 4.3 Appeal Statuses 31 4.4 Customs Warehouse Statuses 31 4.5 Report templates 31 4.6 Configuration blueprint (CBP) 35 4.7 Scheduler Jobs 35 4.8 User Interface 35 ## Introduction This document defines & illustrates the business requirements, process flows as well as the detailed functional requirements of eCMS Offence, Penalty, Appeal modules to be implemented for Department of Revenue and Customs, Bhutan. Also included are modules for Customs Warehouse for detained/seized/confiscated goods. Enforcement allows customs to manage breach of Customs law, policies, and regulations. It can be triggered at clearance process. Enforcement is also known as Offence Management, and these are used interchangeably. The function explains management of breach of Customs laws and regulations. The function includes notification of offenders, compounding of offences and waiver of interest on penalties. ## Scope The scope of the Offence module is as below: ## Offence Management Penalty ## Appeal Customs Warehouse ## Definitions and Abbreviations The table below lists the different acronyms and abbreviations as well as the definitions used throughout this SRS. ## References The creation of the BECMS SRS was referenced using the following documents: ## FUNCATIONAL REQUIREMENT SPECIFICATION.docx TECHNICAL REQUIREMENT SPECIFICATION.docx ## Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-3.pdf Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-4.pdf ## Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-5A.pdf Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-5B.pdf ## Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-6A.pdf Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-6B.pdf ## Functional Requirement Offence module shall provide the functionalities for the Enforcement in the Customs to manage the offence committed during the import or export of goods, determine the penalty, admit/release goods from a customs warehouse and allow the declarant/CFA to submit an appeal afterwards. ## Below is a diagram of the overview of the Offence process: OFFENCE OVERVIEW ## Offence Offence Management eCMS enables an offence officer to complete offence reports that have been created by a declaration goods inspection failure reported by a customs officer. eCMS also allows an offence officer to create ad-hoc offence reports due to risk/intelligence failure. An offence can involve personnel or declaration goods. The offence report will also contain the demand note to pay and the action applied on the goods involved. ## Pre-Requisites The user who created the declaration is a registered Declarant (or CFA) in eCMS. The customs officer who updated the failed physical examination is a registered customs officer in eCMS. The offence officer who will facilitate the offence process is a registered offence officer in eCMS. The customs warehouse/temporary storage officer involved in an offence is a registered customs warehouse/temporary storage officer in eCMS. The declarant/CFA, customs warehouse/temporary storage officer, customs officer and offence officer are authorized to access eCMS and have access to the required application. ## Process Flow Use Case Diagram ## Note/s: All Offence Reports can be viewed/updated by offence officers. ## Business Validation Appeal ## Submit Appeal eCMS enables a declarant/CFA/warehouse operator/temporary storage operator involved in an offence to appeal for a refund/cancellation of the demand note payment. The appeal is subject to the approval of a Customs Settlement Committee, Customs Head Office, or Ministry of Finance. ## Pre-Requisites The Declarant/CFA/warehouse operator/temporary storage operator users involved in the appeal (appellant) should be registered in eCMS. The user representing the Customs Settlement Committee, Customs Head Office, or Ministry of Finance should be registered in eCMS. The appellant and approving officers are authorized to access eCMS and have access to the required application. The appellant has an Offence Report with a demand note (Paid or Unpaid). ## Process Flow Use Case Diagram ## Business Validation Note/s: All appeals can be viewed/updated by members of the same party that created it. ## Withdraw Appeal eCMS enables a declarant/CFA/warehouse operator/temporary storage operator involved in an offence to withdraw the appeal for a refund of the demand note payment. ## Pre-Requisites Declarant/CFA/warehouse operator/temporary storage operator users should be registered in eCMS. Declarant/CFA/warehouse operator/temporary storage operator users are authorized to access eCMS and have access to the required application. ## Process Flow Use Case Diagram ## Business Validation Note/s: All appeals can be viewed/updated by members of the same party that created it. ## Customs Warehouse Admit Goods eCMS will enable a customs warehouse officer to admit goods into a customs warehouse. The request to admit goods into a customs warehouse will be generated after an offence officer indicates which goods will be detained/seized/confiscated in an offence report. ## Pre-Requisites Offence users for determining which goods will be admitted into a customs warehouse should be registered in eCMS. Customs warehouse officers for admitting goods should be a registered customs warehouse officer in eCMS. Both offence and customs warehouse officers are authorized to access eCMS and have access to the required application. Customs warehouse locations have been configured in the system and customs warehouse officers have been assigned to them. ## Process Flow Use Case Diagram ## Business Validation Note/s: All customs warehouse officers assigned to the same customs warehouse can view/update the same customs warehouse records. ## Release Goods eCMS will enable a customs warehouse officer to release goods from a customs warehouse. Goods to be released from a customs warehouse can be due to an offence officer releasing detained/seized goods back to the trader or when customs warehouse officer disposing/auctioning goods. ## Pre-Requisites Offence officers for determining which goods will be released from a customs warehouse should be registered in eCMS. Customs warehouse officers for releasing goods should be a registered customs warehouse officer in eCMS. Both offence and customs warehouse officers are authorized to access eCMS and have access to the required application. Customs warehouse locations have been configured in the system and customs warehouse officers have been assigned to them. ## Process Flow Use Case Diagram ## Business Validation Note/s: All customs warehouse officers assigned to the same customs warehouse can view/update the same customs warehouse records. ## System Integration Appendix ## Item Statuses The following are the item statuses at various stages: ## Offence Statuses The following are the offence statuses at various stages: ## Appeal Statuses The following are the appeal statuses at various stages: ## Customs Warehouse Statuses The following are the customs warehouse statuses at various stages: ## Report templates Detention Report ## Seizure Report Inventory Tracking ## Configuration blueprint (CBP) Configuration Blueprint (CBP) for Offence, Appeal ## Configuration Blueprint (CBP) for Customs Warehouse Scheduler Jobs ## User Interface Please refer to the prototype. Note: Though we released the prototype, actual UI implementation look-and-feel may vary based on SmartGWT framework. Process Steps P01.1: Inspection Failure While processing declaration goods, the customs officer can report an Inspection Failure via the Inspection module. This will trigger the system to create an Offence Report with the following data at the General Information tab: Offence Report Number Offence Source – set to Inspection Failure Business Transaction Module – set to Declaration Details of the Declaration involved in the inspection failure Status – set to Draft The Offence Report Number will have the following format: OFN<YYMMDD#####> where: YY – year MM – month DD – day ##### - running sequence number The offence officer will be able to see the draft Offence Report and complete the rest of the details. Note/s: For a declaration that does not have previous declarations, the customs officer can also decide to require a offence officer to update the declaration first after reporting the inspection failure. The Offence Report will still be created but will have a Pending Declaration Amendment status and will be viewable only until the customs officer has completed amending the declaration. For inspection failures that are due to undeclared goods, the declarant/CFA can create a new declaration for the undeclared goods and then during inspection, customs can mark that declaration as inspection failure and route to offence. P01.2: Amend Declaration The offence officer will amend in a separate menu the declaration that was involved in an offence. After the amendment, the Offence report will use the amended data for the demand note computation. P01.3: Select Routed Offence Report An offence officer can select an Offence Report that was created due to an inspection failure and edit the report to complete the rest of the details at the items, documents, and demand note tabs. Note/s: The Offence Report will be viewable only if the customs officer is still amending a declaration after an inspection failure. After the amendment is finished, the Offence Report status will be changed into Draft, and become editable. P01.4: Create Ad-hoc Offence Report An offence officer can create an ad-hoc Offence Report. The report will have the Business Transaction Module set to Ad-hoc at the General Information tab. The offence officer can complete the rest of the General Information details. If the Offence Type is Administrative, the offence officer will need to select the customs warehouse/temporary storage officer involved. Only one customs warehouse/temporary storage officer can be selected for this offence. The Items tab will also be hidden since it is not needed. If the Offence Type is Customs/Criminal, the offence officer must select the Offence Category and: if the category is Declaration, the offence officer will need to select the declaration number involved if category is Passenger Cargo, the offence officer will need to enter all the declaration details After entering all the mandatory inputs, the user can save the General Information data. But before allowing the General Information to be saved, the system will validate the inputs and will display messages if there are errors encountered. If there are no validation issues, the Offence Report Number will be generated the report will have a Draft status. The Offence Report Number will have the following format: OFN<YYMMDD#####> where: YY – year MM – month DD – day ##### - running sequence number Note/s: The Items tab is applicable only for Customs/Criminal offences. P02: Select Item/s If the Offence Type is Customs/Criminal, the offence officer can select the goods available from the declaration entered at the General Information tab and determine the action applied to them by selecting any of the following statuses: Detained (only for Customs offence) Seized (only for Customs offence) Handover to Royal Bhutan Police (only for Criminal offence) Note/s: At least one of the goods in the declaration involved in the offence should have a corresponding status. If at least one of the goods has a Detained status, the Demand Note tab will be hidden. This is to allow the declarant/CFA and offence officer to settle the issue within an allowed period. Once the issue has been settled, the offence officer can update the Offence Report to release the detained goods. If there are seized goods remaining, the Demand Note tab can be shown. If the issue was not settled after an allowed period, a background process will update the Offence Report so that the detained goods will now become seized and then notify the offence officer. The offence officer can then edit the report and see the computed Demand Note tab. P03: Attach Documents The offence officer can update the offence report by attaching related documents (if any). P04: Compute Demand Note Amount Based on Offence Type The system will compute the demand note based on the following: For Administrative offence: 1st Offence – Nu. 10,000 2nd Offence – Nu. 20,000 3rd Offence – Nu. 100,000 For Customs offence: 50% of the invoice The offence officer can update the initial computed amount for the demand note. Note/s: The demand note payment cannot be zero/less than zero. If the declaration was amended after inspection failure, the demand note computation for Customs offence will be 50% of the invoice generated after the amendment. P05: Save Offence Report The offence officer saves the complete Offence Report after entering all the necessary data. But before allowing the report to be saved, the system will validate the report as a whole and will display messages if there are errors encountered. If there are no validation issues, the system will save the report and send a notification to the user/party involved in the offence. The system will also determine the status of the offence report: If all the goods were handed over the Royal Bhutan Police, then the Offence Report status will become Closed. If at least one of the goods was detained, then the Offence Report status will become Submitted. If all the goods are seized, then the Offence Report status will become Pending Payment. The user involved in the offence can use the Offence Report Number to see the payment for the demand note via the Payment module. Once the Offence Report has been submitted, the Declaration involved in the offence can no longer be amended. P06.1: Handover Goods to Royal Bhutan Police The offence officer hands over the goods in the offence report to the Royal Bhutan Police and this will be done outside eCMS. P06.2: Settle Detained Goods Issue with Declarant/CFA The declarant/CFA and the offence officer can settle the issue regarding the detained goods outside eCMS. P06.3: Seize the Detained Goods If the declarant/CFA and the offence officer were not able to settle the issue regarding the detained goods after an allowed period, a background process will update the Offence Report so that the detained goods will now become seizedoffence. The Offence Report will be set to Draft status again so that the offence officer can update the report with the demand note amount. After saving the update, the report status will become Pending Payment. Note/s: Goods whose status was changed by the background process from Detained to Seized cannot be updated to Detained again. P06.4: Release the Detained Goods If the issue regarding detained goods was settled successfully within an allowed period, the offence officer can update the Offence Report and update the goods status from Detained to Released. The customs warehouse officer will be notified and will facilitate the release of the detained goods via the Customs Warehouse module. If all the goods were released, then the Offence Report status will become Closed. If there are remaining goods, then these should be the Seized goods. Please refer to Process #04 for setting the final demand note amount, and Process #05 for completing the Offence Report again. P06.5: Admit Goods to Customs Warehouse The customs warehouse officer will receive the customs warehouse record with a Pending Admission status. The officer will facilitate the actual movement of the detained/seized/confiscated goods into the warehouse and update the record of goods admitted. These will be done via the Customs Warehouse module. Note/s: Goods admitted as detained and status changed from detained to seized and then confiscate, customs warehouse status remains admitted. P06.6: Suspend Licence If the customs warehouse/temporary storage officer involved in the offence has committed the offence for the third consecutive time, the system will suspend/cancel the user’s account in eCMS via the Registration module. P07.1: Pay Demand Note The user involved in the offence can use the Offence Report Number to see the payment for the demand note via the Payment module. If the offence is an Administrative type, then the Offence Report status will become Closed. If the offence is a Customs type, then the Offence Report status will become Paid. P07.2: Register Demand Note eCMS will send the details of the Demand Note to the Revenue System via system integration. Note/s: It also expected that, when a payment has been made, the revenue system will return details of the receipt to the eCMS. P07.3: Confiscate the Seized Goods The offence officer has the option to confiscate goods that have been seized and while the demand note is still pending payment. The officer can update the Offence Report with a Pending Payment status and update the goods status from Seized to Confiscated. If all the goods have been confiscated, then the Offence Report status will become Closed. If there are remaining goods, then these should be the Seized goods and the Offence Report status will still be Pending Payment. P07.4: Cancel Demand Note If the Offence Report has a Pending Payment status and the offence officer updated it to confiscate all the goods, then the system will cancel the Demand Note payment. P07.5: De-Register Demand Note eCMS will send the details of the Demand Note deregistration to the Revenue System via system integration. P07.6: Release the Seized Goods The offence officer has the option to release all seized goods only after: the trader submitted an appeal to avoid paying the demand note the trader paid the demand note After this, the Offence Report status will become Closed. P07.7: Release Goods from Customs Warehouse The customs warehouse officer will update the customs warehouse record associated with the Offence Report and release the goods that have a Release to Trader status. The officer will facilitate the actual release of the detained/seized goods from the warehouse and update the record of goods that are still admitted. These will be done via the Customs Warehouse module. [TABLE] S/N | Validation Rules 1 | At least one of the goods in the declaration involved in the offence should have a corresponding status. 2 | The demand note payment cannot be zero/less than zero. 3 | The status of item/goods can be updated from Seized to Released only if the demand note has been paid. 4 | All seized goods must be updated to release to trader after demand note payment. 5 | Confiscated goods cannot be released to trader / declarant. [TABLE] Process Steps P01: Create Appeal To create an appeal, the user must first select an Offence Report that that user is involved with. An Offence Report can only be selected if: The report is not used in another appeal The offence involves a demand note. The user can edit the appeal to add remarks and attach documents if required. After updating the appeal, the user can submit. P02: Submit Appeal After entering all the mandatory inputs, the user can submit the appeal. But before allowing the appeal data to be saved, the system will validate the inputs and will display messages if there are errors encountered. If there are no validation issues, the Appeal Number will be generated the report will have a Submitted status. The Appeal Number will have the following format: APL-<YYYY##########> where: YYYY – year ########## - running sequence number Upon submission, the system will determine the officer that will be receiving the appeal for approval: If the appeal involves a demand note that is less than Nu. 200,000 (configurable in the system), and is the user’s first appeal submission, the approver will be the Customs Settlement Committee If the appeal involves a demand note that is greater than or equal to Nu. 200,000 (configurable in the system), or is the user’s second appeal submission after rejection, the approver will be the Customs Head Office Appeal Committee If the appeal is the user’s third appeal submission after rejection, the approver will be the Ministry of Finance. Note/s: At the Offence module, Offence Report associated with the Appeal will have a Pending Approval status under the Appeal column. P03.1: Reject or Approve The appeal is routed to an officer for approval. The officer selects the appeal and determines which of the following statuses will be applied: Approve Reject The appellant will be notified of the approval result. If the appeal is to be approved and the appellant had paid the demand note, the approving officer can also set the refund amount less than or equal to the demand note amount. Otherwise, there is no refund required. If the appeal has been approved, the appellant has not yet paid the demand note, and the Offence Report has a Pending Payment status, then the Offence Report status becomes Closed. If the appeal has been rejected and the appellant has not yet paid the demand note, the Offence Report status becomes Pending Payment and the appellant must pay the demand note. If the appeal is rejected for the first time, the appellant can update the appeal and submit again (refer to Process #02 for the officer who will be receiving the re-submitted appeal). Once the appeal has been rejected by the Ministry of Finance, the appeal’s rejection status becomes final, the appeal can no longer be updated, and the appellant can now only do the appeal via the court of law outside eCMS. Note/s: If the appeal has been rejected, the Offence Report associated with the Appeal will have a Rejected status under the Appeal Status column. If the appeal has been resubmitted after rejection, the Offence Report associated with the Appeal will have a Pending Approval status under the Appeal Status column. If the appeal has been approved, the Offence Report associated with the Appeal will have an Approved status under the Appeal Status column. If the appeal has been rejected, the Offence Report associated with the Appeal will have a Rejected status under the Appeal Status column. The refund amount cannot be zero. P03.2: Route to Customs Head Office Appeal Committee Approver If the current appeal approver is the Customs Settlement Committee and 30 days had passed without any action, the appeal will be routed to the Customs Head Office Appeal Committee via a background job process. P03.3: Route to Ministry of Finance Approver If the current appeal approver is the Customs Head Office and 30 days had passed without any action, the appeal will be routed to the Ministry of Finance via a background job process. P03.4: Refund Demand Note If the appeal was approved, then the approved status of the appeal becomes final and can no longer be updated. If the appellant has paid a demand note beforehand, the appellant can proceed to do a refund via the Refund module. P03.5: Cancel Demand Note If the appeal was approved, then the approved status of the appeal becomes final and can no longer be updated. If the appellant has not yet paid the demand note beforehand, the system will cancel the payment instruction and send a de-registration of the payment to the Revenue System. P04: Appeal Expires If the current appeal approver is the Ministry of Finance and 45 days had passed without any action, the appeal will be expired via a background job process. The expired status of the appeal is final, and the appeal no longer be updated. The appellant can now only do the appeal via the court of law outside eCMS. Note/s: At the Offence module, Offence Report associated with the Appeal will have a Expired status under the Appeal column. [TABLE] S/N | Validation Rules 1 | If the appeal involves a demand note that is less than Nu. 200,000 (configurable in the system), or is the user’s first appeal, the approver will be the Customs Settlement Committee 2 | If the appeal involves a demand note that is greater than or equal to Nu. 200,000 (configurable in the system), or is the user’s second appeal, the approver will be the Customs Head Office Appeal Committee. 3 | If the appeal is the user’s third appeal, the approver will be the Ministry of Finance. 4 | The expired status of the appeal is final and can no longer be updated. 5 | If the appeal was rejected for the third time, its rejection status is final and can no longer be updated. 6 | Only one appeal record can be created for an offence report 7 | The refund amount cannot be zero. [TABLE] Process Steps P01: Search Appeal Pending Approval The user can select an existing appeal that has been submitted and not yet Approved/Rejected. A reason is required before saving the withdrawal update. P02: Withdraw Appeal After the user saves the withdrawal update, the status of the appeal becomes Withdrawn and can no longer be re-used. [TABLE] S/N | Validation Rules 1 | Approval is not required for withdrawing an appeal. 2 | Once an appeal has been withdrawn it can no longer be re-used. [TABLE] Process Steps P01.1: Detain/Seize/Confiscate Goods Offence officer updates a goods status in an offence report so that it declares the number of items detained/seized/confiscated. This is done via the Offence module. This will generate a customs warehouse record with a Pending Admission status and will contain the goods for admission. P01.2: Search Record Requesting for Admission Offence officer can select a customs warehouse record that was generated after goods were detained/seized/confiscated in an offence report. Each of the goods in the record will contain a specific number of items pending admission, and this will be initially set to the number of items detained/seized/confiscated. The customs warehouse officer can admit a specific number of items less than or equal to the number of items pending admission. After entering the number of items to be admitted, the officer can save the record. If there are no validation issues, the system will save the entered data. Note/s: The number of admitted items cannot be zero/less than zero. P01.3: Create Ad-hoc Record of Goods for Admission Offence officer can also create an ad-hoc customs warehouse record to admit goods. The offence officer can select the warehouse to admit the goods. Multiple goods can be included in a customs warehouse record. After entering the HS code details of the goods and the number of items to be admitted, the officer can save the record. If there are no validation issues, the system will save the entered data. Note/s: The number of admitted items cannot be zero/less than zero. P03: Admit Goods After the system saves the goods details and number of items admitted: If the customs warehouse record was created from an offence report: for each of the goods in the record, the number of items admitted will be subtracted from the number of items pending admission if one of the goods has items pending admission, then the status of the customs warehouse record will be Partially Admitted if all the goods have no items pending admittance, then the status of the customs warehouse record will be Fully Admitted If the customs warehouse record is an ad-hoc record, then the status of the customs warehouse record will be Fully Admitted [TABLE] S/N | Validation Rules 1 | For customs warehouse requests generated by an offence report, the number of items to be admitted can be less than or equal to the number of items pending admission. 2 | The number of admitted items cannot be zero/less than zero. [TABLE] Process Steps P01: Allow Release of Detained/Seized Goods Offence officer updates the status of goods in an offence report so that its items that had been detained/seized become released. This is done via the Offence module. P02: Search Goods for Release Customs warehouse officer searches a customs warehouse record with admitted goods and determines the number of items to be released and how they will be released. The number of items to be released can be less than or equal to the number of goods admitted. The release status available will be based on the following: If the goods had been released in an offence report, the goods status can be updated to Release to Trader If the goods are not associated with an offence report or had been confiscated in an offence report, the goods status can be updated to any of the following: Destroy Auction After entering the number of items to be released, the officer can save the record. If there are no validation issues, the system will save the entered data. Note/s: The number of released items cannot be zero/less than zero. P03: Release Goods After the system saves the number of items to be released and their release status: if the customs warehouse record previously is Fully Admitted and then all the goods became released, then the customs warehouse record will no longer show up the Customs Warehouse menus for Admitting/Releasing Goods if the customs warehouse record previously is Partially Admitted and then all the goods became released, then: the customs warehouse record will no longer show up the Customs Warehouse menus for Releasing Goods the customs warehouse record will still show up in the Customs Warehouse menus for Admitting Goods, so the customs warehouse officer can admit the rest of the items if the customs warehouse record previously is Fully/Partially Admitted and then not all the goods became released, then: the customs warehouse record will still show up in the Customs Warehouse menu for Admitting Goods, so the customs warehouse officer can admit the rest of the items the customs warehouse record will still show up in the Customs Warehouse menus for Releasing Goods, so that the customs warehouse officer can release the rest of the items A release history of the goods will also be created for reference. [TABLE] S/N | Validation Rules 1 | The number of items to be released can be less than or equal to the number of goods admitted. 2 | The number of released items cannot be zero/less than zero. 3 | If the goods had been released in an offence report, the goods status can be updated to Release to Trader 4 | If the goods are not associated with an offence report or had been confiscated in an offence report, the goods status can be updated to any of the following: • Destroy • Auction [TABLE] Service Provider | Service Consumer | Service Description Declaration | Offence | Retrieve the Declaration details for offence report Passenger Cargo | Offence | Retrieve Declaration details for offence report Inspection | Offence | Create a draft offence report due to an inspection failure of declaration goods Payment | Offence | Generate the payment details from the demand note Customs Warehouse | Offence | Retrieve the Customs warehouse associated with the Customs office assigned to the Declaration involved in the offence [TABLE] Item Status | Description Detained | For Customs offence type. Goods will be stored in the customs warehouse and there is no demand note payment required. Goods can be released to the trader/declarant after settling the issue with offence officer. Seized | For Customs offence type. Detained goods become seized if the issue between the trader/declarant and the offence officer was not settled within a specific period. Goods will be stored in the customs warehouse and demand note payment is required. Goods can be released to the trader/declarant after demand note has been paid/appeal has been filed. Handed Over to Royal Bhutan Police | For Criminal offence type. Goods will be handed over to the Royal Bhutan Police. Confiscated | For Customs offence type. Seized goods become confiscated while the demand note is not yet paid. Goods will be stored in the customs warehouse. Goods can be released later for auction/disposal. Released | For Customs offence type. Can refer to any of the following: 1. Detained goods were released to the trader/declarant after settling the issue with offence officer. 2. Seized goods were released to the trader/declarant after demand note has been paid/appeal has been filed. 3. Confiscated goods were released for auction/disposal. [TABLE] Offence Status | Offence Type | Description Pending Declaration Amendment | Not Applicable | Offence officer has decided to amend the declaration after reporting the inspection failure. Draft | Administrative Customs Criminal | 1. Offence officer has created/updated the Offence report details but not yet saved at the Summary tab to finalize the report. 2. Offence officer has completed amending the declaration after reporting the inspection failure. Draft | Customs | A specific number of days has passed, and the background process has updated the status of goods from Detained into Seized. The Offence Report status will be reverted into Draft status so that the offence officer can update the report, set the final demand note amount and save the report at the Summary tab again to finalize the report. Submitted | Customs | The offence officer has finalized the report that was in a Draft status and the status of all goods is any combination of the following: Detained or Detained and Seized Note: A customs warehouse record will be created with a Pending Admittance status. Pending Payment | Administrative | 1. The offence officer has finalized the report that was in a Draft status. 2. The appellant has not yet paid the demand note and the appeal was rejected. Pending Payment | Customs | 1. The demand note is not yet paid, and the status of all goods is Seized. 2. The demand note is not yet paid, and the offence officer updated the status of some of the goods from Seized into Confiscated. 3. The appellant has not yet paid the demand note and the appeal was rejected. Paid | Administrative | The demand note has been paid. Paid | Customs | The demand note has been paid. Closed | Administrative | 1. Customs/Warehouse officer has paid the demand note. 2. The appellant has not yet paid the demand note and the appeal was approved so that there is no demand note to pay. Closed | Customs | 1. The demand note has been paid and the offence officer has updated the status of all goods into Released. 2. The demand note has not yet been paid and the offence officer has updated the status of all goods into Confiscated. 3. The appellant has not yet paid the demand note and the appeal was approved so that there is no demand note to pay. Closed | Criminal | Offence officer has finalized Offence report details for a Criminal offence. [TABLE] Appeal Status | Description Pending Approval | The appeal has been submitted/resubmitted after rejection and is pending approval. Approved | The appeal has been approved. Rejected | The appeal has been rejected. Expired | The appeal has expired. [TABLE] Customs Warehouse Status | Description Pending Admittance | None of the goods have been admitted into the warehouse. Partially Admitted | Some of the goods have been admitted into the warehouse. Fully Admitted | All the goods have been admitted into the warehouse.
