Functional Requirements 7 1.1 Overview 7 1.2 Risk Management Process 7 1.3 Risk Analysis Process 8 1.4 Profile Based Quantitative Assessment 9 1.5 Risk Configuration 10 1.5.1 Rule Editor 10 1.5.2 Risk Threshold 10 1.5.3 Risk Profile Creation Process 10 1.5.4 Risk Profile Management 11 1.5.5 Random Selectivity for Red Lane 11 1.6 Risk Assessment Process 12 1.7 Risk Review / Monitoring Process 14 1.8 Use Cases 15 1.8.1 Lane Management Use Cases 15 1.8.2 Profile Management Use Cases 15 1.8.3 Risk Assessment on Declaration Use Cases 16 ## Appendix A 17 1. Configuration blueprint (CBP) 17 ## Introduction This document defines & illustrates the business requirements, process flows as well as the detailed functional requirements of eCMS Risk module to be implemented for Department of Revenue and Customs, Bhutan. The risk management is one of the core clearance process in the eCMS and is part of the declaration processing. The risk management design follows the WCO guidelines for risk assessment. ## Definitions and Abbreviations The table below lists the different acronyms and abbreviations as well as the definitions used throughout this SRS. ## References The creation of the BECMS SRS was referenced using the following documents: ## FUNCATIONAL REQUIREMENT SPECIFICATION.docx TECHNICAL REQUIREMENT SPECIFICATION.docx ## Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-3.pdf Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-4.pdf ## Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-5A.pdf Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-5B.pdf ## Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-6A.pdf Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-6B.pdf ## Functional Requirements Overview Risk assessment will be conducted on all the submitted declarations. Risk assessment will be based on the profiles configured. Risk assessment is based on the WCO recommended principles with the objective of minimizing risk and improving overall operations efficiency via the use of risk-based selectivity approach. ## Risk Management Process The eCMS Risk Management Process is a 5-step process as shown below. The risk analysis consists of historical analysis on the past transactions and the outcome & then deriving the risk indicators and profiles for assessment through quantitative analysis of the current consignments. Depending on the outcome of the risk assessment, the treatments measures are applied accordingly. The process includes a performance monitoring step where the risk indicators and profiles are reviewed periodically on the effectiveness and tuned & optimized. The risk analysis, profiling and monitoring/review is done by the risk intelligence unit of the customs administration. The risk assessment is done by the system and the treatment measures are applied by customs operational staff. ## The risk management process includes: Risk Analysis is done using the workbench. ## Rule Editor Profile ## Threshold Configurations Risk Profiling – done after risk analysis. The output of the analysis is the profile configuration. Targeted Profiles – Specific profiles assigned with probability and consequence. ## Risk Assessment Risk assessment is done against the profiles as and when the data/transaction is available. ## Risk Treatment Risk actions like inspection, quarantine, lab tests etc. are configured for profiles. Assessment officers can take appropriate actions based on the risk indicator score output through the lane. ## Risk Performance Monitoring System will identify the risk for any transactions with area and action level. Risk team can monitor the risk details periodically and can fine tune the risk profiles, based on the business requirement. ## Risk Analysis Process System offers a holistic quantitative risk assessment approach taking into consideration of known risks. The functional overview of the approach is as below: The risk assessment engine is an independent engine that runs any transaction data through the assessment process. This enables the assessment engine to do a quantitative risk analysis on all information as and when it is available in the clearance process supporting a progressive risk assessment in the supply chain. The risk indicators or the fields are generic, predefined and a complete list is included. These fields will be applicable to any transaction. As long as the transaction contains the fields required for a profile to be hit, the profile will be assessed for that transaction. Quantitative Risk Assessment is based on the WCO recommended approach of deriving the significance of risk through a scoring mechanism. The overall risk is quantified based on risk indicators and the cumulative scores are applied to the particular transaction. The system supports the following configurations. ## Profile Based Quantitative Assessment The purpose of the profile based quantitative assessment is to identify and categorize known risks. Profile based assessment considers 2 factors for quantifying the risk i.e. the probability of occurrence and the impact of the risk. Risk scores are configured at each profile level. Risk score will be derived based on expert approach where Risk Management officer based on the experience will use below formula: ## Risk Significance Score = Likelihood X Consequence Likelihood/Probability Scores are as below: 1-Very Low, 2-Low, 3-Medium, 4- High, 5- Very High ## Impact/Consequence Weightage Scores. Sample scoring is defined below: 10-Very Low, 15-Low, 20-Medium, 25- High, 30- Very High The consequence will be decided by the risk analysts/expert. Customs can configure their own profiles. ## The evaluation of the profile-based score will follow the below process: Profile Threshold ## As sample configuration for profile threshold is shown below: Risk Configuration ## Rule Editor Risk rules can be composed for any of the available fields in the rule editor. The rules will be applied horizontally across irrespective of the document. For e.g., a rule defined with “Country of Consignment” = “China”, will be applied to declaration documents. Risk indicators form the key aspect of a risk management approach adopted in the system. Risk indicators can be defined, and the rules are composed using the rule editor. The rules configured in the rule editor is applied systematically & progressively as more information becomes available for a cargo in the clearance process. ## Risk Threshold Risk threshold configurations will be done for profile based. Officer can configure the thresholds. Sample risk threshold configuration is shown below. The threshold should be audited, and all history should be captured. ## Risk Profile Creation Process The below section illustrates the process of linking Risk Action and Risk area with while creating a risk profile in the system. ## The risk administration involved creation of the following configurations: Risk Lane ## Risk Threshold Risk Profile ## Risk Alerts / Notification Risk Profile Management This section describes the maintenance of Risk Profile Data such as adding risk profile record, update risk profile, search risk profile and delete risk profile. The risk profile is created to link the action taken for a risk area. Risk profiles are the lowest level and defined at a granular level. Risk profiles are defined for declaration. The risk areas are assigned to the risk profiles. Risk rules configured in the rule editor can be associated here. Only 1 risk rule can be associated per profile. ## The following are the risk significance attributes: Probability of occurrence ## Impact of Occurrence General notification alert can be configured for profiles. ## Design Considerations for configuration of Risk Random Selectivity for Red Lane Customs requires a certain percentage of the declarations which are declared to be on GREEN lane by the system to go through the RED lane instead. The percentage is configurable on the lane. This random selection shall help them (Officer) to check the quality of the Risk Profile Management as well as the flaws if any. ## Design Consideration Risk Assessment Process Note : Process between P06 and P07 will be considered as risk treatment process. Based on risk outcome officer will review and act on the declaration/s accordingly. ## Risk Review / Monitoring Process During the risk review intelligence officer has to check the quality of the Risk Profiles and their outcome, based on the outcome and feedback from various customs officers, risk office will fine tune the profile periodically. Additionally, intelligence officer will collect risk details from various sources and update the profile to identify the vulnerable / fraudulent transaction which tries to enter the country. ## Use Cases Lane Management Use Cases ## Profile Management Use Cases Risk Assessment on Declaration Use Cases ## Appendix A Configuration blueprint (CBP) Configuration Blueprint (CBP) for Risk. Low | 1 | Very low probability of this risk occurring. (For e.g. import of agriculture from Iran) Low | 2 | Low probability of this risk occurring Medium | 3 | Medium probability of this risk occurring High | 4 | High probability of this risk occurring Very High | 5 | Very high probability of this risk occurring. (for e.g. consignment with country of origin as “China”) [TABLE] Risk Assessment Steps (Profile Based) P01: Risk Assessment Initialize The risk assessment will be initiated when the transaction to be assessed is made available. The data in the transaction will be mapped to the generic risk indicators (fields) and all relevant profiles details will be assessed. P02: Scan Profiles After the Risk Assessment is triggered, it will go through each profile which is created already in the system. Profiles which do not meet the risk indicator criteria for that transaction will be ignored. For e.g. if Postal Transit Declaration data is being assessed and it does not contain HS Code, all profiles with HS Code as a risk indicator will be ignored. P03: Profile Score Computation The profile score will be computed. For the computation method refer the design consideration as below. The final score will go through the threshold configurations. Depending on the range of the threshold configuration, the final lane will be assessed i.e. Red, Yellow, Green and Blue etc. The risk treatment or actions to be taken to mitigate the risk will be derived through the profiles. P04: Random Selectivity In addition, for cases of green or lower, a random selectivity will be applied to convert the lane to Yellow/Red i.e. 2%. [TABLE] Lane | Threshold Red | 75 & above Yellow | >=45 <75 Green | <45 [TABLE] Lane | Threshold (Any one of the area) | Areas Red | 75 & above | Fraud Yellow | >=45 <75 | Security Yellow | >=60 <75 | All Green | <45 [TABLE] S/N | Description 1 | Audit trail shall be provided for the basic operations of this functionality. 2 | General notification template can be defined for the profiles. When profile is hit, the corresponding notification will be sent to the configured recipients (customs). [TABLE] S/N | Validation Rules 1 | Audit trail shall be provided for the basic operations of this functionality. 2 | System determines the number of transactions to be sent from Green lane to Red lane based on previous working day transactions. This is determined by the system backend job during assessment of declaration. 3 | System randomly selects configured percentage of transactions which are determined as GREEN lane to pass through RED lane. 4 | Those declarations submitted by trader with ACT status will be exempted from random selectivity. [TABLE] Risk Assessment for Declaration P01: Retrieve the declaration The system will retrieve the declaration data from the declaration module and use this detail for subsequent risk analysis. P02: Determine the ACT Status System will check the importing party and verifies the Authorized Complaint Trader (ACT). If the party is having ACT status, then the declaration will be assigned to Bule lane directly. P03: Evaluate using Risk Profiles System will go through each profile which are already available in system and profile score will be calculated. P04: Determine Risk on Declaration The final score will go through the threshold configurations. Depending on the range of the threshold configuration, the final lane will be assessed i.e. Red, Yellow, Green and Blue etc. If a transaction has hit 2 profiles, the highest risk will be taken as the final. For e.g. if one profile indicates “Green” and another indicates “Yellow”, “Yellow will be taken as the final lane. P05: Random Selectivity In addition, for cases of green lane, a random selectivity will be applied to convert the lane to Yellow/Red. P06: Manually Change Lane Customs officer can also change the lane manually by accessing the risk assessment record. Lowering lane is not possible in the system i.e. Red to Green, however officer has option to increase the risk lane i.e. Green to Yellow / Red. P07: Flag declaration for Inspection If the lane is changed, lets assume that lane is changes from Green to Yellow/Red, then the system flags that declaration for Inspection.

In this sub-system, Customs valuation unit creates and uses the historical transaction data as reference for valuation of all commodities in the declaration. Specific profile-based valuation range may also be defined when valuation officers are sure on the valuation of certain commodities meeting certain criteria. Profile based valuations are used to target specific cases of valuation frauds and “as such” will be used less frequently than transaction based. ## This valuation sub-system also captures the value based on last transactions made during the period for all the HS Codes. For transaction method, the system builds the valuation database. Profile based or transaction-based valuation can be selected based on the HS Code. Once eCMS receives the declaration, the declaration value is verified with the valuation database or the profile if configured. The valuation assessment will indicate if the goods are “under value” or “overvalued” or cleared. The valuation assessing officer may update his inputs on the valuation. ## Valuation process is involved in Import, Transit, Warehouse, Temporary Import, Re-Import Regime flows. Refer to the regimes flows in the declaration processing SRS. ## Configure Valuation Criteria (Transaction & Profile Based) Description The configuration valuation criteria are the process of setting the Lower and Upper percentage range based on the number of past transactions or transactions for particular duration of time. ## The valuation criteria can be of two types: Global Valuation criteria ## Specific Valuation criteria Transaction based (H.S Codes) ## Profile based (H.S Codes) The Global Valuation criteria refers to the default criteria for all the Items and is considered when there are no available Specific Valuation criteria for the H.S Code of that corresponding item. ## This functionality allows Customs control to establish the verification criteria based on the historical valuation records available in eCMS system and the past transaction details captured in the eCMS system. ## The configuration set for the criteria is used to check the value declared by the Declarant for an Item in the declaration that falls in the Customs criteria value or not. ## Pre-Requisites For setting the specific valuation criteria, the H S Codes should have been created in Tariff Management module. ## Transaction Based This transaction-based valuation methodology will be used to achieve DRC’s both Transaction [Past number transaction] & Similar Goods [HSCode] valuation process. Once the criteria are set, the H.S Codes provided in the declaration items matches this criteria and calculates the customs value as per the past transaction history of the declarations. The transaction history to be considered is according to No. of past transactions/Historic duration set for that H.S Code or global criteria. ## Global Valuation Criteria The Customs user can edit the Global valuation criteria and set the values like lower and upper percentage range and set the values for the type of transaction criteria (No. of past transactions/Historic duration i.e. past no. of days). The Global criteria cannot be set for multiple records and set only once for all the declarations. The set global criteria are the default criteria for a declaration item if there are no specific criteria set for the item’s HS Code. ## Specific Valuation Criteria The Customs User can provide the Specific valuation criteria for each of H S Codes with a valuation criteria like the type of transaction criteria (No. of past transactions/Historic duration i.e. past no. of days). ## Minimum Price List System will have the database of minimum price list. Officer can view and update the valuation result accordingly. This code table can be managed by the valuation admin or senior officer based on access right / role assigned. eCMS system will have valuation database for minimum price list where officer can search valuation for HS code and update the valuation result for items. However, for declared HScode if the minimum list price is available in the database, system will show the value in the valuation screen for the officer to view and decide appropriate customs value, Note : DRC shared the data to create the database for minimum price list for initial rollout. ## Profile Based This valuation methodology is similar to DRC’s Identical Goods process which can be used with profile-based configuration. ## The profile-based configuration for valuation criteria is a process of setting the specific profile with valuation boundaries i.e. upper and lower limits with variance at HS Code level. ## The profile setup will comprise of the following key inputs: Process Flow ## Use Cases Customs Value Calculation ## Description After the submission and completion of Payment and Declaration Approval processes, the declaration is updated to Pending Valuation status. The backend process for customs value picks the declaration with Pending Valuation status and calculates the customs value. The Customs value calculation is the backend process for calculating the Customs value for each item based on the criteria provided by the Customs after the Customs Officer approves the declaration. ## Pre-Requisite The declaration should have been submitted by the declarant and has been auto approved or manually approved by the Customs Officer. ## The backend process should be triggered to calculate the Customs value once the Customs Officer approves the declaration, and the status of the declaration is Pending Valuation. The General Valuation criteria must be set prior to the initiation of backend process. ## Process Flow Customs Value Calculation ## The status of each item is updated to ‘Cleared’ when the declared value is equal to the HS code value or if the declared value is within the range of historical values. Otherwise, the item will be sent to inspection officer. ## Valuation Assessment Description This is the process when the Customs Valuation Officer checks the items declared in the declaration and updates the status of the valuation as cleared/under value/over-value. The system will however maintain the value declared by the declarant as well. ## Pre-Requisite The declaration should be accepted by customs, payment completed and pending for valuation ## Process Flow Use Case ## Appendix A Configuration blueprint (CBP) Configuration Blueprint (CBP) for Valuation. for Regional Cooperation SCTS | Single Customs Trade System SITA | International Aeronautical Telecommunications Society TPN | Taxpayer Number TPN | Taxpayer Number UPU | Universal Postal Union [TABLE] S/N | Functinality | Validation Rules 1 | Header Info | Profile validity, effective date, regime/CPC group 2 | HS Identifier | This is HS-Code 3 | Profile Indicators | These are fields that are retrieved from the HS table. For e.g. the profile indicator fields like Country of Origin, Qty and Qty UOM etc. 4 | Operators | The profile indicator fields may have logical operators for e.g. “=”, “in”, “like”, “starts with” etc. to enable configuring the profile fields effectively. 5 | Boundaries | Upper & lower percentile [TABLE] Process Steps P01: Profile Creation Customs Officer will initiate the valuation profile by inputting the values like profile type, code, start date, end date, valuation value, percentile lower, percentile upper etc. P02: Valuation Updated in system Profile is created and picked by system when declaration is due for pending valuation. P03: Valuation Criteria Valuation officer can create the specific criteria like HS Code with valuation value, percentile lower and percentile upper. P04: Criteria updated in system Specific criteria created and picked by system when declaration is due for pending valuation [TABLE] S/N | Process Description 1 | Customs value calculation is the backend process of calculating the Customs value of the items based on the criteria provided by the Customs. After the submission of the declaration and completion of Payment and Declaration Approval processes, the declaration is updated to Pending Valuation status. 2 | The backend process of Customs valuation for the declared items in the submitted declaration is triggered when the status of the declaration is Pending Valuation. 3 | The backend process checks the specific criteria for each item against the H.S Codes. This means that first the criteria set to H.S code is checked. If there are no specific criteria, then the Global criterion is considered for calculating the Customs value. 4 | If the specific criteria are matched against HS codes, then the backend valuation is triggered and the Customs value is calculated and set to the declaration item. This process is continued for all the items in a declaration and the Customs value is calculated and set to each item. 5 | The Global criteria are considered for calculating the Customs value only if any of the specific criteria are not matched for an item. [TABLE] S/N | Validation Rules 1 | If a criteria is matched: The system checks calculated customs value to the declared value. If the calculated value is more than the configured range, then the system updates the status of item valuation to “undervalue” If the calculated value is less than the configured range, then the system updates the status of item valuation to “overvalue” If the calculated value is more than the configured range, then the system updates the status of item valuation to “cleared (inside defined range)” Example, Percentile value = (declared value – (percentile value/100))*declared value Declared Value - 1000 If percentile lower is 10% then, calculated lower percentile value is 900. If percentile upper is 10% then, calculated upper percentile value is 1100. In this case, range is 900 - 1100 Declared value is 850 and configured range i.e. 900-1100 and calculated value is 1000 which is more than declared value then it should be “undervalue” Declared value is 1200 and configured range i.e. 900-1100 and calculated value is 1000 which is less than declared value then it should be “overvalue”. Declared value is 1000 and configured range i.e. 900-1100 and calculated value is 1000 which is within the range then it should be “Inside defined range” [TABLE] Process Steps P01Valuation Profiles System scans the valuation profiles if any and calculate the customs value accordingly. P02: Valuation by Transaction Value System will scan the valuation history for past number of transactions or past number of days based and calculate the customs value accordingly. P03, P04 and P05: Valuation result Valuation result will be updated for each item based on the customs valuation calculated by system. Possible valuation result is. Undervalue Inside defined range(acceptable) Overvalue P06: Valuation Result Update The process for declaration valuation verification involves the valuation officer to update the assessment results. The valuation officers cross verifies the declared value (item) by the declarant and the Customs value calculated by the system and updates the status of the valuation accordingly. The valuation officer assesses the goods/items and checks the declared value and the Customs value and can update below statuses: Cleared Undervalue Overvalue Each item in the declaration has to be updated separately with any of the above statuses. If the status is undervalued, the valuation officer will input the “customs value” and the customs “unit price” for the item including any remarks for the inspection officer to note. Cleared (Inside Defined Range) The valuation officer updates the cleared status if the declared value and the Customs value fall in between the percentage of upper and lower values. Undervalue The Undervalue status is updated by the valuation officer, if the Customs value is more than the declared value. Overvalue The Over value status is updated by the valuation officer, if the Customs value is less than the declared value. If Under value status is updated by the valuation officer, also system will provide an option to the valuation officer to route either “Yellow” or “Red” lane. The comments made by the valuation officer and the customs value input will be used subsequently during inspection stage to re-compute taxes and additional payments required. The declaration proceeds to the next step i.e. risk assessment. The outcome of the valuation is passed to the risk assessment module.

There are three (3) kinds of Refunds which are listed below: ## Refund of penalties with the following of an appeal Refund for a wrong classification ## Refunds should be made inside one (1) year of the declaration being acknowledged by the Customs Refund Use Cases ## Refund & Completed Refund Use Case use case diagram for REFUND in ecms ## Refund Backend Pre-Requisite BITS is ready to accept and process the refund details sent by eCMS and respond with the demand notice for the refund. ## Process Flow Figure 5: refund process flow ## Refund Process Steps Refund Status Below shows the status transition of a Refund Instructions made. Pending Refund: It is pending refund in the System. Paid Refund: BITS or the revenue system will generate the demance notice against the refund made by the trader and the status refunded will be updated in the system Cancelled Refund: Refund is Cancelled. ## INTERFACES REQUIREMENTS System Interfaces ## Figure 8: System Interfaces Appendix ## Configurable BLUEPRINT (CBP) [TABLE] System REQUIREMENTS SPECIFICATION for ecms - Refund Module [TABLE] document identification no 3 char SYS ID/ DOC CODE /NN/ V M.n) for details refer to document mgmt stds | document title | status (draft/ released) | date of release | pages ECMS/SRS/01/V1.1 | System requirements Specifications for ECMS Refund | released | 07.2021 [TABLE] role in the project | Name | signature | date (dd-mm-yy) Authors | Technical Team | 22-07-2021 Reviewers | Project Lead | Sujit Patra Approver | Project Manager | Raghavan Jaganathan [TABLE] Name | designation | signature | date (dd-mm-yy) endorsed by system owner. [TABLE] release no | author | CR# | date | summary of changes 1.0 | karma | 8/19/2021 | Initial Release [TABLE] S/N | Abbreviations | Description BITS | Bhutan Integrated Tax System BTC | Bhutan Tariff Classification CFA | Clearing and Forwarding Agent CDS | Customs Declaration System DITT | Department of Information Technology & Telecom DRC | Department of Revenue & Customs eCMS | Electronic Customs Management System EMS | Express Mail Service FRS | Functional Requirements Specification GST | Goods and Services Tax IDEC | Import Duty Exemption Certificate LTO | Liaison and Transit Office LoG | Letter of Guarantee LCS | Land Customs Station MoEA | Ministry of Economic Affairs MoHCA | Ministry of Home and Cultural Affairs MoF | Ministry of Finance MIS | Management Information System Nu | Ngultrum RMA | Royal Monetary Authority RGoB | Royal Government of Bhutan RRCO | Regional Revenue and Customs Office RTO | Regional Trade Office RAMIS | Revenue Administration Management Information System SARC | South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation SITA | International Aeronautical Telecommunications Society SCTS | Single Customs Trade System SAD | Single Administration Document TPN | Taxpayer Number UPU | Universal Postal Union [TABLE] Process Steps P01: Submit Application Users must be able to apply for a refund by completing an online application form and attaching scanned copies of supporting documents, including receipt number of payments, invoices, Customs declaration, and exemption certificate (if applicable). In addition, the form should also allow for the application to be linked to the original Customs Declaration. In case the non-exempted person has paid custom duty, taxes and others., made on behalf of exempted party must define the name of importer and the ID of consignment details. P02: Verify Application When the application has been made, by the applicant Customs will verify the application and supporting documents. If the application has been successfully verified, it must then be forwarded to the next available Assessor at RCCO, on a rotational basis, who will approve the application. During verification of refund application, exemption issued for the refund or not. P03: Notify Application for Rejection If the application for a refund is rejected, the applicant must be notified by email, including the reason for rejection. P04: Reject for Amendment If the application submitted is incomplete or the applicant need further amendment, the same will be reverted to the applicant for amendment by email. P05: Send Confirmation The applicant must be notified by email that their application has been approved P06: Send to Revenue System Once the refund application has been approved by the custom, it will be redirected to the revenue system which will return the generated demand notice for the refund to the eCMS. P07: Process Refund When processing the application, Customs must be able to enter the details of the refund against the original declaration, without changing any of the fields on the original declaration itself. Additional fields must be added, including a remarks field and detailed breakdown of the refund, separating duties, taxes, and penalties. P08: BITS send Refund Status to eCMS Once the refund process has been done BITS will send the refund status to eCMS. P09: Refund Status Update By eCMS When the refund status has been sent by the BITS, the Refund status will be updated by eCMS [TABLE] Status Code | Status Description | Remarks PENDING | Pending | The “Refund Instruction” is pending to be collected. FULL_PAID | Fully Refunded | Refund is made in full. CANCELLED | Refund Cancelled/Rejected | Refund request is cancelled/rejected.

## General electronic Customs management system ## System Admin User Guide ## Version: 1.1 Date: 12.9.2022 ## About CrimsonLogic CrimsonLogic Pte Ltd delivers world-class eGovernment solutions by leveraging on best-practice technologies, quality human capital and global experiences. Our proven track record of end-to-end eGovernment solutions spans across trade facilitation and customs, judiciary, tax, healthcare, and IT security domains. For more information, visit www.crimsonlogic.com ## About Yang Khor Pvt Ltd Yang Khor IT Solutions is a leading In-country Technology Solutions Provider providing solution in terms of hardware, software, support and services as its complete package. Yang Khor IT Solutions has been serving its purpose since 2005, it now has emerged to be unprecedented leader as a Solution Integrator with a differentiated vertical approach providing innovative solutions. Yang Khor IT Solution initially focuses on providing the best solution in terms of hardware and software, to serve the purpose of making life better with the Advance Technology which the world is moving forward with. ## DOCUMENT HISTORY chapter 1 - About this Guide Welcome to the Electronic Customs Management System (eCMS) user guide for System Administrators! This user guide aims to enumerate the process and steps involved in using eCMS. This user guide is divided into different topics and sub-topics. Each topic discusses and shows the steps of the modules that the System Administrators can do in eCMS. ## Purpose and Audience This user guide will help the user to get a quick reference on usage of the system. ## Document Conventions Refer to this section to familiarise yourself with the visual aids used throughout the user guide. ## Navigation To assist you with accessing screens, pages, or windows, refer to the following navigation format: ## Click User Registration>>Users Buttons, fields, and other system elements All system elements are highlighted in Bold text. ## Hyperlinks All topics mentioned in the user guide’s content are hyperlinked. Click on the hyperlink to view the referenced topic. ## Callouts Callouts are presented differently from the original CONTENTS and highlight certain information. There are two types of callouts: tips and warnings. ## Chapter 2 - Getting Started Refer to this chapter to familiarize yourself with the eCMS System; how to log in and log off from the system. ## End-user experience of the self-service process Logging In ## To log in to the eCMS: Type in URL ecms.gov.bt your Internet browser to access the eCMS System. CMS user landing page will display. ## Click on Login and provide the necessary credentials eCMS Login Page Enter the USERNAME and the PASSWORD in the fields provided and Click button. Upon successful login the Electronic Customs Management System Home Page will be displayed. On the login page, the user clicks the Forgot Password? , if the user forget their password. Then they will need to provide the required information and then default password will be send to their mail. ## Dashboard Page Logging Out This function allows the user to log out from the application any time. User can sign out from the TFB System any time by simply clicking the button available at the upper right corner of the user logged-in window. ## Log Out Page Common Icons and Buttons The following are the list of icons and buttons referenced across screens and their functionality. ## Chapter 3-Party Management This functionality allows the eCMS Admin to create and update the party for CMS and Front End users in the eCMS system. ## TPN Master This function allows you to view the list of TPN that has been transfer to eCMS from the RAMIS system when the user register into the RAMIS and also the data will be updated when the operator register themselves into the eCMS and also a party will be allocated to the registered user. TPN is applicable for Clearing Agent and Importer and Exporter during creation of Party. ## To view TPN Master: Login to eCMS application and Click Registration >> TPN Master. The subsequent screen will be displayed. ## Details of TPN Master are as follows: TPN details: ## License Details: Contact Details: ## Permanent Address: Present Address: ## Bank Details: Creating Party This section allows the Company Admin to create the party for CMS and FRONT END users in the eCMS system. ## To create a party: Login to eCMS application as a CMS admin. Click Registration >> Party. The subsequent screen will be displayed. ## Party Detail Page Click add icon to create new party. ## Party Details Tab Enter information in the Party Details fields. Click Save button to save the Party details. Click Ok button to close the confirmation message. Click on Contact Details Tab. The subsequent screen will be displayed. ## Contact Details Tab Enter information in the Contact Details fields. Click Save button to save the Contact details. Click Reset button to reset the data entered if incorect. ## Click Close to close the working page Searching Party This section allows the Company Admin to search, edit, view and print the party for CMS and FRONT-END users in the eCMS. ## To search the party: Click Registration >> Party. The subsequent screen will be displayed. ## Party Search List Page Enter any one of the search criteria to view the party details. Following are the field and button descriptions of the Search User Page. ## Viewing Party Details This functionality allows the Company Admin to view the party details. ## To view the party details: From the search results, click the icon to view the party details. ## Party Details can be saved in different forms PDF, XLS and Save by clicking the icon as shown Click the icon to print preview the party details. ## Print Preview Popup Updating Party Details This section allows the Company Admin to search and edit the party in the eCMS system. ## To update the party: From search result, click the edit icon to update the party details. The following screen will be displayed. ## Party Details Edit Tab Modify the field values and click button. Click Ok button to close the confirmation message. The changes get reflected in the search party grid. ## Chapter 4-Role Management This functionality allows the eCMS Admin to create and update the roles for CMS and FRONT END users in the eCMS. ## Creating Roles This section allows the Company Admin to create roles for CMS and FRONT END users in the eCMS. ## To create a role: Login to eCMS application as a CMS admin. Click Registration >> Role. The subsequent screen will be displayed. ## Role List Page Click Add icon to create new user. The Following screen will be displayed. ## Role Details Tab Enter information in the Role Details fields. Click Save button to save the Role details. Click Ok button to close the confirmation message. Click Reset button to clear the role details fields. Click on Role Privileges Tab. The subsequent screen will be displayed. ## Role Privileges Tab Select the functionality to provide the access rights to the role. Click Save button to save the Role Privileges details. Click Ok button to close the confirmation message. Click Role Filters Tab. The subsequent screen will be displayed. ## Role Filter Tab Click Save button to save the role filters details. ## Searching Roles This section allows the Company Admin to search, edit, view and print the roles for CMS and FRONT END users in the eCMS. ## To search the role: Click Registration>>Role. The subsequent screen will be displayed. ## Role Search List Page Enter any one of the search criteria to view the role details. Enter the search criteria and click icon to view the matching results in the Search Results Page. ## Role List Search Result Page Viewing Role Details This functionality allows the Company Admin to view the role details. ## To view the role details: From the search results, click the icon to view the role details and then click on view for viewing the details ## Role Detail Tab Click Role Privileges tab to view the Role Privileges assigned. ## Role Privilege Tab Click Role Filter tab to view the Role Filters done. ## Role Filter Tab Click the icon to print preview the role details. ## Print Preview Popup Updating Role Details This section allows the Company Admin to search and edit the roles in the TFB system. ## To update the roles: From search result, click the edit icon to update the role details. The changes get reflected in the search role grid. ## Chapter 5-User Management This functionality allows the TFB CMS Admin to create and update the CMS user, FRONT END user, roles and party as well as defining the roles to the respective users. ## Creating CMS User The Company Administrator creates the CMS users using the TFB Application. ## To create a CMS user: Login to eCMS application and click CMS Users. ## CMS User List Page Click icon to create a new CMS user. ## CMS User Personal Details Tab Enter information in the Personal Details fields. Click Save button to save the user details. Click Close button to close the confirmation message. Click Reset button to clear the user personal details. Click User Details Tab. The subsequent screen will be displayed. ## User Details Tab Enter information in the User Details fields. Click Save button to save the user details. Click Ok button to close the confirmation message. Click Reset button to clear the user details tab fields. Click Role Details Tab. The subsequent screen will be displayed. ## Role Details Tab The Company Admin can assign new roles. Click Add icon to assign new TPR role to that particular user. ## Add User Details Popup Select the type of role to be assigned to the user and click save button. Click Ok button to close the confirmation message. Click Reset button to clear the TPR role field. The Company Admin can reset password for the user. Click Reset Password to reset password for a particular user. ## Searching CMS Users This section allows the Company Admin to search, edit, view and print the users in the TFB system. ## To search the user: Click Registration>> CMS User. The subsequent screen will be displayed. ## CMS User List Search Page Enter any one of the search criteria to view the user details. Following are the field and button descriptions of the Search User Tab. Enter the search criteria and Click icon to view the matching results in the Search Results Page. ## CMS User List Search Result Page Viewing CMS User Details This functionality allows the Company Admin to view the user details. ## To view the CMS user details: From the search results, click the icon to view the personal details. ## Personal Details Tab Click User Details tab to view the user details. ## CMS User Details Tab Click Role tab to view and edit the roles. ## CMS User Role Details Tab Click the Reset password to reset password ## View User Role Details Popup Click the icon to print preview the role details. ## Print Preview Details Popup Updating CMS User Details This section allows the Company Admin to search and edit the users in the TFB system. ## To search the user: Click Registration >> CMS User. The subsequent screen will be displayed. ## CMS User List Search Page Click on the user you want to update the details and then update the detail and click onto menu the successful message will be popped up for the same ## User Details Edit Tab Creating RRCO User The Company Administrator can create the Front End users using the eCMS Application. ## To create a Front End user: Login to TFB application and Click Registration >> FRONT END User. The subsequent screen will be displayed. ## System Code Page Select Code Type ‘Active Type’ from the drop-down list. And click to add in the Active type and Save to save the added details: Enter information in the Agent Details fields. Click Close button in success message box to continue. Click Reset button to clear the details. For Update click on the list you want to update and then add the details and Click on Update. ## Agency Type The System Administrator creates and updates the Agency Type ## To create an Agency Type: Click Code Maintenance >> Agency Type. The subsequent screen will be displayed. Select Code Type ‘Active Type’ from the drop-down list. And click to add in the Active type and Save to save the added details: Enter information in the Agent Details fields. Click Close button in success message box to continue. The rule files should be deployed to following folder, “<TFB installed folder>crimsonlogic/trade/tfb2/rel1_0/drools/dtable/”. All rule files should be deployed to the folder listed. Rule files are in xls format and the first tab/sheet in the excel. After deploying the file, the drl files should be deleted/erased from the following folder, “<TFB installed folder>crimsonlogic/trade/tfb2/rel1_0/drools/drl/”. ## General Release No 1.0 – March 2021 ## Endorsement by System Owner (internal) release history ## Table of Contents Table of Contents 3 ## Introduction 4 A. Definitions and Abbreviations 4 ## B. Code Maintenance Overview 14 2.1 Code Maintenance to create, update, view. 14 2.2 Process Flow for Code Maintenance (Generic) 15 2.3 Use Case Diagram for Code maintenance to create/update and view. 18 ## Reset Password Functional Requirements 19 3. RESOURCE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM OVERVIEW 24 5.1 Resource Management 24 5.2 Resource Assignment 26 5.3 Use Cases for Resource Management 30 ## Appendix A 32 1. Configuration blueprint (CBP) 32 ## Introduction This document defines & illustrates the business requirements, process flows as well as the detailed functional requirements of CMS System Administration module to be implemented for Department of Revenue and Customs Bhutan. ## Definitions and Abbreviations The table below lists the different acronyms and abbreviations as well as the definitions used throughout this SRS. ## References The creation of the CMS SRS was referenced using the following documents: ## FUNCATIONAL REQUIREMENT SPECIFICATION.docx TECHNICAL REQUIREMENT SPECIFICATION.docx ## Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-3.pdf Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-4.pdf ## Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-5A.pdf Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-5B.pdf ## Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-6A.pdf Bhutan eCMS Technical Proposal TECH-6B.pdf ## Audit Trail Functional Requirements Audit Trail Overview The Audit Trail module is used to audit various functionalities in CMS modules by storing the details in audit tables. The Audit Trail module contains mainly two functions. The first one is called Data Collector and the other one is called Data Viewer. All modules in CMS will have audit logging. The Audit Trail module is used by the system administrator (Customs) for system auditing and transaction auditing. Detailed audit tracking of each transaction can be done using the Audit Trail module. The Audit Trail module is a centralized module, and it tracks CMS audit. It is comprised of a front end for administrators to query and view a transaction audit log. At the backend all submitted transactions are audit trailed. System events like login/log out etc. will also be audited. The IP of the logged in user will also be tracked in the audit logs. ## Audit Trail Data Collector The Audit Trail Data Collector collects audit data from individual modules. Its function is to receive audit trail data from applications and then store the data in the database. ## Audit Type Audit type defined for the data collector determines if the audit is a transaction audit or a system error or system event. The following audit types are defined: Error – Errors & exceptions generated in the system. Log – This is general audit information. System – System events like system/instance restarts, instance shut down etc. ## Viewing Audit Trail A UI shall be provided for the system admin to view the audit logs. The UI will include filter options & search options to look for audit trail based on: ## Time period of audit Module ## User Id Audit type The search page will have a view option to view the audit record. The user will be able to see the data as a name value pair. For e.g. Declaration data will be shown as below: ## Declaration Number: DECL1000101 Declaration Type: Import ## CPC Group: Import from Home Destination Country: SG ## Audit Requirement Below is the table showing the information captured for each transaction. The business transaction reference number is the key for all transaction. ## Use Case Diagram for Audit Data Collector and Audit Viewing Code Maintenance Functional Requirements ## Code Maintenance Overview Code Maintenance is used to maintain the codes used in eCMS for a set of predefined code type. Code Maintenance allows for customs officer to create/update, view the code. The code type will be preloaded from the code master. After which, the customs officers can make the necessary updates. The code entered must be unique for that code type. ## Code Maintenance to create, update, view. Code Maintenance allow for the users to view, add, update. To add a new code, select the green, ‘+’ from the top right and user will be presented with a page (below). All the user requires to enter the code and description. The code entered must be unique for that code type. Example, Incoterm code type cannot have duplicate ‘EXW’ code. Validation is done during save process. ## Process Flow for Code Maintenance (Generic) Below is the table showing the description of each code type. ## Use Case Diagram for Code maintenance to create/update and view. Reset Password Functional Requirements ## Reset Password Overview User can reset password in Registration module. Password automatically generated by system and notification will send to registered user email. ## Process Flow for Reset Password (Generic) Use case for Reset Password. ## Notice and Update Functional Requirements Notice and Update Overview Admin will create or Update Notice/News under System Admin Module, Once Created/Updated Notice/News will publish on eCMS portal, Users can view the published notice details. ## Process Flow for Notice and Update (Generic) Use case for Notice and Update. ## Resource Management FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS RESOURCE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM OVERVIEW CMS use the resource management to assign officers to perform certain business functions like document verification, inspection on a specific declaration etc. The assignment is linked to a specific business transaction. The manager/supervisor of the customs office will configure resource management and can manually assign officers to task. ## Resource Management The setup for customs Admin and supervisor includes the following: ## Calendar year configuration Work shift assignment ## Setup vacation period of custom officers Task Configuration ## Pending tasks Calendar Year Configuration ## In the calendar year configuration, there are 4 tabs which requires setup: Calendar Setup for calendar year. ## Work week Setup of office hours for each day of the week. ## Work Shifts Working shifts Each custom officer is assigned a work shift when on duty. ## Holidays Setup for eCMS to recognize public holidays ## Work Shift Assignment This setup the custom officer’s “work shift” and the start and end date of the work shift assignment. ## Here are the fields needs to be setup: User ID – custom office user id. This is the ID which has been setup in the Registration-CMS User. From Date and To Date – the start and end of the configured work shift. Shift Name – This is the shift defined during the setup of the calendar. Active – it is valid. ## Setup of vacation period of custom officers All custom office needs to setup the vacation period so eCMS assignment engine will know whether an officer is present and can be assignment with new tasks. ## Here are the fields needs to be setup: User ID – custom office user id. From Date and to date - Start and end date of vacation. Remark - description. Active – value for eCMS assignment engine to know whether custom office is on vacation. ## Task Configuration This is the setup of the task and the roles of the assigned modules. ## Here are the fields needs to be setup: Task code – task code, unique. ## Task Name – Description of the task Module – Module for this task. Role – eCMS will only display the roles which is tied to the module. The role of the custom officers assigned to this task. This is tied to the CMS user’s role. Party – once set, it is only for the defined organization i.e. Customs. Customs office – once set, it is valid for the defined custom office. ## Algorithm Round Robin – each office is assigned a task assigned fairly. ## Due dates (from creation date) Days – number of days for the task to be completed once assigned. Type of Days – Working days/Calendar days. Calendar days mean weekend included while working days is tied to the work week as setup. ## Pending Tasks. This is used for reassignment of task to another officer. Supervising officer will use the function to assign task to another officer. ## Resource Assignment There are 2 ways for resources to be assigned to a task manual and automatically. ## Assignment Engine The automatic task assignment engine will be running on a periodic time to assign newly arrived task to the available officers. The engine will follow routing as per flow diagram below. ## Process Steps Design Considerations ## Manual Assignment Manual assignment will be available for the supervising custom officer to assign task which is not completed within the schedule or when a task is not assigned to any officer. Supervising officer uses the pending task menu found in Resource Management to assign task to specific custom officer. ## Overdue task engine There will be an engine which runs daily searching for open task that has past due dates. When a past due task is found, an email notification is sent to the supervisor informing about the pending task. The supervisor can take action by either reassigning to another custom officer or let is remain as it. ## Process Steps Business Rules Refer the “System Admin CBP” excel template for business rules and user group access/role matrix. ## Use Cases for Resource Management Admin Setup and Supervisor Use Case ## Manual Task Assignment Use Case Engine Assignment Use Case ## Appendix A Configuration title: System Design Specification APPLICATION V2.0
content:
[TRADER] System Design Specification APPLICATION V2.0

## General Release No 2.0– Apr,2022 ## Prepared By Reviewed by ## Approved By Authorized for Release ## Contents 1. INTRODUCTION 4 1.1 Scope 4 1.2 Definitions and abbreviations 4 1.3 References 5 1.4 Product Perspective 5 2. Design viewpoints 5 2.1 Interface viewpoint 5 2.1.1 Authorized Complaint Trader 5 2.1.2 Exemption 7 2.1.3 Duty Free Quota 9 2.1.4 CFA Authorization 12 3. Dependency Viewpoint 15 4. ER Diagram 17 4.1 (Exemption ER Diagram) 17 4.2 Authorized Compliance Trader (ACT) Er diagram 18 4.3 Duty Free Quota er diagram 19 4.4 CFA Authorization ER diagram 20 ## INTRODUCTION The eCMS, as its name implies, will be a system for the DRC’s Customs & Excise Division, hereafter referred to as “Customs”, that will provide best-in-class services to the Bhutan‘s business community, in support of the Bhutan‘s aspirations to modernize core customs administration functions as part of customs modernization requirements and in line with the international conventions and national regulations such as The Customs Act of Bhutan 2017 and Customs Rules and Regulations of Bhutan 2017. Implementation of the electronic customs management system will further help to propel Bhutan’s rankings by making it easier and clearer for traders and businesses to have access to information and enable them to submit regulatory compliance forms/documents digitally. This document is intended to act as the SDD (Software Design Document) for the Application module. ## Scope This document defines & illustrates the business requirements, process flows as well as the detailed functional requirements of eCMS Application module (Authorized Compliant Trader and Exemption) to be implemented for Department of Revenue and Customs, Bhutan. ## Definitions and abbreviations References Signed off SRS_eCMS_Application_Exemption_V1.0_Finalized. ## Product Perspective Design viewpoints ## Interface viewpoint The Interface design focuses on the screen designs for various services provided by the Application module. ## Authorized Complaint Trader Submit Application: A user will prepare an application for ACT after logging into eCMS. Trader when submits the application, will have a unique reference number generated. The application will be received by DRC for further verification and Approval/ Rejection by the DRC: Verify Application: Level 1. The verifier based on the review will either recommend, reject, or reject for amendment. During verification, if the verifier concludes that the application is invalid for any reason, then the Verifier will provide reasons for rejection and reject the application. The applicant shall be notified of the rejection including the reason for rejection by email. ## Assessor: Level 2 If the application has been recommended for ACT by the verifier, System will assign the application to the work queue of an Assessor at the Customs head office. If the assessor determines that the application needs to be rejected for any reason, then the assessor will reject the application and provide reasons for rejection. eCMS will notify the applicant of the rejection. During assessment, if the Assessor concludes that the provided documents and related details are in order, then the Assessor can approve the application for ACT certification. In this case, System will certify the applicant as an ACT in eCMS. ## Applicable fees are configured in the System, If no fees are applicable, system will allow printing of certificate of registration. ## If fees are applicable, a payment advice shall be generated and sent to Revenue SYSTEM Revenue system will send a payment confirmation to eCMS after collecting payment in Revenue system. After receipt of collection message, eCMS will enable printing of “Authorized Compliant Registration certificate” and ACT certification will be restored. ## Exemption Exemptions can be applied for specific items and for a specific reason (for example, for setting up a Manufacturing unit etc). ## An FE user can apply for exemption in eCMS after logging into eCMS An FE user will login to eCMS and prepare an application for Import Exemption. In case of a CFA applying exemption on behalf of the importer, User shall provide the TPN number of the Importer/exporter. User will provide required mandatory information for getting an exemption and submit. A unique number shall be generated for the track of application. Upon submission, System will generate an application number. ## Screenshot for Exemption Creation Verification: Level 1 When the exemption application has been submitted, System will route the application for review to the work queue of the Verifier (Custom) The verifier based on the review will either recommend, reject, or reject for amendment. The status of the application shall reflect the action taken by the verifier. During verification, if the verifier concludes that the application is invalid for any reason, then the Verifier will provide reasons for rejection and reject the application. The applicant shall be notified of the rejection including the reason for rejection by email. Amendment: if the documents submitted are incomplete or the application needs further amendment, the same will be reverted to the applicant for amendment ## Screenshot for Level 1 Exemption Approval (by Verifier) Level 2 Approval If the exemption has been verified and recommended by the verifier, System will route the application for review to the work queue of an Assessor at the Customs Head Office. Assessor will check recommended application detail and determine if it can be approved. If the assessor determines that the application needs to be rejected for any reason, then the assessor will reject the application and provide reasons for rejection. eCMS will notify the applicant of the rejection by email. The application can be reverted to the verifier for further review too by the assessor. If the application is approved, the applicant must be issued an Import Duty Exemption Certificate (IDEC), which must be allocated a unique system generated reference number and will be valid for one (1) year. System will notify the applicant on the approval of the Exemption request. System will allow applicant to print the exemption from the system. ## Screenshot for Level 2 Exemption Approval (by Assessor) Duty Free Quota An external user can apply for Duty-Free Quota in eCMS. The application will be made available in the public portal and will not require the user to login to eCMS. ## For applicant: The system shall allow the applicant to key in CID. If the applicant keys in the CID, the same should hit the eCMS PIN Master, and list all the TPN registered against the CID. For the selected TPN, System will fetch the related TPN details and display in the application. For duty free quota, only individual shall be allowed (No Business or Company TPN) ## Screenshot for Duty Free Membership Application Verify Application When the duty-free quota application has been submitted, System will route the application for review to the work queue of a Verifier at the Head Office. During verification, if the verifier concludes that the application is invalid for any reason, then the Verifier will provide reasons for rejection and reject the application. The applicant shall be notified of the rejection including the reason for rejection by email. Amendment: if the documents submitted are incomplete or the applicant need further amendment, the same will be reverted to the applicant for amendment by email. ## Screenshot for Verification of DutyFree Membership Application (by Verifier) Approve Duty Free Application If the Duty-Free Quota has been verified and recommended by the verifier, System will route the application to the work queue of an Assessor at the Customs Head Office. Assessor will check recommended application detail and determine if it can be approved. If the assessor determines that the application needs to be rejected for any reason, then the assessor will reject the application and provide reasons for rejection. eCMS will notify the applicant of the rejection. If the application is approved, System will generate an approval letter with a unique system generated Quota number which shall be valid till 31st Dec of the approval year based on date of approval. System will notify the applicant on the approval of the Duty-Free Quota request and include the Quota details as well. ## Screenshot for Duty Free Application Approval (by Assessor) CFA Authorization A Trader will need to authorize a CFA to act on its behalf and transact in eCMS as its representative. For this, the Trader will need to apply from the Portal (outside Login) and indicate the CFA to be authorized. Upon submission, the application shall be reviewed and approved by a Verifier at the Customs Head office. Post approval from Customs, the CFA can act on behalf of the Trader and submit declarations and other trade related documents in the System. Application. The system will allow the applicant to key in CID as well as TPN. The system will validate the keyed in CID and the TPN and accordingly allow the applicant to process further. In case of a business, the system will allow to key in the business license no and the TPN. If the TPN belongs to a Company, then the Applicant will be required to provide the Company registration number for authentication, the system will validate the keyed in TPN and the company registration number and accordingly allow the applicant to proceed to fetch the TPN details and display in the Application. If the keyed in details is validated then System will fetch the related TPN details and display in the application (in case the TPN belongs to a Company, then system will follow authentication using Company registration number as mentioned in Step 2 before displaying TPN details). After providing a valid TPN, Trader shall indicate the CFA which needs to be authorized from a list of registered and active CFA’s in eCMS and proceed to submit the application for authorizing the selected CFA. Only one CFA per application can be indicated. The system will also allow the applicant to select the start date and end date. (validity of the authorization) ## Application can be for: CFA Authorization ## Verification Level 1 System will assign the application to the work queue of a Verifier at the Customs head office The verifier will verify the applicant details and determine the validity of the application. The verifier based on the review will either approve or reject the application. During verification, if the verifier concludes that the application is invalid for any reason, then the Verifier will provide reasons for rejection and reject the application. The applicant shall be notified of the rejection including the reason for rejection by email. ## Screenshot CFA approver from Cust end Approve Authorization During verification, if the Verifier concludes that the provided details are in order, then the Verifier can approve the Authorization. In this case, System will authorize the CFA to act on behalf of the Trader. After approval, System will send a notification to the Trader and the CFA. ## CFA De-authorization Dependency Viewpoint The Dependency Viewpoint refers to the interconnection of classes that have a common goal. The Application Module uses quite a few classes that shares information and parameters among themselves. This Application Service class also gets its configuration information from a different config file and uses service helpers class for doing the business logic processing and Application DAO class from ORM package for achieving db-centric activities. The service helpers class provides business and data access logic with distributed transaction supports. The Application DAO class performs the assigned responsibilities depending on dao helpers class and reads a third config file to do so. The dao helpers class accesses the data from the database using a data source. The data source depends on the database driver (mysql-connector.jar), which is supplied externally. The data available in the data package is associated with type and values. ## General Release No 2.0– Apr,2022 ## Prepared By Reviewed by ## Approved By Authorized for Release ## Contents 1. INTRODUCTION 4 1.1 Scope 4 1.2 Definitions and abbreviations 4 1.3 References 5 1.4 Product Perspective 5 2. Design viewpoints 6 2.1 Interface viewpoint 6 2.2 Dependency Viewpoint 8 2.3 System Database Schema 9 2.4 Field Details 9 ## INTRODUCTION The eCMS, as its name implies, will be a system for the DRC’s Customs & Excise Division, hereafter referred to as “Customs”, that will provide best-in-class services to the Bhutan‘s business community, in support of the Bhutan‘s aspirations to modernize core customs administration functions as part of customs modernization requirements and in line with the international conventions and national regulations such as The Customs Act of Bhutan 2017 and Customs Rules and Regulations of Bhutan 2017. Implementation of the electronic customs management system will further help to propel Bhutan’s rankings by making it easier and clearer for traders and businesses to have access to information and enable them to submit regulatory compliance forms/documents digitally. This document is intended to act as the SDD (Software Design Document) for the Application module. ## Scope This document defines & illustrates the business requirements, process flows as well as the detailed functional requirements of eCMS Application module (Authorized Compliant Trader and Exemption) to be implemented for Department of Revenue and Customs, Bhutan. ## Definitions and abbreviations References ## Signed off SRS_eCMS_Registration_V1.0 Product Perspective ## Design viewpoints Interface viewpoint The Interface design focuses on the screen designs for various services provided by the Declaration module. Based on the CPC Group certain sub-processes are optional, and some are mandatory. The generic process will consist of the sub-process as given: ## Approval Payment ## Valuation Centralized Risk ## Inspection Additional payment (if any) ## Release Import Declaration Submission ## Create Declaration for import: Screenshot for Declaration type: Direct entry for Home Use ## Screenshot for Bill of Lading Screenshot for Invoice details ## Screenshot for item details Screenshot for duty ## Screenshot to upload supporting document Screenshot for Import duty submission Import Declaration Approval is done at the Cust end, where in the assigned officer will do the due diligent and approve the declaration: ## Screenshot general information Screenshot for Bill of Lading ## Screenshot for invoice and consigner Screenshot for supporting document ## Screenshot for summary Screenshot for approval of Import Declaration ## Payment The system will allow payment for the declaration accepted by customs. Upon completion of payment process the system will automatically forward the declaration to the next process If the declaration is not subjected for payment, the system will automatically forward the declaration to the next process. the system will also route the additional payment for a declaration to payment process. the additional payment will be linked to a particular declaration. ## Screenshot for Details Screenshot for Payment approval Screenshot for Receipt downloaded. ## Valuation The system will determine the customs value at item level and accordingly determine whether the declared value is under or over value. The system based on the order of execution (please refer the SRS Valuation) will reflect the system value for items that are either under or overvalued. The system will allow the customs officer to decide on valuation based on the finding presented by the system and amend the declared value accordingly. The system will give an option to the valuation officer to direct the declaration to yellow or red channel. ## Screenshot for Valuation Result Centralized Risk Assessment ## The system will perform the risk assessment based on the risk profile in the system The lane will be decided based on profile criteria met. The possible outcomes are “Green”, “Blue”, “Yellow” or “Red” lanes. “Green” lane will go for release process. “Blue” lane will go for Post clearance audit after release. “Yellow” will go for document verification. “Red” will go for physical inspection. ## Screenshot for Risk Assessment Examination ## Yellow Channel If the declaration is directed to yellow lane, the declaration will be reflected in the document verifier’s dashboard the system will also provide a platform to the document verifier officer to submit the examination report. The document verification officer may review the documents and decide to release or route for physical inspection or for re-assessment ## The system will then follow the additional payment process Red Lane If the declaration is directed to red lane, the declaration will be reflected in the inspection’s dashboard Upon physical inspection carried out by the inspection team, the system will also provide a platform to the inspection officer to submit the inspection report that is standard and incorporated in the system. Based on the inspection REPORT, the assessor will either. release the good send back to the declarant for amendment. Direct the declaration to the offences and penalties: Declaration intercepted with customs offence after examination can be routed to Offence and Penalties process by Inspection Officer ## Blue Lane The system will automatically direct the declaration submitted by ACT to blue lane The system will also provide a feature for the customs to direct a particular declaration to the blue lane. ## Green Lane The declaration directed to green lane will be released by the customs. Note: The system will provide an option for customs to upgrade the declaration as follows. ## Green Lane to either yellow or red channel Yellow lane to red channel ## Screenshot for Check non-containerized cargo Screenshot for Document check ## Screenshot for Document check complete Physical Examination: Physical examination is created in the system and then the examination happened offline , then once done the inspection offer will update the report and close the examination , the declaration then proceeds further in the flow. ## Screenshot for Physical Examination Screenshot for Physical examination Report ## Release Cargo Upon completion of the customs procedures the system will generate a release order. The system will allow both the declarant and the customs office to print the release order if need be. During gate out the gate officer will be presented with the release order. Based on which the gate officer will release the cargo and the same will be recorded in the system. ## The system will record the release time Screenshot for Release Cargo Order ## Screenshot for Release Cargo details (non-containerized) Updates Screenshot for Release Cargo Screenshot for declaration processing for different regimes and CPC. Based on the CPC Group certain sub-processes are optional, and some are mandatory. For e.g., for temporary import or export, an approved TIER application will be required. ## Screenshot for Declaration type: Entry for Home use after Temporary Admission Screenshot for Declaration Type: Entry for Home use ex-warehouse after ware housing Procedure ## Screenshot for Declaration type: Import for Home use after transit Screenshot for Declaration type: Import for home use after international transit ## Screenshot for Declaration Type: Simplified Declaration Screenshot for duty free store entry for home use ## Screenshot for Declaration type: Duty free store for home use without custom duty Screenshot for Declaration type: Post parcel Declaration ## Screenshot for Declaration type: import after temporary export for additional items Screenshot for Declaration type: Entry for home use after export of faulty goods. ## Export: Screenshot for Export for Declaration Type: Direct/Permanent Export ## Screenshot for Export: Bill of Lading Screenshot for Invoice and Consigner ## Screenshot for Uploading Supporting Document Screenshot for Export Summary ## Approval for Export Declaration Declaration Approval ## If no payment due move on to Valuation Export Valuation: ## Screenshot for Export Valuation The valuation officer approves and updates the Valuation result Screenshot for Valuation Result. ## Assessment Screenshot for risk assessment ## Gate in After the risk assessment it is forwarded to gate in pass. Post Gate in pass update Cargo details as below: ## Screenshot to update Containerized Cargo Screenshot to update Non-containerize details ## Screenshot for Gate in Pass approval Dependency Viewpoint The Application module uses quite a few classes that share information and parameter among themselves to achieve the required functionalities. If the customs officer rejected the request for amendments, the request will be routed back to the user for update and re-submission. If the customs officer approved the request, the request will have an Approved status. ## Additional Air Cargo Manifest The user creates an additional air manifest starting with the request header. The user selects a manifest created by the user’s party and with an Approved status. ## Screenshot for additional air manifest Create Airwaybills The user can create air waybill/s only after the header data has been saved. The user can create as many AWBs in the system. ## OR Upload Airwaybills. The user can also create an additional air manifest by uploading a file in eCMS After the system uploads the manifest file, the system will create and save the corresponding additional air manifest header & AWBs with a Draft status. A unique Provisional Additional Manifest Number will also be generated and saved along with the additional air manifest. ## Submit Additional Air Cargo Manifest The user submits the additional air manifest after creating the necessary AWBs. ## Approve Additional Air Cargo Manifest The manifest is routed to a customs officer for approval. The Applicant is notified via email after the updating the status (Whether approved/Rejected/Resubmission) ## Screenshot Additional Air manifest approval Request for Temporary Storage The user can choose to move the consignment to temporary storage by submitting a Temporary Storage Request. The temporary storage officer who receives the request will facilitate the actual movement of the consignment to the temporary storage. ## Screenshot for Temporary Storage Request Passenger Manifest ## Create Passenger Manifest Header: eCMS will enable the user to submit passenger manifests through manual input or upload. ## The user can also create a passenger manifest by uploading it as a file : Screenshot to Create Passenger Manifest ## Create OR Upload Passenger Manifest File The user can create the passenger record only after the header data has been saved.
