title: System Design Specification System Administration
content:
[CUSTOMS] System Design Specification System Administration

## General Release No 1.0– Mar,2022 ## Document History Prepared By ## Reviewed by Approved By ## Authorized for Release Contents 1. INTRODUCTION 4 1.1 Scope 4 1.2 Definitions and abbreviations 4 1.3 References 5 1.4 Product Perspective 5 2. Design Considerations 6 3. Architectural Strategies 9 4. System Architecture 10 5. Design viewpoints 11 5.1 Audit trail overview 11 5.2 Audit Trail Data Collector 11 5.3 Audit Type 11 5.4 Viewing Audit Trail 11 5.5 interface Viewpoints 12 6 Code Maintenance overview 12 6.1 Code maintenance to create, update, view 12 7 Reset Password overview 13 8 Notice and update overview 14 9 Resource Management System overview 14 10 Calendar configuration 15 11 Work shift Assignment 15 12 setup of vacation period of custom officers 16 13 Task Configuration 17 14 Pending 17 15 Dependency viewpoint 19 16 system database schema 20 17 field details 20 ## INTRODUCTION The eCMS, as its name implies, will be a system for the DRC’s Customs & Excise Division, hereafter referred to as “Customs”, that will provide best-in-class services to the Bhutan‘s business community, in support of the Bhutan‘s aspirations to modernize core customs administration functions as part of customs modernization requirements and in line with the international conventions and national regulations such as The Customs Act of Bhutan 2017 and Customs Rules and Regulations of Bhutan 2017. Implementation of the electronic customs management system will further help to propel Bhutan’s rankings by making it easier and clearer for traders and businesses to have access to information and enable them to submit regulatory compliance forms/documents digitally. This document is intended to act as the SDD (Software Design Document) for the System Administration. This document defines & illustrates the business requirements, how system can work as well as the detailed functional requirements of eCMS System Administration module to be implemented for Department of Revenue and Customs Bhutan ## Scope Registration of a party and user is one of the core functions of eCMS. This module takes care of the following activities: • Registration of a Party • Registration of a User ## Definitions and abbreviations References ## Signed off SRS_eCMS_Registration_V1.0 Product Perspective ## Design Considerations Below is the summary of the aspects which were considered during design. Compatibility - The system can operate with other products that are designed for interoperability. Standard WCO data model and recommended WCO Customs processes are followed for the System to integrate and communicate with other similar Customs system. Extensibility - New capabilities can be added to the software without major changes to the underlying architecture and this is achieved by identifying and making components highly configurable wherever possible and, also, the framework supports some degree of on-the-fly Customization to extend functionality with minimum effort. Modularity - The resulting software comprises well defined, independent components which leads to better maintainability. The components could be then implemented and tested in isolation before being integrated to form a desired software system. This allows division of work in a software development project. Fault-tolerance - The software is resistant to and able to recover from component failure. Well defined error messages for various anticipated behavior are catered and provided for. Maintainability – This is a measure of how easily bug fixes or functional modifications can be accomplished. High maintainability can be the product of modularity and extensibility. Reliability (Software durability) - The software can perform a required function under stated conditions for a specified period. Reusability - The ability to use some or all the aspects of the preexisting software with little to no modification. Robustness - The software can operate under stress or tolerate unpredictable or invalid input. Security - The software can withstand and resist hostile acts and influences. Usability - The software user interface must be usable for its target user/audience. Default values for the parameters must be chosen so that they are a good choice for most of the users. Performance - The software performs its tasks within a timeframe that is acceptable for the user. Portability - The software should be usable across several different conditions and environments. Scalability - The software adapts well to increasing data or added features or number of users. ## Resource Managements The setup for customs Admin and supervisor includes the following: ## Calendar year configuration Work shift assignment ## Setup vacation period of custom officers Task Configuration ## Pending tasks Calendar year Configuration ## In the calendar year configuration, there are 4 tabs which requires setup: Calendar Setup for calendar year. ## Work week Setup of office hours for each day of the week. ## Work Shifts Working shifts Each custom officer is assigned a work shift when on duty. ## Holidays Setup for eCMS to recognize public holidays ## Work Shift Assignment This setup the custom officer’s “work shift” and the start and end date of the work shift assignment. ## Here are the field needs to be setup: User ID – custom office user id. This is the ID which has been setup in the Registration-CMS User. From Date and To Date – the start and end of the configured work shift. Shift Name – This is the shift defined during the setup of the calendar. Active – it is valid. ## Task Configuration This is the setup of the task and the roles of the assigned modules. ## Here are the field needs to be setup: Task code – task code, unique. ## Task Name – Description of the task Module – Module for this task. Role – eCMS will only display the roles which is tied to the module. The role of the custom officers assigned to this task. This is tied to the CMS user’s role. Party – once set, it is only for the defined organization i.e. Customs. Customs office – once set, it is valid for the defined custom office. ## Algorithm Round Robin – each office is assigned a task assigned fairly. ## Due dates (from creation date) Days – number of days for the task to be completed once assigned. Type of Days – Working days/Calendar days. Calendar days mean weekend included while working days is tied to the work week as setup. ## Pending Tasks This is used for reassignment of task to another officer. Supervising officer will use the function to assign task to another officer. ## Resource Assignment There are 2 ways for resources to be assigned to a task manual and automatically ## Architectural Strategies Microservices architecture pattern is seen as a viable alternative to monolithic applications and service-oriented architectures. The components are deployed as separate units through an effective, streamlined delivery pipeline. The pattern’s benefits are enhanced scalability and a high degree of decoupling within the application. Owing to its decoupled and independent characteristics, the same components can be separately developed, deployed, and tested without interdependency on any other service component. ## The benefit of decomposing an application into different smaller services are numerous: Modularity: This makes the application easier to understand, develop, test, and become more resilient to architecture erosion. Scalability: Since microservices are implemented and deployed independently of each other, i.e., they run within independent processes, they can be monitored and scaled independently. Distributed development: it parallelizes development by enabling small autonomous teams to develop, deploy and scale their respective services independently. It also allows the architecture of an individual service to emerge through continuous refactoring. Microservice-based architectures facilitate continuous integration, continuous delivery and deployment ## System Architecture Microservices Architecture ## Design viewpoints Audit trail overview The Audit Trail module is used to audit various functionalities in CMS modules by storing the details in audit tables. The Audit Trail module contains mainly two functions. The first one is called Data Collector and the other one is called Data Viewer. All modules in CMS will have audit logging. The Audit Trail module is used by the system administrator (Customs) for system auditing and transaction auditing. Detailed audit tracking of each transaction can be done using the Audit Trail module. The Audit Trail module is a centralized module, and it tracks CMS audit. It is comprised of a front end for administrators to query and view a transaction audit log. At the backend all submitted transactions are audit trailed. System events like login/log out etc. will also be audited. The IP of the logged in user will also be tracked in the audit logs. ## Audit Trail Data Collector The Audit Trail Data Collector collects audit data from individual modules. Its function is to receive audit trail data from applications and then store the data in the database. ## Audit Type Audit type defined for the data collector determines if the audit is a transaction audit or a system error or system event. The following audit types are defined: Error – Errors & exceptions generated in the system. Log – This is general audit information. System – System events like system/instance restarts, instance shut down etc. ## Viewing Audit Trail A UI shall be provided for the system admin to view the audit logs. The UI will include filter options & search options to look for audit trail based on: ## Time period of audit Module ## User Id Audit type The search page will have a view option to view the audit record. The user will be able to see the data as a name value pair. For e.g. Declaration data will be shown as below: ## Declaration Number: DECL1000101 Declaration Type: Import ## CPC Group: Import from Home Destination Country: SG ## interface Viewpoints The Interface design focuses on the screen designs for various services provided by the system administration module. The screen to apply for system administration for Department of Revenue and Customs Bhutan is provided below. ## Figure 1.0 Screenshot for system Admin Audit Trail ## Code Maintenance overview Code Maintenance is used to maintain the codes used in eCMS for a set of predefined code type. Code Maintenance allows for customs officer to create/update, view the code. The code type will be preloaded from the code master. After which, the customs officers can make the necessary updates. The code entered must be unique for that code type. ## Code maintenance to create, update, view Code Maintenance allow for the users to view, add, update. To add a new code, select the green, ‘+’ from the top right and user will be presented with a page (below). All the user requires to enter the code and description. The code entered must be unique for that code type. Example, Incoterm code type cannot have duplicate ‘EXW’ code. Validation is done during save process. The Interface design focuses on the screen designs for various services provided by the system administration module. The screen to apply for code maintenance for system administration for Department of Revenue and Customs Bhutan is provided below. ## Figure 2.0 Screenshot for system Admin for Code maintenance ## Reset Password overview User can reset password in Registration module. Password automatically generated by system and notification will send to registered user email. The screen to apply for Reset password for system administration for Department of Revenue and Customs Bhutan is provided below. ## Figure 3.0 Screenshot for system Admin for Reset password ## Notice and update overview Admin will create or Update Notice/News under System Admin Module, Once Created/Updated Notice/News will publish on eCMS portal, Users can view the published notice details. The screen to apply for code maintenance for system administration for Department of Revenue and Customs Bhutan is provided below. ## Figure 4.0 Screenshot for system Admin for Notice and update ## Resource Management System overview CMS use the resource management to assign officers to perform certain business functions like document verification, inspection on a specific declaration etc. The assignment is linked to a specific business transaction. The manager/supervisor of the customs office will configure resource management and can manually assign officers to task. ## The setup for customs Admin and supervisor includes the following: Calendar year configuration ## Work shift assignment Setup vacation period of custom officers ## Task Configuration Pending tasks The screen to apply for code maintenance for system administration for Department of Revenue and Customs Bhutan is provided below. ## Figure 5.0 Screenshot for system Admin for resource management ## Calendar configuration In the calendar year configuration, there are 4 tabs which requires setup: ## Calendar Setup for calendar year. ## Work week Setup of office hours for each day of the week. ## Work Shifts Working shifts Each custom officer is assigned a work shift when on duty. ## Holidays Setup for eCMS to recognize public holidays The screen to apply for code maintenance for system administration for Department of Revenue and Customs Bhutan is provided below. ## Figure 6.0 Screenshot for system Admin for calendar configuration ## Work shift Assignment This setup the custom officer’s “work shift” and the start and end date of the work shift assignment. ## Here are the field needs to be setup: User ID – custom office user id. This is the ID which has been setup in the Registration-CMS User. From Date and To Date – the start and end of the configured work shift. Shift Name – This is the shift defined during the setup of the calendar. Active – it is valid. The screen to apply for work shift Assignment for the System Administration is provided below. ## Figure 7.0 Screenshot for system Admin for work shift Assignment ## setup of vacation period of custom officers All custom office needs to setup the vacation period so eCMS assignment engine will know whether an officer is present and can be assignment with new tasks. ## Here are the field needs to be setup: User ID – custom office user id. From Date and to date - Start and end date of vacation. Remark - description. Active – value for eCMS assignment engine to know whether custom office is on vacation. ## Figure 8.0 Screenshot for system Admin for setup of vacation period customs ## Task Configuration This is the setup of the task and the roles of the assigned modules. ## Here are the field needs to be setup: Task code – task code, unique. ## Task Name – Description of the task Module – Module for this task. Role – eCMS will only display the roles which is tied to the module. The role of the custom officers assigned to this task. This is tied to the CMS user’s role. Party – once set, it is only for the defined organization i.e. Customs. Customs office – once set, it is valid for the defined custom office. ## Algorithm Round Robin – each office is assigned a task assigned fairly. ## Due dates (from creation date) Days – number of days for the task to be completed once assigned. Type of Days – Working days/Calendar days. Calendar days mean weekend included while working days is tied to the work week as setup. The screen to apply for Task Configuration for the System Administration is provided below. ## Figure 9.0 Screenshot for system Admin for setup of Task configuration for customs ## Pending This is used for reassignment of task to another officer. Supervising officer will use the function to assign task to another officer. The screen to apply for Task Configuration for the System Administration is provided below. ## Figure 10.0 Screenshot for system Admin for pending ## Dependency viewpoint The system administration module uses quite a few classes that share information and parameter among themselves to achieve the required functionalities. Field Details 12 ## INTRODUCTION This document defines & illustrates the business requirements, process flows as well as the detailed functional requirements of eCMS Offence, Penalty, Appeal modules to be implemented for Department of Revenue and Customs, Bhutan. Also included are modules for Customs Warehouse for detained/seized/confiscated goods. Enforcement allows customs to manage breach of Customs law, policies, and regulations. It can be triggered at clearance process. Enforcement is also known as Offence Management, and these are used interchangeably. The function explains management of breach of Customs laws and regulations. The function includes notification of offenders, compounding of offences and waiver of interest on penalties. ## Scope The scope of the Offence module is as below: ## Offence Management Penalty ## Appeal Customs Warehouse ## Definitions and abbreviations References ## Signed off SRS_eCMS_Registration_V1.0 Product Perspective ## Design viewpoints Interface viewpoint The Interface design focuses on the screen designs for various services provided by the Registration module. ## The screen to create Offence based on offence source: Create based on Inspection Failure Create based on Information. ## Based on Above Sources divided Into three types: Customs Offence ## Administrative Offences Criminal Offence ## Creating Offence Dependency Viewpoint The Registration module uses quite a few classes that share information and parameter among themselves to achieve the required functionalities. The package diagram of registration module is provided below. ## In the diagram, following dependencies between different packages are shown: web package is dependent on the business package, business packages depend on the data package and ORM package depend on the data package. ## These dependencies are explained below: The Web package of Registration Module contains the Registration Controller class that reads configuration information from a config file and uses the class from the business package to delegate responsibilities. This Registration Service class also gets its configuration information from a different config file and uses service helpers class for doing the business logic processing and Registration DAO class from ORM package for achieving db-centric activities. The service helpers class provides business and data access logic with distributed transaction supports. The Registration DAO class performs the assigned responsibilities depending on dao helpers class and reads a third config file to do so. The dao helpers class accesses the data from the database using a data source. The data source depends on the database driver (mysql-connector.jar), which is supplied externally. The data available in the data package is associated with type and values. All of the dao helpers class from ORM package, the service helpers class from business package and the Registration Controller class from the web package may throw different exception classes at different points of time, which are redirected to the external logging sub-system. This logging sub-system is used for analysing the flow of control of the application. ## System Database Schema (er diagram) ER Diagram ## Field Details [TABLE] System design SPECIFICATION for Offence title: eCMS Bhutan :: Web Portal of Electronic Customs Management System
content: Vision, Mission & Core Values Vision A sustained economic growth with stable macroeconomic environment through dynamic fiscal policy and prudent fiscal discipline. Mission Formulate and implement dynamic fiscal policy and strengthen public financial management (PFM) for effective resource mobilization, efficient allocation, prudent expenditure and debt management with proper accountability of public resources. Core Values INTEGRITY and CARE (I- C.A.R.E) Integrity : We do the right thing. Collaboration : We believe in team work. Accountability : We take ownership and accountability. Respect : We value people and treat them with respect. Excellence : We give our best. Related Navigation About eCMS Vision, Mission & Values Goals & Strategies Organizational Structure Contact Us
